items.stem: In Tableau Next, which unified interface builds up a curated library of data connectors and shows every supported platform alongside its specific connection features and requirements?
items.rationale: The Connector Catalog is the single place in Tableau Next that lists the supported external platforms with their connection features and requirements. Data Source Connectors is the documentation section describing individual connectors, not the interface itself.
items.evidence_quote: Centralize your data management by building a curated library of data connectors within the new Connector Catalog. This unified interface shows all supported platforms alongside their specific connection features and requirements.

items.stem: Data is brought into Data 360 by ingestion rather than federation. What happens to the source fields and their data types as the data lands?
options: They are imported without transformation, so the source schema is preserved
They are renamed and retyped to match the Customer 360 Data Model on arrival
They are all stored as text, and typed later when the object is mapped to a DMO
They are collapsed into a single payload field that is parsed each time it is queried
answer: They are imported without transformation, so the source schema is preserved
items.rationale: Ingestion is deliberately as-is: the data lake object keeps the source fields and their data types. Harmonisation into a standard model happens later, during data modeling, when DLOs are mapped to data model objects.
items.evidence_quote: In data ingestion, data from a data source is brought in as is, meaning that fields and their data types are imported without transformation.

items.stem: A Salesforce org is attached to Data 360 by a standard Salesforce CRM connection. What can Data 360 send back to that org?
options: Only data actions
Harmonized Data 360 data and unified metadata
Unified profiles and calculated insights, once the DMOs are mapped
Segment membership, for any activation target configured in that org
items.rationale: A standard CRM connection is one-directional for data: Data 360 ingests from the org and returns only data actions. Syncing unified metadata or exposing Data 360 data and features inside the connected org requires a Data 360 companion connection instead.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 ingests data and sends back only data actions. This type of connection doesn’t share any data back to the connected org.

items.stem: Many Salesforce connectors ship with a Salesforce-defined data stream definition that already includes the mapping to the DMO structure, so a data stream can be set up quickly. What is that prebuilt definition called?
items.rationale: Salesforce connectors offer starter data bundles: ready-made data stream definitions with the DMO mapping (and often DMO relationships) already in place, which you can also customise. A data kit is a packaging and deployment mechanism, not the connector's prebuilt stream definition.
items.evidence_quote: A starter data bundle is a Salesforce-defined data stream definition that includes mapping to the Data Cloud DMO structure.

items.stem: Tableau Next file-based connectors keep a connection current by running a full refresh on a schedule. What does each refresh cycle do to the data?
options: Replaces the previously downloaded data with the whole new file
Appends the rows that were added to the file since the last cycle
Updates only the individual values that changed since the last cycle
Re-reads the file only when its modified date has changed
answer: Replaces the previously downloaded data with the whole new file
items.rationale: A full refresh downloads and rewrites the entire file every cycle, even if one value changed, which is why very large files are better scheduled weekly or monthly. It is not an incremental or change-detecting update.
items.evidence_quote: A full refresh replaces old data it previously downloaded with a new file. Think of it as erasing a physical whiteboard completely and rewriting the entire lesson from the beginning, even if only one or two words changed.

items.stem: Some source rows can’t be ingested into Data 360 because of data quality issues, such as a null value in the primary key. Data 360 stores those rejected rows in a dedicated data lake object. What is that kind of DLO called?
items.rationale: Rejected rows are logged as problem records and land in a problem record data lake object named after the data stream, so they can be queried rather than being silently lost. They are not written to the target DMO, and there is no separate error log object.
items.evidence_quote: Records that can’t be ingested into Data 360 due to data quality issues are logged as problem records and stored in a problem record data lake object (DLO).

items.stem: A client removes a standard Salesforce CRM connection from Data 360. What happens to the data that Data 360 had already ingested from that org?
options: It is deleted, apart from trust files
It is kept in its data lake objects until someone deletes them
It is kept but marked read-only for a 30-day grace period
It is kept, and only further ingestion from the org stops
answer: It is deleted, apart from trust files
items.rationale: Removing a standard CRM connection both stops ingestion and deletes everything ingested from that org, with trust files the only exception; the ingested contribution also drops out of unified profiles at the next identity resolution run. Nothing is retained for later cleanup.
items.evidence_quote: After you remove a standard Salesforce CRM connection, Data 360 stops ingesting data from the connected org and deletes all the data it ingested from that org, except trust files.

items.stem: Name the Tableau Next data-connection setting, off by default, that you turn on so an external database's data is temporarily cached in Data 360 and queries against it run faster.
items.rationale: Data acceleration is the caching option on an external database connection, turned on by choosing Full Refresh or Incremental Refresh, and it is off when the connection is first added. It is not a separate connector or a data stream refresh mode, and enabling it can affect credit consumption.
items.evidence_quote: Data acceleration improves query performance by temporarily caching data in Data 360.

items.stem: In a Tableau Next workspace you add data through the Beta Salesforce Connections option, choose an org, and select a standard or custom CRM object. What does that route produce from the object?
options: A data lake object holding that object's data
A zero-copy federated view that leaves the records in the CRM org
A semantic model published back into the CRM org
A CSV extract staged in the workspace for later upload
answer: A data lake object holding that object's data
items.rationale: Salesforce Connections converts standard and custom CRM objects into data lake objects from inside Tableau Next, so the data lands in Data 360 rather than staying in the source org. A federated view is what zero-copy Direct Connect gives you, and a semantic model is something an author builds afterwards on top of the resulting object.
items.evidence_quote: You can now convert standard and custom CRM objects into Data Lake Objects without ever leaving Tableau Next.

items.stem: In Data 360, what does the term data stream refer to?
options: The connection to a data source together with the data ingested through it
A scheduled SQL job that aggregates ingested records into an insight
The mapping between a data lake object and a data model object
A live query issued against an external warehouse without copying data
answer: The connection to a data source together with the data ingested through it
items.rationale: A data stream is the connection plus its ingested data. Aggregating with SQL is a calculated insight, DLO-to-DMO wiring is mapping, and querying without copying is federation.
items.evidence_quote: Data streams are the connections and associated data ingested into Data 360.

items.stem: Connecting to data directly in Tableau Next, rather than through a semantic model or an upload, means connecting to which Data 360 objects?
options: DMOs and CIOs
DLOs and DMOs
Data streams and data spaces
DLOs and data graphs
items.rationale: Direct connection is to data model objects and calculated insight objects - the harmonised and derived layer, not the raw landing objects.
items.evidence_quote: You can access data for creating visualizations and dashboards by connecting to data directly (Data 360 DMOs and CIOs), by connecting to a semantic model that already has a data connection, or by uploading your own data from CSV files.

items.stem: Acceleration is switched on for a zero copy data stream, and the cached object has a datetime field to use as its record modified field. What is the shortest interval Data 360 supports between incremental refreshes of that cached data?
items.rationale: Objects with a datetime field can be incrementally refreshed as often as every 15 minutes. Ten minutes is the Salesforce CRM connector's own incremental refresh cadence, not the cache refresh floor, and 24 hours is only the threshold above which you can also pick a time and day.
items.evidence_quote: You can incrementally refresh all objects with a datetime field as frequently as every 15 minutes.

items.stem: A client keeps several years of archived transactions in a big object in their Salesforce org and wants that history in Data 360 through the Salesforce CRM connector. What do you tell them?
options: The connector can't ingest big objects at all, so the history needs another route in
It works, but only in batch processing mode, because big objects can't be streamed
It works once the object is added to the DataCloudEntities Change Data Capture channel
It works only if the data lake object for the big object is created manually beforehand
answer: The connector can't ingest big objects at all, so the history needs another route in
items.rationale: The Salesforce CRM Connector doesn't support ingestion of big objects, so no processing mode or channel setting makes it work; the data has to arrive by another means, such as a file or API ingest. Batch versus streaming and the Change Data Capture channel affect how supported objects are processed, not whether a big object can be ingested.
items.evidence_quote: The Salesforce CRM Connector doesn’t support ingestion of big objects from Salesforce CRM.

items.stem: For one zero copy method, Data 360 reads the records a workflow needs directly out of the external system using its own query engine, which is only possible when the external data is organized in a supported open table format. Which method is that?
options: File Federation (Storage)
Query Federation (Compute)
Caching, by enabling acceleration on the data stream
Data ingestion into a standard data lake object
items.rationale: File federation targets the storage layer: Data 360 queries the external files itself, which is why a supported open table format is required. In query federation the external system's own compute engine runs the SQL and returns rows, and caching copies data into a local DLO rather than reading it in place.
items.evidence_quote: File Federation (Storage): Data 360 directly queries external storage systems, provided the data is organized using a supported open table format.

items.stem: A team wants to load dozens of small reference tables into Data 360 as CSV file uploads, one data stream each. At most how many data streams and data lake objects can be created from file uploads?
items.rationale: File upload is capped at a maximum of 100 data streams and DLOs, so a design that needs more reference tables than that has to use a connector or the Ingestion API for the remainder. The 2 GB and 1,050 column figures are per-file limits, not a count of streams.
items.evidence_quote: You can create a maximum of 100 data streams and DLOs from file uploads.

items.stem: A custom field on a connected Salesforce CRM object is being retired, and it is currently ingested by a Data 360 data stream. Put the removal steps in the order that avoids ingestion errors.
options: Disable the field in Data 360
Delete the field in the connected CRM with Object Manager
Remove the field from the Data 360 permission set in the connected CRM
answer: Delete the field in the connected CRM with Object Manager
Remove the field from the Data 360 permission set in the connected CRM
items.rationale: Disabling in Data 360 first stops ingestion of the field so the later CRM deletion can't break data stream refreshes; the permission set entry is cleaned up last, once the field no longer exists. Deleting in CRM first is what causes the ingestion errors.
items.evidence_quote: To delete a field from your connected CRM, first disable that field from Data 360 to avoid ingestion errors in data streams. After you disable a field, you can delete the field through the connected Salesforce CRM Object Manager admin tool. Then remove the field from the Data 360 permission set in that connected Salesforce CRM.

items.stem: A table being federated into Data 360 from an external source contains a column whose data type Data 360 doesn't support. Deploying the data stream fails until that column is removed or cast at the source.
items.rationale: The unsupported column is simply ignored: it appears on the Unsupported Fields tab during data stream creation and the rest of the table federates normally, so no change at the source is required to deploy. Nested types such as array and struct are never brought across.
items.evidence_quote: If the source data contains a data type that's not supported in Data 360, the column is ignored. During data stream creation, fields whose data types aren’t supported in Data 360 are listed under the Unsupported Fields tab.

items.stem: A team deploys the Content Document, Content Version, and Content Document Link data streams to bring CRM file attachments into Data 360, but nothing beyond file names and properties arrives. What is missing?
options: A search index, without which only file metadata is ingested
A data transform to unpack the file content into a data lake object
A mapping from the content data streams to the Individual data model object
A Files-enabled permission set for the running user of each data stream
answer: A search index, without which only file metadata is ingested
items.rationale: The three content data streams on their own ingest metadata for all files; creating a search index is what triggers ingestion of the file content itself, including the historical backlog in reverse chronological order. No data transform or DMO mapping performs that step.
items.evidence_quote: If you create the content data streams without an accompanying search index, Data 360 ingests only file metadata. To trigger file ingestion, create a search index.

items.stem: A data stream ingests a database table into a data lake object using the Incremental refresh mode, and some rows have since been removed from the source table. How do you get Data 360 to drop those rows from the data lake object?
options: Mark the records in the source system with a delete flag, which the next update acts on
Delete the records from the source table and let the next incremental update notice
Upload a delete file that lists the primary keys of the records to remove
Delete the records from the data lake object in Data Explorer
answer: Mark the records in the source system with a delete flag, which the next update acts on
items.rationale: An incremental refresh only picks up rows added or changed since the last run, so a row that has simply vanished from the source stays in the DLO; you flag it as deleted in the source, for example record_delete_flag = true, and the next update removes it. Delete files belong to the upsert mode on file-based connectors.
items.evidence_quote: To remove records from an incrementally updated DLO, mark deleted records in your source system with a Delete Record Flag.

items.stem: A data stream keeps rejecting rows, and the team wants to investigate the rejected rows later. For how many days does Data 360 retain problem records while the data stream still exists?
items.rationale: Problem records are kept for 30 days, so a backlog older than that is gone. Deleting the data stream earlier destroys its problem record DLOs before the 30 days elapse, which is why investigation has to happen while the stream is still in place.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 stores problem records for 30 days. However, if you delete a data stream with problem records before the 30 days, its problem record DLOs are also deleted.

items.stem: An existing Amazon S3 data stream in Data 360 is renamed through Edit Data Stream. The data lake object that the stream feeds is renamed to match.
items.rationale: Editing a data stream's name leaves the name of the DLO it uses untouched, so the two drift apart and a tidy-up rename cannot fix a badly named object. Naming conventions therefore have to be settled when the stream and its DLO are first created.
items.evidence_quote: Changing the name of a data stream doesn’t change the name of the data lake object (DLO) that the data stream uses.

items.stem: One data stream lands guest checkout records that carry both profile and engagement data, and the business needs each kind in its own data lake object. What do you set up in Data 360?
options: Multiple data transforms that read the same source DLO and write to different DLOs
Two data streams over the same source, each mapping only the fields it needs
One data transform whose output node writes to two DLOs at once
Two data model object mappings from the single DLO, one per subject area
answer: Multiple data transforms that read the same source DLO and write to different DLOs
items.rationale: The split happens after ingestion: several transforms read the one DLO the stream created and each writes its own target DLO. Mapping the single DLO to two data model objects harmonises the data but leaves one DLO, and a transform writes to the target its output node names rather than fanning out to two.
items.evidence_quote: To split a single data stream into multiple objects, set up multiple data transforms that read from the same source DLO and write to different DLOs.

items.stem: A data lake object can only come into existence as a by-product of bringing data into Data 360; there is no way to create one by hand.
items.rationale: Ingestion creates DLOs automatically, but a DLO can also be created manually - which is how a target object is prepared ahead of a transform or a streaming write.
items.evidence_quote: A DLO is automatically created from data brought into Data 360, but can also be created manually.

items.stem: A client will not allow a large warehouse table to be copied into Data 360, but wants it available for analysis. What does an external data lake object give them?
options: A reference that points to the data physically stored in the external source
A nightly full copy of the table held in Data 360 storage
A cached extract that Data 360 refreshes every 30 minutes
A one-off snapshot taken at the moment the object is created
answer: A reference that points to the data physically stored in the external source
items.rationale: An external DLO carries metadata and points at data that stays where it is. Every other option involves copying, which is the thing the client has ruled out.
items.evidence_quote: An external DLO acts as a reference, and points to the data physically stored in an external data source.

items.stem: Pair each Data 360 object type with what it actually is.

pairs.right: A container for the data brought into Data 360
A harmonized grouping of data created from data streams, insights, and other sources
A storage container with metadata for the data federated from an external data source

answer: Data lake object (DLO)::A container for the data brought into Data 360
Data model object (DMO)::A harmonized grouping of data created from data streams, insights, and other sources
External data lake object::A storage container with metadata for the data federated from an external data source
items.rationale: Ingestion lands data in a DLO; harmonisation maps DLOs onto the canonical DMO; federation produces an external DLO that holds metadata rather than the data itself.
items.evidence_quote:
| Data lake object (DLO) | A container for the data brought into Data 360. | A DLO is automatically created from data brought into Data 360, but can also be created manually. |
| Unstructured data lake object (UDLO) | A container for unstructured data referenced by Data 360. | A UDLO is created manually. |
| Data model object (DMO) | A harmonized grouping of data created from data streams, insights, and other sources. | A DLO is mapped to a DMO. |
| Unstructured data model object (UDMO) | A group of data created from an unstructured data source. | A UDLO is automatically mapped to an existing or new UDMO. |
| External data lake object | A storage container with metadata for the data federated from an external data source. |

rows: A container for the data brought into Data 360.
A DLO is automatically created from data brought into Data 360, but can also be created manually.
A container for unstructured data referenced by Data 360.
A harmonized grouping of data created from data streams, insights, and other sources.
A DLO is mapped to a DMO.
A group of data created from an unstructured data source.
A UDLO is automatically mapped to an existing or new UDMO.
A storage container with metadata for the data federated from an external data source.
An external DLO acts as a reference, and points to the data physically stored in an external data source.

items.stem: A Tableau Next workspace needs data before anything can be built in it. Which routes are supported for making data available in a workspace?
options: An existing data model object (DMO) in Data 360
A semantic model that already has a data connection
An upload of your own data from files or cloud-based resources
A direct ODBC connection configured inside the workspace
A published Tableau Desktop extract copied into the workspace
answer: An existing data model object (DMO) in Data 360
A semantic model that already has a data connection
An upload of your own data from files or cloud-based resources
items.rationale: These are the three documented routes. Tableau Next reaches data through Data 360 objects, through a semantic model that already carries a connection, or through an upload - not through its own database drivers, and not by importing Tableau Desktop artefacts.
items.evidence_quote: You can access data from an existing data model object (DMO) in Data 360, connect to a semantic model that has a data connection, or upload your own data from files or cloud-based resources.

items.stem: When creating a Salesforce CRM data stream in Data 360, a separate data stream is produced for each object selected. At most how many Salesforce objects can be selected in one pass?
items.rationale: Object selection for a CRM data stream is capped at 30 per pass, so a large Sales and Service footprint has to be brought in over several rounds. The 15 character limit belongs to the connection alias and 100 is the file upload data stream cap.
items.evidence_quote: Select up to 30 Salesforce objects to include in the data stream and click Next.

items.stem: Disabling a field in a Data 360 data stream also clears it out of the data lake object, so neither the field nor the data ingested into it before it was disabled remains there. True or false?
items.rationale: Disabling only stops new data arriving for that field: the field stays in the DLO and the data ingested before it was disabled is still available, and a DLO field can't be deleted at all. That is also why the name of a disabled field can't be reused.
items.evidence_quote: The disabled field remains in the data lake object (DLO), and the data ingested before the field was disabled is still available in the DLO.

items.stem: A Salesforce CRM data stream keeps processing in batch mode when the customer expected near-real-time streaming. Which conditions change the processing mode to batch?
options: The object, object type, or derived field doesn't support streaming
Batch ingested standard or custom formula fields are included in the data stream
The data stream has custom entities whose deployment status is In Development rather than Deployed
More than 30 Salesforce objects were selected when the data stream was created
The periodic full refresh interval for the data stream is set to None
The data stream was created from a starter data bundle instead of by picking objects
answer: The object, object type, or derived field doesn't support streaming
Batch ingested standard or custom formula fields are included in the data stream
The data stream has custom entities whose deployment status is In Development rather than Deployed
items.rationale: Unsupported objects or derived fields, batch ingested formula fields, and custom entities left In Development all push the stream back to batch. The object cap and the bundle used to create the stream are unrelated to streaming eligibility, and a full refresh interval of None simply means periodic full refresh is off.
items.evidence_quote: Streaming isn't available under the following conditions, which change the processing mode to batch: The object, object type, or derived field don't support streaming. See Object Support for CRM Data Streams. You include batch ingested standard or custom formula fields in your data stream. Learn how to create a Salesforce CRM cdata stream. Your data stream has custom entities where the deployment status is In Development instead of Deployed.

items.stem: An Excel file is uploaded to a Tableau Next workspace with the Data Interpreter, and it cannot work out the data type of one column. How is that column handled?
options: It is typed as a string
It is typed as a number
It is left untyped until someone assigns a type
It is excluded from the uploaded data
answer: It is typed as a string
items.rationale: The Data Interpreter falls back to a string type for any field whose type it can't identify, so a column that should be numeric or a date can arrive as text and needs checking before modelling. The upload is not blocked and the column is not dropped.
items.evidence_quote: If the Data Interpreter doesn't identify a field’s data type, it automatically assigns a string type to that data.

items.stem: Salesforce publishes an optimal data volume for each zero copy federation source when caching is enabled, and exceeding it produces polling time-out and job execution errors. Pair each source with the volume observed in testing.
options: Amazon Redshift
Snowflake
Databricks
Google BigQuery

pairs.right: Up to 234 GB
Up to 20 GB
Up to 23 GB
Up to 10 GB

items.rationale: Redshift tolerates by far the largest cached volume at 234 GB, BigQuery the smallest at 10 GB, with Snowflake at 20 GB and Databricks at 23 GB close together. These are the figures a sizing conversation turns on, and the equivalent row counts quoted alongside them are only representative.
items.evidence_quote: During the testing phase, we observed that the optimal data volume returned from the data lake when caching is enabled is up to 234 GB for Amazon Redshift, 20 GB for Snowflake, 23 GB for Databricks, and 10 GB for Google BigQuery.

items.stem: A client wants to federate their warehouse tables into Data 360 with zero copy instead of ingesting them. Which capabilities can they not use against that federated data?
options: Streaming data transforms
Near real time identity resolution
Rapid segmentation and activation
Batch data transforms
Identity resolution
Segmentation
items.rationale: Zero copy federation supports the batch versions of these capabilities - batch data transforms, identity resolution and segmentation all work - but not their real-time or rapid variants, nor schema extension on the external object. The distinction to remember is batch yes, streaming and rapid no.
items.evidence_quote: You can’t use these features of Data 360 when federating data from external sources. Extending schema with formula fields or data type changes, Changes in data types, Data sharing of external DLOs and DMOs with an external data lake, Rapid segmentation and activation, Streaming data transforms, Near real time identity resolution, Streaming predictions in BYOM, Changes to the source table schema (field name changes, capitalization changes)

items.stem: A Salesforce CRM connector data stream exposes a Full Refresh Interval, which decides when its periodic full refresh is triggered. Select every value that interval can be set to.
options: None
5 Days
10 Days
25 Days
30 Days
50 Days
90 Days
items.rationale: The interval is a fixed menu of None, 10, 25 and 50 days, and None, the default, disables the periodic full refresh entirely. Arbitrary values such as 30 or 90 days cannot be entered, and a stream in streaming mode cannot have the interval configured at all.
items.evidence_quote: For Full Refresh Interval, choose between None, 10 Days, 25 Days, or 50 Days, depending on your organization’s needs.

items.stem: The Full Refresh extract method sends all data for all time on every cycle, and Data 360 supports it only up to a stated data size. What is the largest volume it can be used on, in millions of rows?
items.rationale: Full Refresh is supported on data of 100 million rows or smaller; past that the design has to move to Delta Extract by Date or by Number. It is the figure that decides whether a large source can keep using a full snapshot at all.
items.evidence_quote: The Full Refresh extract method can be used on data of 100 million rows or smaller.

items.stem: When refreshing an uploaded file in Tableau Next, what is the largest CSV file size supported, in MB?
items.rationale: Refresh caps CSV at 100 MB and Excel at 10 MB. The two numbers are different, which catches people who remember only one of them.
items.evidence_quote: Files are limited to 10 MB for Excel files and 100 MB for CSV files for refreshes.

items.stem: What causes a streaming data graph in Data 360 to refresh automatically?
options: A change in the source data
A refresh interval defined on the data graph
A manual rebuild of the data graph
A change to the data graph's filter conditions
answer: A change in the source data
items.rationale: Streaming data graphs run automatically when source data changes and update only the affected data, which is the point of choosing them over a scheduled refresh. They have no defined interval to set, and the refresh type can't be switched after creation.
items.evidence_quote: Unlike scheduled refreshes that rely on defined intervals, streaming data graphs run automatically when source data changes.

items.stem: Put these four stages of the Data 360 data flow into the order in which they happen.
options: Prepare your data through transformation and data governance features
Harmonize your data to a standard data model
Unify data with identity resolution rulesets
Query and analyze data using insights
answer: Prepare your data through transformation and data governance features
Harmonize your data to a standard data model
Unify data with identity resolution rulesets
Query and analyze data using insights
items.rationale: Transformation and governance shape the raw landed data, harmonization maps it onto the standard data model, identity resolution then unifies the harmonized records into profiles, and insights are calculated on that unified result. Expecting identity resolution to run before the data is harmonized to the model is the usual mistake in a delivery plan.
items.evidence_quote: Prepare your data through transformation and data governance features. Harmonize your data to a standard data model. Unify data with identity resolution rulesets. Query and analyze data using insights.

items.stem: A consultant builds a data graph by choosing fields from several related DMOs. What does Data 360 create as the result?
options: A single read-only record holding all the combined data in one JSON blob
A materialized DMO whose fields can be edited and remapped later
A calculated insight object that recomputes the chosen fields on a schedule
A query-time view over the source DMOs that stores nothing itself
answer: A single read-only record holding all the combined data in one JSON blob
items.rationale: A data graph pre-prepares the chosen fields into one read-only record whose combined data sits in a single JSON blob, which is why queries against it return almost instantly. It is not an editable object like a DMO, not an aggregation like a calculated insight, and it does store the prepared data rather than resolving the joins at query time.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 then collects and changes these chosen fields into a single, read-only data graph record. This record puts all the combined data into one JSON blob.

items.stem: Two source systems each use the value 1001 as a customer identifier, and both streams are harmonized into the same data model object. Data 360 keeps the two apart by adding key qualifier fields to the DLO fields that hold those identifiers. Name the capability those qualifier fields implement.
items.rationale: Key qualifier fields are the mechanism; the capability they implement is Fully Qualified Keys, which qualifies a key value with its source so that identical primary or foreign key values arriving from different systems do not conflict once they are harmonized into one DMO. Identity resolution decides which people are the same person; it does not stop raw key values colliding.
items.evidence_quote: Use Fully Qualified Keys (FQK) to avoid key conflicts when data from different sources are harmonized in the Data 360 data model. Configure key qualifier fields for all data lake object (DLO) fields that contain a key value to use FQKs.

items.stem: In a Data 360 data graph, what is the name for the primary key of the primary data model object, which acts as the graph's main identifier and the initial access point for retrieving its data?
items.rationale: The root key is the primary key of the data graph's primary DMO and is what a retrieval starts from, which is why it can also be flagged in DMO metadata to speed up refresh computation. A primary key on a child DMO or a key qualifier is not the root key.
items.evidence_quote: Root Key is the primary key of the primary data model object (DMO) of the data graph. In a data graph, a root key is the main identifier. It is also the initial access point for data retrieval.

items.stem: A governance lead sketches a Data 360 tag structure three deep: a top-level tag, a tag beneath it, and a third tag beneath that. Which tag structure does Data 360 actually support?
options: One parent and multiple children, but only one level of hierarchy
Multiple parents and multiple children, nested to any depth
One parent and one child, nested to any depth
No parent or child relationships at all, so tags stay flat
answer: One parent and multiple children, but only one level of hierarchy
items.rationale: A tag can sit under one parent and can itself have many children, but the hierarchy stops there, so a grandchild tag is not possible and a three-deep design has to be flattened or expressed with classifications instead. Tags are not flat either, which is the other common misreading.
items.evidence_quote: Tags can have one parent and multiple child tags, but they don't support more than one level of hierarchy.

items.stem: A batch data transform built in Tableau Next is removed because nobody needs it any more. What becomes of the data it had already written to its target?
options: It stays where it is, in the target object
It is deleted along with the transform
It is retained for 30 days and then deleted
It is deleted only if the transform created the target object
answer: It stays where it is, in the target object
items.rationale: Deleting the transform removes only the recipe, not its output, so the target object and its rows survive and anything built on them keeps working. That also means a deleted transform leaves data behind that nothing refreshes any more, which is the clean-up trap.
items.evidence_quote: Delete any batch data transforms that you no longer need. Deleting a batch data transform doesn’t delete its target data.

items.stem: In Data 360, ingested data keeps its source schema until it is mapped onto the standard, extensible model that Salesforce ships with the platform. What is that standard model called?
items.rationale: Mapping targets the Customer 360 Data Model, the shipped and extensible model whose objects are the DMOs. Data lake objects hold the preserved source schema before mapping, and the semantic model in Tableau Semantics sits above the mapped data rather than being the mapping target.
items.evidence_quote: During data mapping, the preserved data source schema is mapped to an opinionated and extensible data model, called the Customer 360 Data Model.

items.stem: Data Lens offers three interface views for exploring a data object in Data 360. Pair each view with what it presents.
options: Profile View
Data Grid View
List View

pairs.right: Columns drawn as colored bars that summarize distributions, values, and nulls
A spreadsheet-like view of row-level detail
A place to show or hide fields to streamline what you see

answer: Profile View::Columns drawn as colored bars that summarize distributions, values, and nulls
Data Grid View::A spreadsheet-like view of row-level detail
List View::A place to show or hide fields to streamline what you see
items.rationale: The three views do different jobs: Profile View summarizes each column graphically, Data Grid View drops to individual rows, and List View only controls which fields are displayed. No pairing works in more than one direction.
items.evidence_quote: Profile View: Shows data columns as colored bars, summarizing data distributions, values, and nulls. You can click values to include/exclude or highlight relationships. Data Grid View: A spreadsheet-like view for viewing row-level details. Synchronized with the profile pane for consistency. List View: Show or hide fields to streamline your view.

items.stem: In Data 360 data governance, what is the name for a hierarchical set of categories and subcategories of tags that classifies data by its type, sensitivity, usage, or domain?
items.rationale: A taxonomy is the hierarchy itself; tags are the individual labels inside it and classifications add sensitivity or usage meaning to those tags. Consistent taxonomies are what let masking and access policies be applied accurately.
items.evidence_quote: In Data 360 data governance, a taxonomy is a hierarchical set of categories and subcategories (or tags) that classifies data based on its type, sensitivity, usage, or domain.

items.stem: How is unified lineage made available in a Data 360 org?
options: It is available automatically in all customer orgs, with no setup required
An admin must enable it for each data space in Setup
It requires installing the lineage data kit in the org
It must be switched on for each object you want traced

items.rationale: Unified lineage needs no provisioning: a background job collects lineage for existing objects and captures later changes incrementally. There is no per-data-space switch, no data kit to install, and no per-object opt-in.
items.evidence_quote: Unified lineage is automatically available in all customer orgs and no setup is required.

items.stem: Pair each Customer 360 Data Model contact point object with the kind of value it is designed to hold for an individual.

items.stem: Without any custom permission sets being built, who can already open Data Explorer and Profile Explorer in a Data 360 org?
options: Data 360 admins and data aware specialists
Every user who holds a Data Cloud license
Only users assigned the Data Cloud Architect permission set
Nobody, until access is granted explicitly
answer: Data 360 admins and data aware specialists
items.rationale: Both explorers are on by default for Data 360 admins and data aware specialists. Reaching any other role, or taking access away from those two, means cloning a Data 360 permission set and editing the system permissions.
items.evidence_quote: Data Explorer and Profile Explorer are enabled by default for Data 360 admins and data aware specialists.

items.stem: A client already prepares data with batch data transforms in Data 360 and asks what they would gain or lose by building them in Tableau Next instead. What actually differs?
options: How you reach and create a transform
Which node types you can put on the canvas
How the data processing logic behaves at run time
Which transformations a transform node can contain
answer: How you reach and create a transform
items.rationale: Tableau Next wraps the same engine: the entry points and some UI elements are its own, while the transformation capabilities, node functionality and processing logic are the Data 360 ones. Tableau Next does add its own limitations page, but none of them changes node types, transformations or run-time processing.
items.evidence_quote: While accessing and creating batch data transforms differs in Tableau Next, the transformation capabilities, node functionality, and data processing logic are identical to Data 360.

items.stem: Data 360 publishes control events for configuration objects such as data streams, segments and calculated insights, carrying values like ImportRunStatus and LastRunStatus. Which Salesforce tool do you use to set up notifications on those events without opening each record?
items.rationale: Control events are consumed by building flows in Flow Builder, which is what lets an admin be notified of a failed data stream refresh or calculated insight run instead of checking records in Lightning Experience.
items.evidence_quote: Set up notifications for your Data 360 data in Flow Builder and create reports to see your Data 360 statuses.

items.stem: Data 360 adds lineage fields to a data object so you can tell where each record came from. Pair each lineage field with what it identifies.
options: Data Source
Data Source Object
Internal Organization

pairs.right: The system the records came from, also known as the external source ID
The object or file within that system that the record came from
The business unit that owns the data record

answer: Data Source::The system the records came from, also known as the external source ID
Data Source Object::The object or file within that system that the record came from
Internal Organization::The business unit that owns the data record
items.rationale: Data Source names the originating system, Data Source Object narrows that to the specific table, file or external object, and Internal Organization identifies the owning business unit inside that system.
items.evidence_quote: Data Source—A reference ID for the logical name referring to the source of records, also identified as the external source ID. For example, SFMC_1487860 indicates records from Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement (SFMC) and the internal Org Id. Data Source Object—A reference ID for the logical name of the object where the record came from, such as the name of a cloud storage file or another connector's external object. For example, SFMC_1487860_Campaign indicates records from Marketing Cloud Engagement, the internal Org Id, and the object Campaign. Internal Organization—A reference ID to the business unit or other internal organization that owns the data record.

items.stem: A client asks which time zone Data 360 applies when it publishes and refreshes segments and activations, and where that setting is controlled. What governs it?
options: The time zone set in Salesforce
A separate Data 360 time zone configured in Data Cloud Setup
A time zone property set on the data space
UTC, which Data 360 uses for every scheduled job
answer: The time zone set in Salesforce
items.rationale: Data 360 does not hold its own time zone setting for segment publishing and refreshing, so to change it you change the time zone in Salesforce; there is no data space or Data Cloud Setup time zone to adjust.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 uses the time zone set in Salesforce when publishing and refreshing segments and activations.

items.stem: A client exports customer data from a legacy system as one wide table, with every related attribute repeated as extra columns on the customer row. Which shape does the Data 360 standard data model require before that data can be mapped to it?
options: Normalized: divided into multiple tables with established relationships
Denormalized: combined into a single table so retrieval is faster
Either shape, because field mapping reshapes the data automatically
Denormalized for profile data and normalized for engagement data
answer: Normalized: divided into multiple tables with established relationships
items.rationale: The standard data model is normalized, so a denormalized spreadsheet-style export has to be transformed into related tables before mapping. Mapping does not reshape the data for you, and the requirement is the same for every object category.
items.evidence_quote: The Data 360 standard data model is normalized, so incoming data must be normalized before it can be mapped to the data model.

items.stem: A consultant lays out a batch data transform with input, filter and join nodes and then finds that Data 360 will not let the transform be saved. Which node type is mandatory in every batch data transform?
options: Output
Aggregate
Schema change
Formula
items.rationale: The output node is what writes the results to a target data lake or data model object, so a transform without one produces nothing and cannot be saved. Aggregate, schema change and formula nodes are all optional shaping steps.
items.evidence_quote: You can’t save a batch data transform without an output node.

items.stem: A Data 360 org runs either on Salesforce's own first-party infrastructure or on public cloud infrastructure, and support cases and incident notices sometimes turn on which one it is. What is Salesforce's term for that infrastructure an org's Data 360 instance runs on?
items.rationale: Salesforce calls the infrastructure a Data 360 instance runs on its functional domain, abbreviated FD, and it is found with the instance and endpoint on the Data Cloud Setup home page. A data space is a logical partition of data inside the org, and a hyperforce instance is not the term the documentation uses here.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 runs on both Salesforce's first-party infrastructure and public cloud infrastructure, referred to as a functional domain (FD).

items.stem: Creating a search index configuration in Data 360 also creates two extra data model objects: one stores the chunked content, and the other stores the vector embeddings generated from it. Name the data model object that stores those embeddings.
items.rationale: The embeddings land in a dedicated index data model object, whose primary key is one row per embedding. The chunk table holds the text the embedding was generated from, and the source DMO or UDMO holds the content itself, so neither is where the vector is kept.
items.evidence_quote: The index data model object (IDMO) stores generated vector embeddings.

items.stem: In a batch data transform formula, how does the output of a window function differ from the output of an aggregation function?
options: It returns a result for every input row, whereas an aggregation groups rows
It returns one result per group, whereas an aggregation returns one per row
It returns a result only for the first row of each partition
It returns a result only once the whole transform run has finished
answer: It returns a result for every input row, whereas an aggregation groups rows
items.rationale: A window function calculates over a window of related rows but still emits a value on each row, which is why it can be used for running totals, ranks and row-to-row comparisons without collapsing the grain. Collapsing rows into groups is exactly what an aggregation does instead.
items.evidence_quote: Unlike aggregation functions that group rows, window functions return a result for each row.

items.stem: A data graph is scheduled to refresh more often than once a day, and between refreshes it keeps showing records the source has already deleted and relationships that don't line up. Name the condition the documentation gives for these temporary inconsistencies.
items.rationale: Data drift is the documented side effect of refreshing a data graph more frequently than once per day; the rapid cycles don't fully reconcile source updates, and the daily full refresh is what clears it.
items.evidence_quote: When you schedule a data graph to refresh more frequently than once per day, you can experience data drift.

items.stem: In the Customer 360 Data Model, what does the engagement subject define?
options: Interactions with a party, such as a phone call or an email a customer receives
Contact information, personal or business, for a specific customer or account
The products, catalogs and price books a company offers for sale
The consent and communication preferences captured for a customer
answer: Interactions with a party, such as a phone call or an email a customer receives
items.rationale: The engagement subject covers interactions with a party, which is why its DMOs are things like Email Engagement, Website Engagement and Shopping Cart Engagement. Contact details for a customer belong to the party subject instead.
items.evidence_quote: The Customer 360 Data Model engagement subject defines interactions with a party. Example interactions could be speaking to a customer over the phone or receiving a customer email.

items.stem: A client running Informatica IDMC for master data management asks whether adopting Data 360 identity resolution means they can retire it. What is Salesforce's stated position?
options: Data 360 isn't an MDM system, so identity resolution complements the existing MDM rather than replacing it
Data 360 identity resolution supersedes MDM once unified profiles have been built
Data 360 and IDMC MDM can't run in the same landscape, so the client has to choose one
Data 360 takes over master data for customer records, leaving IDMC to master everything else
answer: Data 360 isn't an MDM system, so identity resolution complements the existing MDM rather than replacing it
items.rationale: IDMC creates a golden record through MDM while Data 360 creates unified profiles through identity resolution, and Salesforce positions the two as complementary: the MDM keeps managing master data and unified profiles become the activation layer over it. Neither product is presented as a substitute for the other.
items.evidence_quote: Because Data 360 isn’t an MDM system, its Identity Resolution capabilities don’t replace IDMC MDM functionality. Instead, it acts as a complement to your existing MDM solutions.

items.stem: How does the streaming audit data model object in Data 360 differ from a standard audience DMO?
options: It is a single, append-only object that keeps a continuous historical log of everything sent
It is rewritten in place on each run, so only the most recent activation payload remains
It stores aggregate counts of the records sent rather than the records themselves
It is a query-time view over the activation target that stores nothing of its own
answer: It is a single, append-only object that keeps a continuous historical log of everything sent
items.rationale: The audit DMO accumulates rather than replaces, which is what makes it usable as an audit trail of streaming activations. An object that was overwritten each run, or that held only counts, could not serve that purpose.
items.evidence_quote: Unlike standard audience DMOs, the streaming audit DMO is a single, append-only object. It serves as a continuous historical log of everything sent via a streaming DMO activation.

items.stem: A source table has no single column that uniquely identifies a row, so the team wants to designate several columns together as the primary key. Data 360 allows composite keys to be assigned for only one kind of data share. Name that kind.
answer: Bring Your Own Lake data share
items.rationale: Composite keys are a Bring Your Own Lake (BYOL) data share capability only, so a design that depends on them has to be scoped to BYOL sources; for other sources the same effect has to come from a formula field that concatenates the columns into a single primary key.
items.evidence_quote: In Data Cloud, you can assign composite keys only for Bring Your Own Lake (BYOL) data shares.

items.stem: When files arrive at Data 360 out of sequence, the platform needs a reference point to decide whether an incoming record is newer than the one already stored. Name the field, designated on the source object during setup, that provides it.
items.rationale: The record modified field is chosen when the source object is defined and is what stops an older file overwriting a newer record when ingestion order does not match event order. The primary key identifies which record is being updated, not which version wins.
items.evidence_quote: The record modified field acts as a reference point when the system is deciding whether to update the record in the event data is received out of order.

items.stem: Three unstructured data lake objects in Data 360 reference case-recording files held in three different external blob stores, and the three sources are logically the same object. What does the UDLO-to-UDMO mapping model allow here?
options: All three UDLOs can be mapped to a single UDMO
Each UDLO must be mapped to its own UDMO
One UDLO can be mapped to all three UDMOs
The three UDLOs must be merged into one UDLO before mapping
answer: All three UDLOs can be mapped to a single UDMO
items.rationale: The relationship is 1:1 or N:1: many UDLOs can share one UDMO, which is exactly how logically identical sources in different stores are consolidated. What is not allowed is the reverse - a single UDLO fanning out to several UDMOs.
items.evidence_quote: The relationship between UDLOs and UDMOs can be 1:1 or N:1. In other words, each UDLO can be mapped to at most 1 UDMO, while multiple UDLOs can be mapped to a single UDMO.

items.stem: A calculated insight has just been created in Data 360 and a marketer wants to build segment criteria on the metric it produces. What does Data 360 require before that insight can be used in a segment?
options: It must be validated in Data Explorer
It must be published to a data space
It must be scheduled to run at least daily
It must be converted into a streaming insight
answer: It must be validated in Data Explorer
items.rationale: Validation in Data Explorer, where the author checks that the data and formulas are accurate, is a prerequisite for using an insight in a segment. Scheduling and data space membership affect when and where the insight runs, but neither is the gate on segmentation.
items.evidence_quote: After creation, validate your calculated or streaming insight in Data Explorer to ensure that your data and formulas are accurate. You must validate an insight before you use it in a segment.

items.stem: The Customer 360 Data Model groups recorded issues such as support tickets into its case subject area. Which data model objects does that subject area include?
options: Individual
Account
Account Contact
Case
Contact Point Email
Party Identifier
