items.evidence_quote: The case subject area includes the individual, account, account contact, and case data model objects.

items.stem: A client wants to use the Data 360 features that respond in milliseconds, such as real-time segments, real-time identity resolution and real-time data actions. What has to be built before any of them can be used?
options: A real-time data graph
A streaming data transform on each source object
A real-time calculated insight
A data stream configured for upsert refresh
items.rationale: The real-time capabilities all read from a materialised real-time view of the data model, so a real-time data graph is the prerequisite for the whole set. A streaming data transform only reshapes records as they land and does not create that view.
items.evidence_quote: To use real-time capabilities, you must first create a real-time data graph.

items.stem: The output node of a batch data transform can create a brand new data model object to receive the results, and that object can then feed another batch data transform, identity resolution, calculated insights and segmentation. What is this kind of data model object called?
items.rationale: A batch data transform can only write into a transform-type DMO, and Salesforce calls that object a transform data model object. It is an ordinary DMO for downstream consumers, but only a data transform can populate it.
items.evidence_quote: The object that holds the output is called a transform data model object.

items.stem: Put the three things that nodes on a batch data transform canvas do into the order the data moves through them.
options: Bring in data with an Input node
Manipulate the data with Transform, Join, Aggregate or Filter nodes
Write the results to a target with an Output node
answer: Bring in data with an Input node
Manipulate the data with Transform, Join, Aggregate or Filter nodes
Write the results to a target with an Output node
items.rationale: A batch data transform reads from input nodes, changes the data through the intermediate nodes strung together on the canvas, then writes the result to a target object that downstream processes can consume.
items.evidence_quote: Batch data transforms provide nodes that allow you to bring in data, transform it, and write the results to a target.

items.stem: A data stream has landed a batch of order records in Data 360. Before that data can be used for segmentation, activation or analytics, what has to be done to it?
options: It must be mapped to a data model object (DMO)
It must be added to a data graph as the primary object
It must have a secondary index defined on its primary key
It must be classified with an ExternalData.Visibility tag
answer: It must be mapped to a data model object (DMO)
items.rationale: Mapping into the Customer 360 Data Model is the gate every downstream Data 360 operation sits behind. Data graphs, secondary indexes and visibility tags are all optional refinements applied after mapping, not prerequisites for using the data.
items.evidence_quote: Data imported into Data 360 must be mapped to a DMO before it can be used for segmentation, activation, analytics, or any other operation.

items.stem: A client insists that a large warehouse table stays where it is and is never copied into Data 360, but analysts still need to run queries against it. Which Data 360 query capability is the right one to reach for?
options: Query federation
Query Editor
Data 360 Connect API
Data Cloud One
items.rationale: Query federation runs the query on the partner-managed compute, so nothing is duplicated into Data 360. Query Editor and the Connect API are ways of issuing queries against Data 360 objects, and Data Cloud One is a multi-org access pattern, not a way of leaving data in place.
items.evidence_quote: Use query federation to query your partner-managed compute without duplicating your data into Data 360.

items.stem: Name the Data 360 capability that conceals sensitive field values when they are queried, so authorized users can still work with the data and its relationships without seeing it in plaintext.
items.rationale: The feature conceals values at query time without altering the stored data, its accuracy or its relationships. Encryption at rest is a separate protection, and access policies decide whether a user sees the data at all rather than how it is displayed.
items.evidence_quote: Dynamic data masking conceals sensitive data without altering its usability, accuracy, or relationships.

items.stem: An org is rolling out fully qualified keys and adding a key qualifier for each source system. At most how many active key qualifiers can be added?
items.rationale: The ceiling is 20 active key qualifiers, and a qualifier counts as active while it is used on a DLO field, so making room means removing one from every field that references it and then deleting it. Teams that mint a qualifier per source system hit this and have to consolidate.
items.evidence_quote: Configure key qualifiers for all DLO fields that contain either a primary or foreign key. You can add up to 20 active key qualifiers.

items.stem: A client wants Vehicle Telematics Event records from Data 360 shown on the Vehicle record page in their org, but identity resolution has not been completed for that data. Which enrichment gets them there?
options: A Direct-DMO related list enrichment
A related list enrichment through the Unified Individual object
A copy field enrichment on the Vehicle record
A Data 360 Profile Insights Lightning component
items.rationale: A Direct-DMO related list uses a direct relationship between the DMO and the Salesforce object, so it does not wait on identity resolution. Ordinary related lists and copy fields both hang off the Individual or Unified Individual, and Profile Insights shows a calculated insight measure on a person record, so all three depend on unification being done.
items.evidence_quote: Direct-DMO related lists show information from any DMO that's connected to the Salesforce object through a direct relationship. The direct relationship doesn't require identity resolution to be completed for the DMO.

items.stem: Data 360 offers three kinds of insights. Pair each one with the way it processes data.
options: Calculated insights
Streaming insights
Real-time insights

pairs.right: High volume data processing and metrics generation
Continuous stream processing as data is received, with time windows as little as 1 minute
Processing in real time, with results in milliseconds

answer: Calculated insights::High volume data processing and metrics generation
Streaming insights::Continuous stream processing as data is received, with time windows as little as 1 minute
Real-time insights::Processing in real time, with results in milliseconds
items.rationale: Calculated insights are the high-volume metric engine, streaming insights process continuously with windows down to a minute, and only real-time insights answer in milliseconds. Reaching for a streaming insight when the requirement is millisecond personalization, or a real-time insight when the requirement is heavy historic computation, is the classic mis-scope.
items.evidence_quote: | How is data processed? | High volume data processing and metrics generation. | Continuous stream processing as Data 360 receives data. Time windows as little as 1 minute. | In real-time, with results in milliseconds. |

rows: High volume data processing and metrics generation.
Continuous stream processing as Data 360 receives data. Time windows as little as 1 minute.
In real-time, with results in milliseconds.
Collected in batches as sets of records and processed as unit.
Work on events as they’re updated via streaming data from Web SDK and Mobile SDK.
Data 360 processes insights for every event that updates in the real-time data graph.
How can you use this data in Data 360?
Perform complex calculations usually needing large historic data.
Handle micro batches of a few records.
Calculates an insight from a single record to drive personalization logic using aggregate metrics.
Personalized ecommerce experience with recommendations based on which products the user is viewing.

items.stem: When scoping a Data 360 build, which data streams arrive with their DMO mappings and object relationships already in place, so the team does not have to establish them?
options: Streams deployed through standard data bundles
Streams created from an ingestion API endpoint
Streams whose DLO field names exactly match the DMO field names
Streams created by uploading a CSV file
answer: Streams deployed through standard data bundles
items.rationale: Only standard data bundle deployments get mappings and relationships automatically; for every custom data stream the team must make sure the required mappings and relationships are set up properly. Automapping can suggest field mappings once you pick a target DMO, but it is a suggestion you review and save and it never creates the object relationships.
items.evidence_quote: Mappings and relationships are set up automatically only for data streams that are deployed through standard data bundles.

items.stem: A marketer wants segment criteria built on a metric produced by a streaming insight. Data 360 supports using a streaming insight in segmentation and activation.
items.rationale: Segmentation and activation do not support streaming insights, so a requirement to segment on a metric has to be met with a calculated insight instead. Streaming insights exist to drive near real-time orchestration and data actions, not audience building.
items.evidence_quote: Note: Segment and activation don't support streaming insights.

items.stem: A design puts a calculated insight into a data graph so that its metrics travel with the profile record. Which conditions does Data 360 place on that?
options: It must be based on a data model object that is also included in the data graph
The DMO's primary key field must be configured as a dimension on the calculated insight object
It must be added at the root of the data graph
It must be added as a child node under the DMO it is based on
All of its measures must also be configured as dimensions on the primary DMO
answer: It must be based on a data model object that is also included in the data graph
The DMO's primary key field must be configured as a dimension on the calculated insight object
It must be added at the root of the data graph
items.rationale: The insight has to share a DMO with the graph, that DMO's primary key has to appear as a dimension on the insight so the rows can be tied to the record, and the insight object can only hang at the root. Trying to nest it under the DMO it derives from is exactly what the documentation rules out.
items.evidence_quote: In Data 360, you can include calculated insights in a data graph as long as they’re based on a data model object (DMO) that’s also included in the data graph. The DMO’s primary key field must be configured as a dimension on the calculated insight object (CIO). You can add a CIO only at the root of a data graph. You can’t add a CIO as a child node under another object.

items.stem: A custom data model object is being created in Data 360 by uploading a CSV file that lists its fields. Put the four columns the CSV must contain into the order Data 360 expects.
options: Data Type
Primary Key
Field Label
Field API Name
items.rationale: Data 360 reads the upload positionally: label, API name, data type, then the primary key flag. If a header row is declared it is ignored and the column names can be anything, so the column order rather than the heading text is what decides which field attribute each value populates.
items.evidence_quote:
The CSV file must have four columns in this order. If the CSV file has a header row, the columns can have any name, but the column contents must follow the order.

- Field Label
- Field API Name
- Data Type
- Primary Key

items.stem: A team starts a new Intelligent Context configuration in Data 360 and, rather than uploading sample files, points it at a data model object so they can see how its content is parsed and chunked. At most how many records can that data model object hold?
items.rationale: A new configuration is evaluated against a deliberately small sample: up to five uploaded files, or a DMO of up to 30 records. A design that expects to tune chunking against a full production object has to be re-planned around that sample size.
items.evidence_quote: To get started with a new Intelligent Context configuration, upload up to five unstructured files or select a data model object (DMO) with up to 30 records.

items.stem: A dynamic data masking policy for structured data in Data 360 offers four masking methods. Pair each method with what a restricted user then sees.
options: Redaction
Nullification
Datetime Rounding
Numeric Rounding

pairs.right: The masked characters replaced with X
The data replaced with NULL
Only the year, or the year and month
The number rounded to a whole number or a set number of decimal places

answer: Redaction::The masked characters replaced with X
Datetime Rounding::Only the year, or the year and month
Numeric Rounding::The number rounded to a whole number or a set number of decimal places
items.rationale: Redaction substitutes X for a chosen number of characters and nullification wipes the value altogether, while the two rounding methods keep a usable but coarser value: dates cut back to year or year and month, numbers rounded to a whole number or a set precision. Choosing between them is a choice about how much analytical value survives the mask.
items.evidence_quote: Redaction - Replace masked characters with X. Select the number of characters to redact. Nullification - Replace data with NULL. Datetime Rounding - Simplify date and time display by showing only the year or the year and month. Numeric Rounding - Round numbers to the nearest whole number or the specified decimal places.

items.stem: Which join types can a calculated insight query use to combine data model objects in Data 360?
options: Inner join
Left join
Right join
Full join
Cross join
Lookup
items.rationale: Calculated insight SQL supports inner, left, right and full joins only. Cross join and lookup are join operations offered by batch data transforms, not by calculated insight queries.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 supports four types of joins in a calculated insight: inner, left, right, and full.

items.stem: A Marketing Cloud Engagement data extension data stream was provisioned with a Refresh mode that no longer suits the client, and Upsert is not available for that stream. Deleting the data stream and re-creating it lets you pick a different Refresh mode.
items.rationale: Where Upsert is unavailable the Refresh settings are fixed at provisioning time, and a deleted-and-recreated data stream still runs on that same Refresh mode, so the refresh behaviour has to be planned for up front rather than corrected later.
items.evidence_quote: If you can’t use Upsert, you can’t change the Refresh settings. When the data stream was provisioned, the Refresh mode was set. Even deleting the data stream and recreating it, still uses that Refresh mode.

items.stem: In a batch data transform you need to enrich each row of the left object with attributes from a second object, and the row count of the left object must not change even where several rows on the right match. Which join operation does that?
options: Lookup
Left join
Inner join
Full outer join
items.rationale: A lookup returns one output row for every row of the left object, so the grain is preserved. A left join also keeps unmatched left rows, but it emits every matched row, duplicating a left row when the right side has several matches.
items.evidence_quote: To ensure that the grain of the results doesn’t change, the lookup output data includes one row for each row in the left object.

items.stem: You plan a streaming data transform in Data 360 to standardize values as records arrive in a data lake object. What does the platform require of the transform's target?
options: It must be an object other than the source object
It must be the source object, so records are cleaned in place
It must be a data model object rather than a data lake object
It must reuse the source object's primary key field
answer: It must be an object other than the source object
items.rationale: A streaming data transform reads one record from a source object and writes to a separate target, so cleaning in place is not possible and a second object has to be planned for. The target can be a data lake object; it is not required to be a DMO.
items.evidence_quote: The source and target objects must be different objects.

items.stem: A security team wants to know what the Suggest Tags feature in Data 360 reads before it proposes governance tags. What does it examine?
options: Object and field metadata, such as their names
A sample of the values held in each field
The query history recorded against each object
The records already linked by identity resolution
answer: Object and field metadata, such as their names
items.rationale: Automatic tagging runs a large language model over metadata such as object and field names and explicitly does not access or analyze customer data, so no field values are sampled. The suggestions still need a steward or admin to approve them.
items.evidence_quote: In Data 360, the Suggest Tags feature uses a large language model (LLM) to look at information such as object and field names and suggests tags based on defined taxonomies. To ensure privacy, it doesn’t access or analyze customer data.

items.stem: When planning how many metrics to put in a single calculated insight view rather than splitting them across several views, what is the maximum number of measures one view can hold?
items.rationale: A calculated insight view is capped at 50 measures and 10 dimensions, which is why the guidance is to split metrics across several views grouped on the relevant object.
items.evidence_quote: Because you can only have a maximum of 50 measures and 10 dimensions, you can organize the view to have different views and group metrics together on the relevant object.

items.stem: A data model object in Data 360 shows a category on the Data Model tab, yet nobody ever chose one for it. Where does that category come from?
options: It is inherited from the first data lake object mapped to the DMO
It is selected by the admin when the DMO is created on the Data Model tab
It is taken from the category of the data space that contains the DMO
It is set by the first segment or activation that references the DMO
answer: It is inherited from the first data lake object mapped to the DMO
items.rationale: A DMO has no category of its own, so the first DLO mapped to it fixes the category, and only compatible DLO categories can be mapped afterwards. Nothing about data spaces, segments or activations assigns the category.
items.evidence_quote: Instead, a DMO inherits its category from the first data lake object (DLO) mapped to it.

items.stem: A modeller proposes a Data 360 formula field holding the number of days since each customer's first purchase. Why is that a poor use of a formula field?
options: The value is calculated once and stored, so it never moves on afterwards
Formulas can't reference date fields from the source schema
Formulas are evaluated on every query, so segments would run slowly
Formulas can't be referenced later at segmentation time
answer: The value is calculated once and stored, so it never moves on afterwards
items.rationale: A formula is a stored, row-based calculation performed as the data lands, not a run-time calculation, so a value that depends on today's date goes stale. It is not a performance problem: nothing is recomputed at query time.
items.evidence_quote: The calculation occurs only at ingestion time and is a stored calculation, not a run-time calculation.

items.stem: A related list enrichment surfaces engagement data on a Contact record page, and no date filter has been added to it. How many days of data does it return by default?
items.rationale: Engagement-based related list enrichments default to the last 7 days; a wider window needs a date filter on the enrichment or a dynamic list, and it costs latency.
items.evidence_quote: By default, related list enrichments that contain engagement data return data from the last 7 days.

items.stem: A design calls for a streaming insight and a real-time insight over engagement data. Which aggregate functions are available to them?
options: SUM
COUNT
AVG
MIN
MAX
MEAN
items.rationale: Streaming and real-time insights are restricted to SUM and COUNT; AVG, MIN, MAX and MEAN are aggregate functions available to batch calculated insights only, so an average has to be modelled elsewhere.
items.evidence_quote: Streaming and real-time insights support only the SUM and COUNT aggregate functions.

items.stem: A copy field enrichment is keeping fields on org records up to date with incremental syncs. A nightly job then changes well over 250,000 records for the fields being copied in one transaction. How does Data 360 handle that volume?
options: It replaces the incremental sync with a full sync, then returns to incremental syncing
It spreads the changes over several incremental syncs until the backlog clears
It stops the enrichment and reports an error in the Sync History tab
It skips the excess changes and counts them in the Records Excluded column
answer: It replaces the incremental sync with a full sync, then returns to incremental syncing
items.rationale: Above the change threshold a full sync is cheaper on latency than a very large incremental batch, so the system substitutes one and switches back afterwards. Records Excluded counts records that fail for other reasons, such as locked or orphaned data.
items.evidence_quote: If more than 250,000 data changes occur in a transaction after any filter conditions are applied for copy field enrichment, the incremental sync is replaced by a full sync. A full sync reduces latency in data syncs for large volumes of changes. After the full sync completes, the system switches to incremental sync again.

items.stem: A data graph is built on one foundation data model object, with other DMOs added around it as related objects. Name the object category that a DMO must not belong to if it is to serve as that foundation object, even though DMOs in it can be added as related objects.
items.rationale: The primary DMO of a data graph can be in any category except Engagement, with Profile the most common choice. Engagement DMOs are still allowed as related objects, so the restriction applies only to the foundation object.
items.evidence_quote: A primary DMO can belong to any category except Engagement, with the Profile category being the most common.

items.stem: A batch data transform joins two data lake objects on a customer identifier that two source systems both issue. What must be true of the DLO fields used in that join so the combined data is not duplicated or misread?
options: Each must have an associated key qualifier field
Each must be the primary key of its own object
Each must already be mapped to the same data model object
Each must be covered by a secondary index on its own object
answer: Each must have an associated key qualifier field
items.rationale: The join has to be on a fully qualified key, so every DLO field used in it needs a key qualifier; DMO fields get theirs automatically. Using a primary key column is only a performance suggestion, not a requirement.
items.evidence_quote: All data lake object (DLO) fields used in the data transform table join must have an associated key qualifier.

items.stem: An architect reviewing the Data 360 data model wants to get rid of a standard relationship between two DMOs that their design does not use. What can they actually do with it?
options: Disable it, but not remove it
Remove it permanently from the Relationships tab
Remove it, but only once the mappings on both of its fields are deleted
Neither: standard relationships can be neither turned off nor removed
answer: Disable it, but not remove it
items.rationale: A standard relationship ships with the data model and can only be disabled; permanent deletion is available for custom relationships, which are also auto-deleted when a field mapping is removed.
items.evidence_quote: You can disable a standard relationship, but you can’t delete it.

items.stem: A streaming data transform uses the UNION operator to split three phone-number columns into separate rows. Which conditions must every SELECT statement in that transform satisfy?
options: Reference the same source data lake object
Map to the same fields for the target DLO
Generate a unique value for the primary key field
Read from a different source data lake object
Write to a different target data lake object
Include a WHERE clause that filters out null values
answer: Reference the same source data lake object
Map to the same fields for the target DLO
Generate a unique value for the primary key field
items.rationale: Every SELECT in a UNION reads the same source DLO, shares one schema on the target DLO, and must produce a unique primary key value, otherwise one of the duplicate values is picked at random. Filtering nulls is only what the worked example happens to do.
items.evidence_quote: To use the `UNION` operator in a streaming data transform, each `SELECT` statement must: Reference the same source data lake object. In the example above, all three `SELECT` statements use the same source data lake object CRMContacts. Map to the same fields for the target DLO. Each `SELECT` statement must have the same schema. In our example, all three `SELECT` statements map to the same set of fields: `PhoneId`, `CustomerId`, `PhoneNumber`, and `PhoneType`. Generate a unique value for the primary key field.

items.stem: A team clones an existing data graph to produce a variant for a second use case. What are they able to change on the clone?
options: The related objects and fields, but not the data space or primary DMO
The primary DMO, but not the data space or the related objects
The data space, but not the primary DMO or the related objects
Only the name, API name and description
answer: The related objects and fields, but not the data space or primary DMO
items.rationale: A clone inherits the original's data space and primary DMO and those two are fixed, while the related objects, fields, filters and naming are all open for change. So cloning is only a shortcut for a variant built on the same foundation object in the same data space.
items.evidence_quote: You can’t change the data space or primary DMO, but you can select different related objects and fields.

items.stem: Cutting down the nodes that do the most processing is the biggest performance lever in a batch data transform. Which node types does Salesforce classify as the heavyweight ones?
options: Join
Aggregate
Compute Relative (multi-row formulas)
Output
Filter
Formula
Schema Change
items.rationale: Join, Aggregate, Compute Relative and Output are the nodes that need real processing, which is why filtering and narrowing the data before it reaches them is the recommended design. Filter, Schema Change and Formula run in memory and are cheap, so adding a filter node ahead of a join costs almost nothing.
items.evidence_quote: | Lightweight (in-memory, fast) | Heavyweight (more processing required) | | --- | --- | | Filter | Join | | Schema Change | Aggregate | | Formula | Compute Relative (multi-row formulas) | |   | Output |

items.stem: A lookup node in a batch data transform adds demographic attributes to opportunity records, and some opportunities have no matching record in the lookup source. What do the looked-up fields contain on those rows?
options: Dimensions are null and measures are 0
Both the dimensions and the measures are null
Both the dimensions and the measures are 0
The row is dropped from the output
answer: Dimensions are null and measures are 0
items.rationale: A lookup keeps every left row, filling unmatched dimensions with null and unmatched measures with zero. That asymmetry matters downstream: a zero from an unmatched row is indistinguishable from a real zero and will quietly drag averages and sums.
items.evidence_quote: Unmatched dimensions are set to null. Unmatched measures are set to 0.

items.stem: A streaming data transform has been running in production for a month, and its SQL now has to bring through an extra column. How does Data 360 let that change be made?
options: Delete the transform and create another one
Edit the SQL and save the transform again
Pause the transform, edit the SQL, then resume it
Clone the transform, edit the clone, then repoint the target object
answer: Delete the transform and create another one
items.rationale: A streaming data transform is immutable once saved, so any change means replacing it, which is worth designing for because the replacement re-reads the source before it starts writing again. There is no edit, pause-and-edit or clone-and-edit path.
items.evidence_quote: You can’t change a streaming data transform after saving it. If you must change your streaming data transform, delete it and create another one.

items.stem: When batch data transforms are built in Tableau Next, at most how many transform definitions can be combined into one batch transform?
items.rationale: Tableau Next caps a batch transform at five combined transform definitions, so a pipeline that needs more has to be split across several transforms run in sequence.
items.evidence_quote: You can have up to five transform definitions combined for one batch transform.

items.stem: A calculated insight in Data 360 is rejected because its SELECT clause lists only customer IDs and order dates, with no aggregation function anywhere in the statement. Which of the SQL rules for insights does it break?
options: Every query must contain at least one measure
Every query must contain at least one nested subquery
Every query must give each selected field an alias
Every query must include a TRY_CONVERT_CURRENCY call
answer: Every query must contain at least one measure
items.rationale: A measure is any field wrapped in an aggregation function, and an insight query has to have at least one, so a purely descriptive SELECT is not a valid insight. Subqueries are optional, aliasing is only constrained for dimensions, and TRY_CONVERT_CURRENCY is required only when a currency field is involved.
items.evidence_quote: A query must contain at least one measure. A measure is any field wrapped in an aggregation function.

items.stem: Data 360 syncs conversion rates for US dollars and euros from one connected CRM org, and rates for Japanese yen and Indian rupees from a second connected CRM org. Data 360 can convert a US dollar amount into Japanese yen from those synced rates.
items.rationale: Conversions are not supported across different connected CRM orgs, so the fix is to add the missing currency rates to each org rather than relying on the union of what has been synced. Ignoring this produces null values in the converted fields.
items.evidence_quote: Data Cloud doesn’t support currency conversions across different CRM orgs connected to it.

items.stem: Salesforce recommends starting small when designing a custom governance taxonomy in Data 360. Put the steps of that recommended approach into the order Salesforce recommends.
options: Begin with a small set of parent tags and a few child tags
Test the taxonomy by tagging a sample set of Data 360 objects
Collect feedback from users and refine the structure before expanding it further
answer: Begin with a small set of parent tags and a few child tags
Test the taxonomy by tagging a sample set of Data 360 objects
Collect feedback from users and refine the structure before expanding it further
items.rationale: The taxonomy is built out only after a small version has been applied to real objects and reviewed by the people who will use it, which is what keeps the tag names usable and the later policy enforcement accurate.
items.evidence_quote: Begin with a small set of parent tags and a few child tags. Test the taxonomy by tagging a sample set of Data 360 objects. Collect feedback from users and refine the structure before expanding it further.

items.stem: In the Customer 360 Data Model, the word "party" names a subject area, a DMO, and two fields. Pair each of them with what it actually is.
options: Party Subject Area
Party Identification DMO
Party Identification ID
Party

pairs.right: A grouping of DMOs related to a contact's data
The object that data stream data is mapped to, holding identifiers such as a driver's license
The field used as the primary key and unique identifier of a contact
The field whose reference ID is used as a foreign key, and that also appears in the Individual DMO

answer: Party Subject Area::A grouping of DMOs related to a contact's data
Party Identification DMO::The object that data stream data is mapped to, holding identifiers such as a driver's license
Party Identification ID::The field used as the primary key and unique identifier of a contact
Party::The field whose reference ID is used as a foreign key, and that also appears in the Individual DMO
items.rationale: Each name sits at a different level: the subject area organises DMOs, the Party Identification DMO is the mapping target, its Party Identification ID field is the primary key, and the Party field is the foreign key that the Individual DMO also carries. Treating Party and Party Identification ID as the same field is the mistake that breaks a mapping design.
items.evidence_quote:
| Party Subject Area | The party subject area is a grouping of DMOs related to a contact’s data. | A subject area helps organize similar DMOs in a data model. |
| Party Identification DMO | A DMO that contains multiple fields about a contact, including identifiers and unique numbers, like a driver’s license. | Data stream data is mapped to this DMO. |
| Party Identification ID | A field in the Party Identification DMO. | This field is used as a primary key and the unique identifier of a contact. |
| Party | A field in the Party Identification DMO. | This reference ID is used as a foreign key. It’s also used in the Individual DMO. |

items.stem: A streaming data transform in Data 360 augments an event stream by chaining several INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN clauses together. At most how many objects can one SQL statement join?
items.rationale: One streaming transform SQL statement can combine at most 5 objects, so a design that needs more enrichment than that has to be split across transforms or handled upstream.
items.evidence_quote: Multiple joins can be combined using additional `INNER JOIN` or `LEFT JOIN` clauses. Up to 5 objects can be joined in one SQL statement.

items.stem: During field mapping in Data 360, a DLO field named subscriber key is offered a mapping to a DMO field named Individual ID the first time that pair is seen in the org, even though the two names share no words and are not close in spelling. Which automapping consideration produced that suggestion?
options: Synonyms
Fuzzy match
Standardized match
Historical data
items.rationale: Automapping includes common synonyms of DLO field names in its comparisons, which is how names with no shared characters can still be matched. Fuzzy and standardized matching are both string comparison techniques and need the names to resemble each other, and historical data only helps once that pair has been mapped before.
items.evidence_quote: Synonyms - Common synonyms of DLO field names are included in comparisons. For example when suggesting mappings for a DLO field `subscriber key`, its synonym `Individual ID` is also considered to compare and map.

items.stem: Row-level security policies are already defined on several data model objects, and a data graph projects fields from those same objects. How does Data 360 decide which users can read that data graph?
options: Exclusively through tag-based controls on the projected fields
By applying the DMO-level row-level security policies to the data graph at query time
By re-evaluating the row-level security policies each time the data graph refreshes
By the data space that the data graph's primary data model object belongs to
answer: Exclusively through tag-based controls on the projected fields
items.rationale: Data graphs do not inherit DMO row-level security at all; access is enforced only through the tags copied onto the projected fields from the participating DMOs and calculated insight objects. A design that assumes RLS carries into a data graph will leak rows, so tag propagation has to be planned deliberately.
items.evidence_quote: DMO-level RLS policies aren’t applied to data graphs. Data graphs enforce access exclusively through tag-based controls on projected fields.

items.stem: A data graph in Data 360 was created with a scheduled refresh. That data graph can later be switched to a streaming refresh from the data graph's properties.
items.rationale: The refresh interval can be changed at any time, but the refresh type cannot: moving between streaming and scheduled means building a new data graph with the required configuration, so the choice has to be made when the graph is designed.
items.evidence_quote: After a data graph is created, you can’t change the refresh type between streaming and scheduled. To use a different refresh type, create a new data graph with the required configuration.

items.stem: A batch data transform takes data lake objects as its inputs. The preview looks correct because the data space selected on the input nodes filters out a region the team does not want. What happens to those filtered-out records when the transform is actually run?
options: They are processed, because data space filters don't apply at run time
They are excluded, because the same filter is reapplied at run time
They are excluded, because the transform reuses the data space chosen for preview
They are processed only when the output object belongs to a different data space
answer: They are processed, because data space filters don't apply at run time
items.rationale: A DLO transform processes every record in its input DLOs at run time, so a preview filtered by a data space is misleading about what the run will produce. To control what downstream users see, the output DLO has to be added to a data space or a filter node added before the output. DMO transforms behave differently, applying the transform's data space filters at run time.
items.evidence_quote: When a DLO transform runs, it processes all records in the input DLOs—data space filters don't apply at run time.

items.stem: The dropdown next to a calculated insight in the Data 360 Calculated Insights list view offers several run-related actions. Pair each action with what it does.
options: Update Stats
Publish Now
Track History
Schedule

pairs.right: Refresh the status, last run time, last run status and last modified date shown for the insight
Run the insight immediately instead of waiting for its batch schedule
Capture the insight's values at a point in time and append them to the history tracking object
Change how often the insight is processed

answer: Update Stats::Refresh the status, last run time, last run status and last modified date shown for the insight
Publish Now::Run the insight immediately instead of waiting for its batch schedule
Track History::Capture the insight's values at a point in time and append them to the history tracking object
Schedule::Change how often the insight is processed
items.rationale: The four actions are easily confused because all four touch running the insight. Update Stats only refreshes the metadata shown in the list, Publish Now forces an immediate run, Schedule changes the processing cadence, and Track History is the only one that keeps a point-in-time copy of the values in a separate history tracking object.
items.evidence_quote: | Update Stats | Update the status, last run time, last run status, and last modified date of the selected calculated insight. | | Publish Now | Run a calculated insight immediately instead of processing it as a batch schedule. | | Track History | Captures data at a specific time and appends the calculated insight object values to the history tracking object. | | Schedule | Modify the processing schedule of a calculated insight. |

rows: Change the calculated insight name and field names.
Duplicate and edit the SQL function from this record.
Turn processing on or off for a calculated insight.
View calculated insight logic in the builder. Available only for calculated insights created with the builder.
Permanently remove a calculated insight and its connections.
Update the status, last run time, last run status, and last modified date of the selected calculated insight.
Run a calculated insight immediately instead of processing it as a batch schedule.
Modify the processing schedule of a calculated insight.

items.stem: Two source fields in a data lake object both hold a customer's email address. In Data 360 field mapping, both DLO fields can be mapped into the same DMO field so that whichever one has a value populates it.
items.rationale: A DMO field can have only one source DLO field, so two DLO fields cannot feed it. The relationship is one-way: a single DLO field may be mapped to more than one DMO field in the same DMO, but not the reverse.
items.evidence_quote: You can map only one DLO field to a DMO field. A single DMO field can't have more than one source DLO field

items.stem: A segment includes an Engagement DMO and filters on its event date field. At most how much history from that event date field can the segment process before it fails?
items.rationale: An Engagement DMO in a segment can be processed over a window of up to 24 months of the event date field; a wider date range makes the segment fail, so long-range engagement analysis has to be designed around that ceiling.
items.evidence_quote: When an Engagement DMO is included in a segment, the segment can process the data records up to 24 months of the event date field.

items.stem: A formula in a batch data transform is being typed by hand. It has to reference a field whose name is one of the reserved keywords and compare that field with the text value New. Which quoting does Data 360 expect?
options: Double quotes around the field name and single quotes around the text value
Single quotes around the field name and double quotes around the text value
Double quotes around both the field name and the text value
Single quotes around both the field name and the text value
answer: Double quotes around the field name and single quotes around the text value
items.rationale: Single quotes mark string literals, and double quotes mark field names that collide with a reserved keyword or that use dot notation after a join. Swapping them makes the parser read the keyword as text and the literal as a field.
items.evidence_quote: If you manually type your formulas, use single quotes ' for string literals and double quotes " for joined fields with dot notation or reserved keywords.

items.stem: History tracking in Data 360 keeps a point-in-time record of an insight's values so the metric can be trended. Which insight types can it be turned on for?
options: Calculated insights only
Calculated and streaming insights
Calculated and real-time insights
Streaming and real-time insights
items.rationale: History tracking is available for calculated insights and for nothing else - the page rules out streaming and real-time insights explicitly - so a design that needs a trend of a streaming metric has to persist it another way.
items.evidence_quote: History tracking is only available for calculated insights.

items.stem: A related attributes personalization use case is delivered partly in Data 360 and partly in Marketing Cloud Engagement. Put the three steps completed in Data 360 into the order the workflow performs them.
options: Create an audience segment
Activate the segment and add attributes
Filter attributes and publish to Marketing Cloud Engagement
answer: Activate the segment and add attributes
Filter attributes and publish to Marketing Cloud Engagement
items.rationale: The segment is built first, attributes are added to it as part of activation, and only then are the attributes filtered and published so that Marketing Cloud Engagement can find the audience in a data extension.
items.evidence_quote: Create an audience segment. Activate the segment and add attributes Filter attributes and publish to Marketing Cloud Engagement

items.stem: Delete Object is used on a standard data model object that has no downstream dependencies. What becomes of that object?
options: It goes inactive and comes back automatically once a field is mapped to it again
It is removed from the org permanently along with its field mappings
It stays active and keeps its field mappings until an admin confirms the deletion
It is turned into a custom data model object so that it can be deleted
answer: It goes inactive and comes back automatically once a field is mapped to it again
items.rationale: Only custom DMOs are fully deleted. A standard DMO is put into an inactive state, still exists in the system, and reactivates by itself as soon as a field is re-mapped to it.
items.evidence_quote: While custom objects are fully deleted, standard objects are placed in an inactive state. Inactive standard objects continue to exist in the system and automatically reactivate after a field is re-mapped to them.

items.stem: Data 360 combines three access control layers for governance. Pair each layer with what it controls.
options: Data Spaces
Role-based Access Control (RBAC)
Attribute-based Access Control (ABAC)

pairs.right: The visibility scope: which data objects or records a user can interact with, with no fine-grained or row-level control
Base access to features and setup: navigation, admin tasks and configuration rights
Policy-driven access by context: object-level, field-level, row-level and masking rules

answer: Data Spaces::The visibility scope: which data objects or records a user can interact with, with no fine-grained or row-level control
Role-based Access Control (RBAC)::Base access to features and setup: navigation, admin tasks and configuration rights
Attribute-based Access Control (ABAC)::Policy-driven access by context: object-level, field-level, row-level and masking rules
items.rationale: Data spaces bound what is visible but cannot express row-level rules, RBAC grants the base ability to navigate and configure, and only ABAC policies deliver object, field, row and masking control. Assuming a data space assignment alone secures data is the classic mistake.
items.evidence_quote:
| Data Spaces | Data visibility scope | Controls which data objects or records a user can interact with. It can be used to grant access to a set of objects but doesn’t support fine-grained or row-level control. |
| Role-based Access Control (RBAC) | Base access to features and setup | Navigation, admin tasks, configuration rights, and access assignment to specific objects within the dataspace. |
| Attribute-based Access Control (ABAC) | Policy-driven access based on context | Object-level, field-level, row-level, and masking rules |

rows: Controls which data objects or records a user can interact with. It can be used to grant access to a set of objects but doesn’t support fine-grained or row-level control.
Base access to features and setup
Navigation, admin tasks, configuration rights, and access assignment to specific objects within the dataspace.
Object-level, field-level, row-level, and masking rules

items.stem: For a scheduled batch data transform to qualify for an incremental run rather than a full run, updates to the input data must stay below what proportion of the total amount of data?
items.unit: percent of the total amount of data
items.rationale: Below 5% of the total data changing, a scheduled transform can run incrementally; above that it falls back to a full run that reprocesses new and existing data. This is the figure that decides whether a large nightly transform stays cheap.
items.evidence_quote: Updates to input data are less than 5% of the total amount of data.

items.stem: An object in Data 360 carries the preconfigured ExternalData.Visibility.Portal tag. Which population does that classification make the object eligible for?
options: Authenticated external users only
Unidentified and authenticated external users
Any user holding the Data 360 User permission set
Internal users only, until an allow policy is added
items.rationale: The Portal tag maps to the Access Level.Portal classification, which is restricted to authenticated external users; it is the Public tag that also opens an object to unidentified external users. The Data 360 User permission set is for internal users and is not how external access is granted.
items.evidence_quote: | Authenticated External Users only | `ExternalData.Visibility.Portal` | `Data Categorization.Access Level.Portal`: Restricted to authenticated external users. |

rows: `Data Categorization.Access Level.Public`: The most permissive level.
`Data Categorization.Access Level.Portal`: Restricted to authenticated external users.

items.stem: A consultant defines a secondary index on a large data lake object so that filters on a non-primary field run faster. What does Data 360 actually build in the org to provide that index?
options: A batch data transform on the object that adds the specified field as the new index
A calculated insight that pre-aggregates the specified field on a schedule
A data graph that caches the specified field as a queryable JSON blob
A streaming insight that maintains the specified field in near real time
answer: A batch data transform on the object that adds the specified field as the new index
items.rationale: Secondary indexes are implemented as a batch data transform over the DLO or materialized DMO, which is also why they are refreshed on a batch cadence rather than instantly. Calculated and streaming insights produce aggregate objects, and data graphs pre-join related records; neither reindexes the base object.
items.evidence_quote: In Data 360, a secondary index is a batch data transform on the provided DLO or materialized DMO that adds the specified field as the new index.

items.stem: Select the object types that a Data 360 secondary index cannot be created on.
options: Zero-Copy Data 360 objects
Unstructured DLOs
Engagement category DLOs
Materialized DMOs of the Derived type
Materialized DMOs of the Bridge type
items.rationale: Zero-copy objects and unstructured DLOs are explicitly out of scope for secondary indexes. Engagement DLOs are in fact one of the best fits, and Derived and Bridge DMOs are materialized types that do support indexing.
items.evidence_quote: Secondary indexes don’t support Zero-Copy Data 360 objects or unstructured DLOs.

items.stem: When you map data lake object fields onto a data model object, the field data types have to line up. Which of these DLO-to-DMO field mappings does Data 360 allow?
options: A Number DLO field mapped to a Text DMO field
A Text DLO field mapped to a Number DMO field
A Boolean DLO field mapped to a Text DMO field
A Currency DLO field mapped to a Number DMO field
answer: A Number DLO field mapped to a Text DMO field
items.rationale: Number into Text is the documented exception to the rule that a DLO field and the DMO field it maps to share a data type, which is why an identifier landed as a number can still be mapped to a text key field. The exception runs one way only, so Text into Number is refused, and Boolean and Currency fields have to be mapped onto fields of their own type.
items.evidence_quote: When mapping a data lake object (DLO) to a data model object (DMO), the data type of the DLO field must match the data type of the DMO field. The only exception is that DLO fields with the Number data type can be mapped to DMO fields with the Text data type.

items.stem: A data stream sourced through a Salesforce connector needs formula fields. Which Formula Return Type data types will the Salesforce connectors and Connector services not support?
options: Email
Percent
Phone
Boolean
URL
Text
Number
Date
items.rationale: Five of the nine Formula Return Type options are unsupported for the Salesforce connectors and Connector services, which leaves a formula on a CRM-sourced stream with Text, Number and Date. A true or false flag therefore has to be produced as text or a number and interpreted downstream.
items.evidence_quote: The Salesforce connectors and Connector services don't support these data types: Email, Percent, Phone, Boolean, and URL for the Formula Return Type.

items.stem: An author building a real-time insight in Visual Insight Builder wants to combine two objects with an inner join. What is possible?
options: Join nodes aren't available for real-time insights at all
Only left joins are available for real-time insights
Join nodes are available for real-time insights but not for streaming insights
All four join types are available for real-time insights
answer: Join nodes aren't available for real-time insights at all
items.rationale: Left, right, inner and full joins are all supported for calculated and streaming insights and none of them for real-time insights, so a real-time insight has to take its combined data from the real-time data graph it is built on rather than from a Join node. Streaming insights, by contrast, do support every join type.
items.evidence_quote:
| Node | Function | **Calculated Insights** | **Streaming Insights** | **Real Time Insights** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Using the Join Node | Left Join | Yes | Yes | No |
| Right Join | Yes | Yes | No |
| Inner | Yes | Yes | No |
| Full | Yes | Yes | No |

For example, Average returns the average value of a numerical column. You can use dimensions to roll up the records to a higher granularity. Dimensions, which are typically textual, categorize and describe data by supplying qualitative data points. They are commonly used to filter and segment data based on specific characteristics, such as customer ID, product type, location, or date. If none of the WHEN conditions are met, the ELSE statement provides an alternative action. The Case node statement must be followed by at least one WHEN/THEN pair, which applies a designated function when the associated condition is true.")

items.stem: Automatic content tagging is switched on for unstructured data lake objects in Data 360, and the content in one object has grown past the documented 5 GB per-object ceiling. What is the stated consequence of rebuilding that object's search index?
options: Every existing tag is removed, so data that was protected is left unprotected
Tags below the confidence threshold are removed and approved tags are kept
The rebuild is blocked until the object is split into smaller objects
Existing tags are kept and only the content above the ceiling stays untagged
answer: Every existing tag is removed, so data that was protected is left unprotected
items.rationale: Past the per-object ceiling a rebuild wipes the tags, and because masking and access policies are driven by tags, the data they protected silently becomes visible. The documented remedy is to split the content into several objects with their own search indexes before that point, not to rely on the rebuild refusing to run.
items.evidence_quote: When the total size exceeds 5 GB, rebuilding the search index removes all existing tags, leaving previously protected data unprotected.

items.stem: A filter node is added to a batch data transform in Data 360 and the author picks the values to keep from the list of values the node offers for that column. That list covers every value the column holds across the full dataset.
items.rationale: The picklist is built from the preview, which is only a sample, so a value that exists in the full dataset but did not appear in the preview is simply absent from the list. Rows the author meant to keep are then filtered out, and the fix is to add the value manually rather than trust the list.
items.evidence_quote: When adding a filter node, the picklist displays only the values present in the preview dataset. Values that exist in your full dataset but weren't included in the preview won't appear as filter options.

items.stem: An existing calculated insight in Data 360 is reopened so its measures can be reworked. Which changes to the measures does Data 360 permit?
options: Add another aggregatable measure to an aggregatable insight
Add any measure to a non-aggregatable insight
Change the API name of an existing measure
Change the data type of an existing measure
Change the rollup behavior of an existing measure
Remove a measure that is no longer wanted
answer: Add another aggregatable measure to an aggregatable insight
Add any measure to a non-aggregatable insight
items.rationale: Editing an insight is additive only, and even then an aggregatable insight will only take further aggregatable measures. API name, data type and rollup behavior are fixed once created and existing measures can't be removed, so a measure that was defined wrongly means building a replacement insight rather than correcting this one.
items.evidence_quote: Measures | - You can’t change the API name, data type, or rollup behavior. - You can add only aggregatable measures to an aggregatable insight. - You can add any measure to a non-aggregatable insight. - You can’t remove existing measures.

items.stem: When you preview the results of a node while building a batch data transform in Data 360, the preview shows a sample of the latest available data. At most how many rows does that sample contain?
items.rationale: A preview samples up to 5,000 rows, so a preview that looks complete is not proof that the full run will behave the same way on a large object. The separate 4,000 figure is the number of previews a user can start per hour.
items.evidence_quote: The preview shows a sample of the latest available data, up to 5,000 rows.

items.stem: One Data 360 org shares a calculated insight object with a second Data 360 org through a data share. What form does the shared object take in the receiving org?
options: A data lake object
A calculated insight object
A data model object
A read-only data stream
items.rationale: Whatever the source object type, a data share lands in the target org as a DLO, so the receiving org has to map and model it again rather than inheriting the original object type.
items.evidence_quote: Regardless of the type of Data 360 object shared by the source org, it is modelled as a DLO in the target Data Cloud org.

items.stem: A field in a running Data 360 data stream was given the wrong data type when the source schema was reviewed. What does correcting that field's data type require?
options: Deleting the data stream and creating it again
Editing the data type on the data stream's schema and refreshing the stream
Adding a formula field of the correct type and disabling the original field
Changing the data type on the mapped data model object field
answer: Deleting the data stream and creating it again
items.rationale: A data type can't be changed once the data stream exists, so the only remedy is to drop and rebuild the stream. Editing the schema afterwards allows fields to be added, updated or disabled, but not retyped, and changing the DMO field does not alter the ingested type.
items.evidence_quote: If you select the wrong data type, you must delete the data stream and re-create it. You can’t change a data type after the data stream is created.

items.stem: To move a data model object to a different category, an engineer deletes every field mapping into it. The DMO goes inactive. What object category does it now show, before it is remapped to a data lake object of the new category?
items.rationale: Deleting the mappings strips the inherited category, leaving the DMO inactive with its object category set to UNASSIGNED until a new DLO mapping gives it a category again.
items.evidence_quote: The DMO becomes inactive with the object category set to UNASSIGNED.

items.stem: An Engagement data stream is set up with Updated Date, a field that changes every time the source record is touched, as its Event Time Field. What goes wrong in the data lake object?
options: Several rows with the same primary key are added, so records are duplicated
Only the newest version of each record is kept, so earlier history is lost
The stream fails validation and can't be saved until a different field is chosen
The records land correctly but are excluded from segmentation until remapped
answer: Several rows with the same primary key are added, so records are duplicated
items.rationale: A mutable event time makes each change look like a new event, so multiple rows sharing one primary key accumulate. Data 360 does not reject the stream or de-duplicate it, which is why the Event Time Field must be immutable and can't be edited after setup.
items.evidence_quote: Using a mutable date field causes duplication of records where multiple records with the same primary key get added to the data lake object (DLO).

items.stem: Salesforce's usual "most restricted access wins" security policy decides which records inside a selected data space a user sees in a related list enrichment.
items.rationale: For related list enrichments, everything in the selected data space is accessible regardless of further Data 360 restrictions, so the most-restrictive rule does not apply. Narrowing what is shown means building a dynamic related list filtered on the data space.
items.evidence_quote: For data spaces, the standard Salesforce security policy of “most restricted access wins” doesn’t apply to the data shown in related list enrichments.

items.stem: A formula in a batch data transform buckets opportunities by week using date_trunc('week',CloseDate). What value does that expression return?
options: The Monday of the week that contains the Close Date
The Sunday of the week that contains the Close Date
The first day of the month that contains the Close Date
The Close Date with its time portion reset to 00:00:00
answer: The Monday of the week that contains the Close Date
items.rationale: date_trunc resets the specified part of the timestamp and everything after it, and for 'week' the week is treated as starting on Monday, so weekly buckets are labelled with Monday dates rather than Sunday ones.
items.evidence_quote: date_trunc('week',CloseDate) returns the Monday of the week of the Close Date.

items.stem: A join node on the batch data transform canvas is matching contact records to lead records, and a single name key is producing duplicate matches. At most how many keys should be used to match records in that join?
items.rationale: Adding a second or third key, such as company alongside name, removes the ambiguity, but the guidance caps the join at five match keys; one of them should be a primary key column for performance.
items.evidence_quote: To improve results, use up to five keys to match records.

items.stem: When building a new real-time data graph, a DMO can be added as a related object even when doing so creates an N:1 relationship with an object already in the graph.
items.rationale: New real-time data graphs reject N:1 relationships and the system blocks the selection outright. Only real-time data graphs created before the restriction keep running with N:1 relationships in them.
items.evidence_quote: Note New real-time data graphs don’t support N:1 relationships between DMOs.

items.stem: An append node combines two objects in a batch data transform. A numeric column exists in only one of them, and null numeric handling is not switched on. What does the append node put in that column for the rows coming from the object that lacks it?
options: Zeroes
Nulls
Empty strings
The column's default value
items.rationale: Unmapped columns are filled with null in general, but an unmapped numeric column gets zeroes unless null numeric handling is enabled, which silently understates averages computed over the appended result. Turning null numeric handling on is what keeps those rows null.
items.evidence_quote: If a numeric column isn’t mapped to a source and null numeric handling isn’t enabled, the append node inserts zeroes instead of nulls for those source rows.

items.stem: Salesforce publishes recommended maximums for a single batch data transform, above which it advises extra performance testing. How many join nodes is the recommended maximum for one transform?
items.rationale: Twenty-five join nodes is the published guideline for one transform, alongside 150 total nodes and 5 output nodes. It is a recommendation rather than a hard cap, so a design that exceeds it should be tested at production scale in a sandbox or split into transforms that run in sequence.
items.evidence_quote: | Element | Recommended maximum | | --- | --- | | Join nodes | 25 |
