150 (transforms above this take longer to preview and run)

items.stem: Salesforce Support handles support cases for the Tableau accelerators for Data 360 that are published on Tableau Exchange and Salesforce AppExchange.
items.rationale: The accelerators are ready-made dashboards that connect Tableau to Data 360 through the Salesforce Data Cloud connector, but they sit outside the supported product: issues go to the Tableau Account Team, who raise them with the Tableau Accelerator Team. A client planning to build on one should know that before it becomes production reporting.
items.evidence_quote: Salesforce Support doesn't support the Tableau accelerators for Data 360 available on Tableau Exchange and Salesforce AppExchange.

items.stem: An org has set fiscal_year_start_month and first_day_of_fiscal_week for its Data 360 queries, and now wants to add a lookup table that maps each day to its own fiscal period so it can model a 4-4-5 calendar. What does Data 360 allow?
options: One approach only, because the standard options and the custom table can't be combined
Both, as long as the custom table is registered before the standard options are set
Both, with the custom table taking precedence wherever the two disagree
Both, but only if the custom table covers periods the standard options leave undefined
answer: One approach only, because the standard options and the custom table can't be combined
items.rationale: Mixing the standard fiscal options with the fiscal_period_table causes configuration errors, so a client with an irregular calendar has to abandon the standard settings entirely and drive everything from the lookup table. There is no precedence or fallback behaviour to rely on.
items.evidence_quote: Choose either the standard options or the custom table approach. You can’t combine both methods, as this causes configuration errors.

items.stem: A batch data transform flattens nested JSON using an uploaded JSON schema file. Select every keyword in that file that Data 360 actually reads.
options: type
properties
items
required
title
description
items.rationale: Only type, properties and items are interpreted; everything else in the schema file, including the required list that a generated schema normally carries, is ignored. So a schema cannot be relied on to enforce anything beyond structure and data type.
items.evidence_quote: Only the 'type', 'properties', and 'items' keywords are recognized from the schema file; all others are ignored.

items.stem: A root key used by Data 360 has been deactivated in the external key manager, and the customer wants to know how long they have to put it back before the situation becomes unrecoverable. Within how many hours must the key be reactivated to avoid data loss?
items.rationale: The reactivation window is 48 hours; past that, the data encrypted with the key is lost rather than merely inaccessible. Email notification arrives before Data 360 processes start failing, which can make the window feel longer than it is.
items.evidence_quote: Reactivate the key within 48 hours to avoid data loss in Data 360.

items.stem: A data stream is deployed through the Salesforce CRM connector from a standard object. A standard Boolean field on that object arrives in Data 360 with which data type?
options: Text
Boolean
Number
Date
items.rationale: The connector maps a standard Boolean field on a standard object to Text, not Boolean, so downstream filters and formulas have to compare strings rather than true/false. Custom Boolean fields, on standard or custom objects, do come through as Boolean, which is why the inconsistency catches teams out.
items.evidence_quote: Mapping for the Boolean object when deploying a data stream and when creating a data stream using a starter bundle. | Object | Field | Mapping | | --- | --- | --- | | Standard Object | Standard Boolean Field | Text |

items.stem: A batch data transform has to pair every row of a product object with every row of a store object. Which constraints does Data 360 place on the cross join that does it?
options: Only one cross join is allowed per data transform
Cross join results are limited to a maximum of 10 million
Multivalue fields aren't supported
Both input objects are limited to a maximum of 100,000 rows
The cross join must be the last node before the output node
Only data model objects can be used as the inputs to a cross join
answer: Only one cross join is allowed per data transform
Cross join results are limited to a maximum of 10 million
items.rationale: Because the output is larger than either input, a cross join is capped at one per transform, at 10 million results, and cannot take multivalue fields. The row caps are not the same on both sides - the left object is capped at 100,000 rows and the right at 1,000, which is why the guidance is to put the larger object on the left. Nothing restricts where the node sits or requires DMO inputs.
items.evidence_quote:
-   Only one cross join per data transform
-   Cross join results maximum of 10 million
-   Left object field (column) maximum of 8 and row maximum of 100,000
-   Right object field (column) maximum of 8 and row maximum of 1,000
-   Doesn’t support multivalue fields

items.stem: A very wide source object is added to an input node in a batch data transform, and the author notices that not every column appears in the preview. By default, how many columns of each source object in an input node does the preview show?
items.rationale: The preview shows the first 100 columns of each source object in an input node by default, which is why a wide object looks truncated even though nothing has been removed from the transform. Hiding further columns is a performance measure, not a change to the transform's output.
items.evidence_quote: By default, the first 100 columns of each source object in an input node are shown in preview.

items.stem: A data graph must include related records that meet either one condition or another, so its author writes the two conditions into the Conditions section joined by OR. Data 360 evaluates that filter as written.
items.rationale: Filter conditions in a data graph are evaluated with AND logic only, so every condition has to be satisfied. An either/or requirement needs a different design, such as separate data graphs or a filter on a prepared field.
items.evidence_quote: Filter conditions in data graphs are evaluated using AND logic only.

items.stem: How deep a hierarchy the flatten transformation can handle in a batch data transform depends on how many rows the source contains. Pair each source size with the number of hierarchical levels it allows.
options: Over 1 million rows
15 million rows
20 million rows

pairs.right: 300 levels
100 levels
50 levels

items.rationale: The depth available falls as the source grows: 300 levels over a million rows, 100 at 15 million and 50 at 20 million, which is also the largest source the transformation will flatten.
items.evidence_quote: 300 levels for over 1 million rows 100 levels for 15 million rows 50 levels for 20 million rows (the maximum)

items.stem: A data access policy is being written in Data 360 Policy Builder with Field selected as the resource to protect. Which action can the rule take?
options: Deny access only
Allow access only
Either allow or deny access
Deny access, then allow it for named users
items.rationale: The action dropdown offers both allow and deny, but a field-level security policy supports deny only, so field policies subtract access from users who would otherwise have it rather than granting it.
items.evidence_quote: Only Deny access is supported in a field-level security (FLS) policy.

items.stem: In a batch data transform, a consultant wants to test whether a product code finishes with a particular suffix using the endsWith string function. What restricts where that function can be used?
options: It can be used only inside a case function
It can be used only when Multiple row formula is enabled
It can be used only when the column is referenced in double quotes
It can be used only in a Filter node, not in a Transform node
answer: It can be used only inside a case function
items.rationale: endsWith, like startsWith, returns True or False and is only permitted within a case function, so the test has to be wrapped in case logic. Multiple row formula is what exposes window functions, and double quotes are a naming rule for reserved keywords, neither of which limits this function.
items.evidence_quote: | `endsWith` | Returns True if the specified string is found at the end of the field value. You can use this function only in `case` functions. |

items.stem: A Formula transformation in a batch data transform outputs a text column and the Length attribute is left as it comes. How many characters will that column hold?
items.rationale: The Length attribute of a text output column defaults to 255 characters even though it can be set anywhere from 1 to 32000, so an author whose formula produces longer strings has to raise it from the default when defining the column.
items.evidence_quote: The maximum number of characters in a text column. Enter an integer from 1 through 32000, inclusive. The default length is 255 characters.

items.stem: A batch data transform has Replace selected for the output Write Mode and meets the criteria to run incrementally. On that run, every record in the output object is replaced.
items.rationale: Selecting Replace only makes Data 360 attempt an incremental run; when the transform does run incrementally it upserts or deletes just the changed records and merges them into the output node. A wholesale replacement happens only when the transform falls back to a full run.
items.evidence_quote: When the transform runs in incremental mode, it upserts or deletes only the changes records, it doesn’t replace them.

items.stem: A client asks what the C360 Semantic Model is for. Which answer describes the problem it is built to solve?
options: Fragmented data and metrics, by offering one model that acts as a primary map across the clouds
Duplicate customer records, by resolving them into unified profiles
Slow dashboard queries, by materializing aggregates as calculated insights
Inconsistent field access, by centralizing Field-Level Security policies
answer: Fragmented data and metrics, by offering one model that acts as a primary map across the clouds
items.rationale: The C360 Semantic Model is a shipped, extensible model giving consistent cross-cloud metrics; de-duplicating customer records is identity resolution, a different Data 360 feature.
items.evidence_quote: The C360 Semantic Model, powered by Data 360, solves the problem of fragmented data and metrics by offering a single model that acts as a "primary map" for your data.

items.stem: In Tableau Semantics you define a field with a formula that sorts each account into the categories Enterprise, Mid-market or SMB. What kind of field have you created?
options: A calculated dimension
A calculated measure
A metric
A numeric bin
items.rationale: Calculated dimensions are the qualitative, categorical fields used to group and classify data; a calculated measure would be a quantitative field that gets aggregated, and a bin only divides a numeric field into equal-sized intervals.
items.evidence_quote: Calculated dimensions are qualitative, categorical fields used to group, classify, and segment data.

items.stem: Tableau Semantics automatically generates a measure that counts the records in a data object and re-adjusts when filters or dimensions change, so an analyst can check that no data was lost after a change. What is this measure called?
items.rationale: The row count measure is generated automatically for a data object and can be reused inside calculated fields; it is not something the modeller has to define with a COUNT formula. It is not available in semantic models created from a Tableau Cloud Published Data Source.
items.evidence_quote: Use the auto-generated row count measure to track the number of records in a data object.

items.stem: A Tableau Plus customer wants to start modelling in Tableau Semantics. Which entitlement do they need for that?
options: The TableauEinsteinPlatform license
The Tableau Next license
The Service Insights App license
The Data Cloud Architect permission set
items.rationale: Data 360 customers get Tableau Semantics with every Data 360 edition, but Tableau Plus customers need the TableauEinsteinPlatform license; the Data Cloud Architect permission set governs what a user may do once the org is licensed, not whether the product is available.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Plus customers need the TableauEinsteinPlatform license to use Tableau Semantics.

items.stem: In the Tableau Semantics VS Code extension, what does the Extend Model command produce?
options: A model that inherits from a base model
An independent copy of the model, with no link back to it
A new data space containing the model's objects
A package that adds the model's objects to an existing model
answer: A model that inherits from a base model
items.rationale: Extending creates an inheritance relationship, which is the whole point: changes to the base reach the extended model. Cloning is the separate command for an independent copy, and confusing the two is how teams end up maintaining the same definitions twice.
items.evidence_quote: Create a model that inherits from a base model.

items.stem: A calculated field defined in a semantic model exists as a physical column in the underlying database.
items.rationale: Calculated fields are definitions evaluated at query time; nothing is materialised in the source. That is why adding one does not consume storage or need a refresh.
items.evidence_quote: Calculated fields don’t physically exist in the database.

items.stem: A prospect asks where Tableau Semantics sits in relation to Data 360. Which description is correct?
options: It operates on top of Data 360 data sources and powers the consumption experiences that source data from Data 360
It is a separate ingestion layer that loads external data into Data 360
It runs inside Tableau Cloud and reaches Data 360 through the Tableau Semantics connector
It is a Tableau Next-only layer that Data 360 Reports cannot use
answer: It operates on top of Data 360 data sources and powers the consumption experiences that source data from Data 360
items.rationale: Tableau Semantics is a layer over Data 360 data sources that feeds every consumption experience, including Data 360 Reports, Tableau Next, intelligent apps and AI. It is not an ingestion mechanism, and it is not hosted in Tableau Cloud - the connector is only one way to consume it.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Semantics operates on top of Data 360 data sources, and powers all consumption experiences that source data from Data 360.

items.stem: Which pair of ingredients makes up a metric in Tableau Semantics?
options: A measure or calculated field, plus a time dimension
A submetric, plus a goal
A dimension hierarchy, plus a global filter
A primary name field, plus a sentiment
answer: A measure or calculated field, plus a time dimension
items.rationale: A metric is a KPI tracked over time, so it needs the quantity itself (a measure or calculated field) and the time dimension that tracks its progression. Submetrics, goals and sentiment are optional additions to a metric, not what constitutes one.
items.evidence_quote: The core components of a metric are a measure or calculated field representing the KPI and a time dimension that tracks its progression over time.

items.stem: Why is a semantic model usable by other Salesforce experiences rather than only by the tool that built it?
options: It is first-class Salesforce metadata
Tableau Next republishes a copy of it to each consuming application
It is stored as a data lake object that any application can query
Each consumer keeps its own synchronised replica of the model
items.rationale: Being metadata rather than an application artefact is what makes one definition available across Data 360. Nothing is copied or replicated per consumer.
items.evidence_quote: Semantic models are first-class Salesforce metadata, so they’re available throughout Data 360 to power analytics and data-driven experiences.

items.stem: In Tableau Semantics, the Primary Name Field is the field that uniquely identifies each record in a table.
items.rationale: Unique identification is the job of the primary key. The Primary Name Field supplies the record's display name, which is what an analytics agent shows when it lists records.
items.evidence_quote: The primary key is the unique identifier for a table record. The Primary Name Field provides the main table record name for display purposes.

items.stem: Tableau Semantics answers business questions by sending customizable semantic queries built from a semantic model. Name the component that does this.
items.rationale: The Query Generator is the component that turns a semantic model into customizable semantic queries; the Semantic Model Builder, by contrast, is where the model is authored rather than queried.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Semantics also uses a Query Generator to leverage the data to answer key business questions by sending customizable semantic queries based on your semantic models.

items.stem: A team manages semantic models as code with the Salesforce Tableau Semantics extension for VS Code. Arrange the stages of one change cycle in the order they happen.
options: Retrieve the semantic model from the Data 360 org as JSON files
Edit the model definitions locally
Test semantic queries against the local definitions
Deploy the changes back to the Data 360 org
answer: Retrieve the semantic model from the Data 360 org as JSON files
Test semantic queries against the local definitions
Deploy the changes back to the Data 360 org
items.rationale: The extension pulls the model down as JSON, edits happen locally, queries can be tested against those local definitions, and only then are changes pushed back to the org - so testing precedes deployment rather than following it.
items.evidence_quote: Retrieve, build, edit, test, and deploy semantic models from your Data 360 org as code, without leaving VS Code. Use the Salesforce Tableau Semantics extension for VS Code to retrieve and build semantic models from your Data 360 org, edit them locally as JSON files, and deploy changes back to your org without leaving your editor. Test semantic queries by using local definitions before deploying.

items.stem: Data 360 security policies govern what a user sees in a semantic model. Match each policy layer to what it controls.
options: ABAC
OLS
FLS
RLS

pairs.right: Determines your access to a semantic model
Determines which objects in the dataspace you can access
Works the same way for individual fields within objects
Filters records dynamically using criteria such as hierarchies, roles, or territories

answer: ABAC::Determines your access to a semantic model
OLS::Determines which objects in the dataspace you can access
FLS::Works the same way for individual fields within objects
RLS::Filters records dynamically using criteria such as hierarchies, roles, or territories
items.rationale: ABAC decides access to the model itself, OLS and FLS remove whole objects and individual fields from design and query, and RLS filters at the record level. Sharing a model does not override any of them.

items.stem: A dbt model is brought into Tableau Semantics through the OSI v0.1 interchange format. What cardinality do the imported relationships arrive with, before anyone edits them?
options: Many-to-many (M:M)
One-to-many (1:M)
One-to-one (1:1)
Many-to-one (M:1)
items.rationale: OSI v0.1 sets every relationship to the same default cardinality and infers fields as dimensions or measures from metadata, so a delivery task after import is correcting cardinality to avoid duplicated or missing rows.
items.evidence_quote: Relationships are established with default cardinality of many-to-many (M:M).

items.stem: A semantic model has been created directly from a Tableau Cloud Published Data Source (PDS). Which limitations apply to that model?
options: Filtering with the like operator isn’t supported
The Row Count feature isn’t available
Table calculations created in the PDS aren’t reflected in the semantic model
Filtering with the Between operator isn’t supported
Aggregating a measure with SUM isn’t supported
Row-level security policies aren’t enforced when the model is queried
answer: Filtering with the like operator isn’t supported
The Row Count feature isn’t available
Table calculations created in the PDS aren’t reflected in the semantic model
items.rationale: PDS-based models lose the like operator, the auto-generated row count and PDS table calculations, which must be rebuilt in the Tableau Semantics layer. Between filters and SUM aggregation still work, and Data 360 security policies including RLS are still enforced.
items.evidence_quote: Filtering with the like operator isn’t supported. The Row Count feature isn’t available. See Row Count in Tableau Semantics for more information. Table calculations created in the PDS aren’t yet reflected in the Semantic Model.

items.stem: The Similar Meanings scan detects synonyms and overlapping definitions that confuse AI agents. Which kind of semantic model is outside its scope?
options: Extended models
PDS-based models
Models that contain logical views
Models built on Data Lake Objects (DLOs)
items.rationale: Neither the base nor the extended objects of an extended model are scanned. PDS-based models are scanned, though only the description and field visibility can be edited to resolve a pair, and a logical view is scanned as a flat object.
items.evidence_quote: Similar meanings are not supported for extended models. Neither base nor extended objects are included in the scan.

items.stem: A semantic model has been retrieved for local editing in VS Code and appears as a set of JSON files. Pair each file with what it holds.

pairs.right: Dimensions and measurements
Joins between objects, with cardinality and join fields
Business metrics
Drill-down hierarchies

answer: relationships.json::Joins between objects, with cardinality and join fields
items.rationale: The file layout mirrors the model's own concepts, which is what makes a semantic model reviewable in a pull request. Calculated fields are the one thing split across two files, one for dimensions and one for measurements.
items.evidence_quote: Data objects (dataObjects.json): Add or modify dimensions and measurements Relationships (relationships.json): Define joins between objects with cardinality and join fields Calculated fields (calculatedDimensions.json, calculatedMeasurements.json): Create computed fields with expressions Logical views (logicalViews.json): Create virtual tables from HardJoin or Union operations Metrics (metrics.json): Define business metrics Hierarchies (dimensionHierarchies.json): Configure drill-down hierarchies

items.stem: A single logical view in Tableau Semantics can combine a union with a join, stacking two similar datasets and then joining the result to a third object.
items.rationale: A logical view does one or the other, and it can hold only one union. Combining the two means building a second logical view over the first rather than doing both in one place, which is a real constraint on how a model is laid out.
items.evidence_quote: You can create one union per logical view. You cannot combine unions and joins.

items.stem: Business Preferences can be added to a semantic model on any Data 360 edition, with no Tableau Next licence involved.
items.rationale: Business Preferences, the place where local terminology and default behaviours are declared for the analytics agent, is gated behind a Tableau Next Standard License, so a Data 360-only customer cannot use it.
items.evidence_quote: Business Preferences requires a Tableau Next Standard License.

items.stem: A new semantic model picks up the relationships already mapped between DMOs in Data 360. What becomes of a relationship that would reference the same object more than once?
options: It is removed
It is imported but left inactive until an owner approves it
It is rewritten as a shared table so the path stays unambiguous
It is kept, and the query generator picks a path at query time
items.rationale: Circular relationships are stripped out when the model is created, because a cycle leaves the query generator with more than one path between objects. Nothing is imported in a disabled state and nothing is silently converted into a shared table.
items.evidence_quote: Relationships that create circular relationships (relationships that reference the same object multiple times) are removed.

items.stem: An edit made in a composed model is written back into the referenced model that it was built from.
items.rationale: Inheritance runs one way only: the referenced model stays the single source of truth and its changes flow down, while changes made in the composed model stay local to it.
items.evidence_quote: Changes made to the referenced model are automatically added to the composed model, but changes made to the composed model aren’t pushed to the referenced model.

items.stem: A new relationship that lets the semantic layer reach the same table by more than one path is allowed, provided the modeller documents which path should be preferred.
items.rationale: Fact trees have to stay cycle-free; the platform does not accept the relationship and leave path selection to convention.
items.evidence_quote: Fact trees must remain cycle-free. Cycles introduce ambiguity: if the system can reach the same table through more than one path, it may not know which to follow, or how to apply filters and aggregations correctly. For this reason, creating a new relationship that introduces a cycle -- such as connecting Marketing directly to Subcategory (which is already reachable through Product) -- is not allowed.

items.stem: Two DMOs have to be combined with an inner join because the logic can't be expressed by connecting them the usual way. Which semantic model construct do you create?
options: A logical view
A shared table
A composed model
A dimension hierarchy
items.rationale: A logical view is the only construct that combines objects with joins or unions instead of relationships, and it then behaves like any other data object. A shared table connects fact tables through a common dimension but does not define a join; a composed model extends another model.
items.evidence_quote: A logical view is a data object that combines objects using joins or unions rather than relationships.

items.stem: Match each semantic model access role to what it allows.
options: Viewer
Editor
Owner

pairs.right: Can open the model and interact with it, but can't change it
Has permission to modify the model
Has full control and can share the model, but the role can't be handed over

answer: Viewer::Can open the model and interact with it, but can't change it
Editor::Has permission to modify the model
Owner::Has full control and can share the model, but the role can't be handed over
items.rationale: Viewer is read and interact only, Editor can modify, and Owner is the original creator with full control plus sharing. The trap is assuming ownership can be reassigned like the other two roles - it cannot be transferred.
items.evidence_quote: Viewer: Users can open the model and interact with it but can't make any changes. Editor: Users have permission to modify the model. Owner: The user who originally created the semantic model has full control. Owners can edit the model and manage access by sharing it with other users. While you can assign the Viewer or Editor access role to others, ownership can't be transferred.

items.stem: Semantic Modeling (Beta) generates a semantic model from a natural language description. Which components can it not produce in this version?
options: Metrics
Groups
Logical views
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server links
Relationships between the selected data objects
Calculated field formulas
items.rationale: Metrics, groups, logical views and MCP server links are out of scope for this release and must be added by hand afterwards. Relationships and calculated field formulas are the opposite case - the system adds them automatically to deliver the final model.
items.evidence_quote: Out of Scope: Advanced components including metrics, groups, logical views, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server links are not supported in this version and will be added in future versions.

items.stem: Sales and Marketing are separate fact tables linked only through a shared Products table. A query asks for an unaggregated field from each fact table and nothing from Products. What does the semantic layer do?
options: It performs a cross-join, pairing every Sales row with every Marketing row
It adds the shared table's key to the query automatically so the rows align
It returns rows from one fact table and nulls for the other
It rejects the query because two fact tables can never appear together
answer: It performs a cross-join, pairing every Sales row with every Marketing row
items.rationale: With no field from the shared table there is no key on which to align the two facts, so every row of one is combined with every row of the other. Including a shared-table field such as Product or Date restores a sensible join axis; the system does not add it for you.
items.evidence_quote: If you query fields from both fact tables without including a field from the shared table, and the fields are not aggregated, the system performs a cross-join.

items.stem: Business preferences added to a semantic model are capped in size. At most how many characters may a single business-preference instruction contain?
items.rationale: Each instruction is limited to 300 characters, and a model accepts up to 50 of them; long or numerous instructions inflate the agent's prompt and slow responses.
items.evidence_quote: You can add up to 50 instructions, with each instruction limited to 300 characters.

items.stem: AI Semantic Description Generator can draft a description for a calculated field whose formula is still invalid, so the author can document the field before fixing the formula.
items.rationale: A description can be generated only once the calculated field is valid, so the formula has to be corrected first; the generator reads a working definition rather than an unresolved one.
items.evidence_quote: You can generate a description only if the calculated field is valid.

items.stem: In a logical view that combines its data objects with joins, every one of those objects must be connected by a join before the logical view can be previewed or saved.
items.rationale: An unjoined object blocks both preview and save, which is why objects are added and joined one at a time rather than dropped in and connected later. The requirement is specific to join-based logical views: a union-based logical view contains no joins at all, and unions and joins can't be combined in the same logical view.
items.evidence_quote: You must create joins between all data objects in the logical view, otherwise you can’t preview or save the logical view.

items.stem: A semantic model has been retrieved into a local folder of JSON files for source control. Which file must be present for the folder to be a usable model?
options: model.json
dataObjects.json
modelInfo.json
relationships.json
items.rationale: Only the file holding the model metadata is required; every other file, including the data objects and relationships, is treated as empty when missing, so a partial folder still deploys.
items.evidence_quote: Only `model.json` is required. Missing files are treated as empty.

items.stem: Editing a semantic model's files locally, which operations can a logical view be built from?
options: HardJoin
Union
Aggregate
Filter
Pivot
items.rationale: Two operations only, which is why a logical view is the answer for combining objects and never for reshaping or summarising them. Aggregation belongs to metrics and calculated measurements.
items.evidence_quote: Logical views (logicalViews.json): Create virtual tables from HardJoin or Union operations

items.stem: An analyst holding the Data Cloud Architect permission set cannot create a union in a logical view. What else does Salesforce say is needed?
options: Access to the Semantic Models object
The Data Cloud Activation Manager permission set as well
Modify All Data on the data model objects in the union
The Tableau Unmetered Platform Analyst permission set
answer: Access to the Semantic Models object
items.rationale: The requirement is stated as Data Cloud Architect AND the Semantic Models object, so the permission set alone is not enough. Object access is easy to overlook because the permission set is the thing people think to check.

-   Data Cloud Architect

AND

items.stem: What is the maximum number of business preferences that can be added to a semantic model?
items.rationale: Business preferences are capped at 20, within a 9000-character budget, so they have to be used for the guidance that matters rather than as a dumping ground.
items.evidence_quote: Your text should stay within the character limit of 9000 characters, with a maximum of 20 preferences.

items.stem: A modeller sets a relationship to many-to-one to make queries faster. What side effect should they check for before trusting the numbers?
options: Row multiplication, because deduplication is switched off for that relationship
Missing rows, because unmatched records are dropped from the join
Currency measures reverting to each record's local currency
The relationship being dropped from the model as a circular reference
answer: Row multiplication, because deduplication is switched off for that relationship
items.rationale: One-to-one and many-to-one cardinality turns off the deduplication algorithm, which is where the speed-up comes from; if the declared cardinality is wrong, rows multiply and results are inaccurate. Records are not dropped, and cardinality has nothing to do with currency conversion or cycle removal.
items.evidence_quote: Defining a one-to-one or many-to-one relationship disables the deduplication algorithm. Performance will improve, but if cardinality is set incorrectly it may cause row multiplication and lead to inaccurate results.

items.stem: A semantic model includes a data lake object among its data objects. Which population of users is then shut out of that semantic model?
options: Users in companion orgs
Users assigned the Viewer access role
Users who hold only the View All permission
Users querying the model through Data 360 Reports
items.rationale: A DLO in the model blocks access for companion org users, which is why a model destined for a companion org should be built on DMOs. Viewers and View All holders can still open the model, and Data 360 Reports is a supported consumption layer.
items.evidence_quote: If the semantic model contains a DLO (Data Lake Object), users in companion orgs won't be able to access the semantic model.

items.stem: Relationships that already exist in Data 360 arrive in a new semantic model automatically. What does a modeller still have to add to those imported relationships by hand?
options: The key qualifier
A join type
A shared table marker on the dimension object
An override in a composed model
items.rationale: The key qualifier comes across from Data 360 but is not attached to the imported relationships, so it has to be applied manually. A join type is never needed, because a relationship combines objects without one.
items.evidence_quote: The key qualifier is also imported directly from Data 360, but you need to add it manually to the imported relationships.

items.stem: In Data 360, at the step where you select the data objects for a new semantic model, how many objects can you select at most?
items.rationale: The object picker caps the selection at 100 objects, which is the figure that decides whether a wide enterprise model has to be split into several models or extended as a composed model.
items.evidence_quote: Select the data objects for your semantic model. You can select up to 100 objects.

items.stem: An analyst wants to trace how opportunities move between pipeline stages, including where one stage branches into several and where separate paths merge. Which Tableau Next chart type is built for that question?
options: A Sankey chart
A waterfall chart
A radial chart
A heat map
items.rationale: Sankey charts are about movement between stages, showing where values split, combine or fall away. A waterfall shows how a single total is built up or eroded, which is a different question about a different shape of data.
items.evidence_quote: Review how data values move across stages in a process to understand how they split, combine, or drop off.

items.stem: Size encoding varies the size of a mark by the value of a continuous measure. Which mark types does Tableau Next support it on?
options: Bar
Square
Circle
Line
Area
Text
items.rationale: Size encoding needs a mark with an area to grow, so it applies to bars, squares and circles. Lines and areas are already shaped by their data, and a text mark has nothing to scale.
items.evidence_quote: Use size encoding to highlight differences in values in bar, square, or circle mark types.

items.stem: A dashboard author wants a set of widgets held together as one unit, so that a single click can trigger an action for everything inside it. Which Tableau Next widget does that?
options: The container widget
The navigation widget
The summary widget
The parameter widget
items.rationale: A container holds other widgets so tasks can be done on the set, and an action assigned to it starts when any widget inside it is clicked. The navigation widget turns dashboard pages into a nav bar, the summary widget merges metrics into a narrative, and the parameter widget collects an input; none of them holds other widgets.
items.evidence_quote: Make widget tasks easier by adding them to a container widget. You can also configure containers with single-click actions to add interactivity to your dashboard.

items.stem: A Navigate To action is being configured on a dashboard widget. Which destination types can be chosen for it?
options: A URL
Another Tableau Next dashboard
A page within a dashboard
A Salesforce record
A Slack channel
items.rationale: The destination is a URL, a dashboard, or a dashboard page, and the page-level one is the useful surprise: the action can land on a specific page of a dashboard rather than its first page. The only other action type a widget can carry is a Salesforce Flow, so neither a record nor a Slack channel is offered as a navigation destination.
items.evidence_quote: Add a Navigate To action to a widget to guide your users to relevant URLs or other Tableau Next dashboards and dashboard pages with detailed information on the selected data.

items.stem: The Tableau Next Marketplace centralises templates for which asset types?
options: Metrics
Semantic models
Dashboards
Visualizations
Data streams
Identity resolution rulesets
items.rationale: Marketplace covers the four Tableau Next authoring assets. Data streams and identity resolution rulesets are Data 360 configuration and are not templated there.
items.evidence_quote: The Tableau Next Marketplace centralizes all templates for metrics, semantic models, dashboards, and visualizations.

items.stem: In Tableau Next, what is a metric?
options: A business KPI tracked over time and derived from one or more measures
A calculated field defined directly on a data model object
A saved filter that applies across every asset in a workspace
A visualization that has been pinned to the analytics home page
answer: A business KPI tracked over time and derived from one or more measures
items.rationale: A metric is a governed KPI built on measures from the semantic model, with sentiment and aggregation attached. It is not a field, a filter, or a pinned chart.
items.evidence_quote: A metric is a business KPI that you can track over time and use to assess performance or business processes. A metric is derived from one or more measures.

items.stem: A metric in Tableau Next is derived from one or more of which kind of semantic model field?
items.rationale: Metrics sit on measures, which is why the semantic model has to define the measure before the metric can exist.
items.evidence_quote: A metric is derived from one or more measures.

items.stem: In Tableau Next, what is a workspace?
options: A container where analysts create, add, and reuse analytic assets to answer questions about their data
A logical partition of Data 360 that determines which records a user is allowed to query
A permission set that grants a user the ability to edit dashboards and visualizations
A curated catalogue of installable dashboard and metric templates shared across the org
answer: A container where analysts create, add, and reuse analytic assets to answer questions about their data
items.rationale: A workspace is the unit of authoring work that holds and reuses analytic assets. A data space is the logical partition of Data 360 data, a permission set grants capability, and the Marketplace is the template catalogue.
items.evidence_quote: A workspace is a flexible place for analysts to create, add, and reuse analytic assets to answer questions about their data.

items.stem: True or false: the changes an analyst makes to data while working in a Tableau Next workspace are written back to the source data in Data 360 and to the original uploaded files.
items.rationale: Work done in Tableau Next leaves the Data 360 source data and the original files untouched, which is why analyst exploration is safe to allow on governed data.
items.evidence_quote: Changes you make in Tableau Next don't affect the source data in Data 360 or in your original files.

items.stem: A user clicks a mark on a dashboard to filter it. Every visualization responds, but one metric tile does not move. What is the most likely reason?
options: The metric's definition doesn't contain the dimension being used as the filter
The metric is built on a calculated field from the semantic model definition
The metric is followed rather than owned by that user
Metrics only respond to filters applied from the filter pane, not from a mark
answer: The metric's definition doesn't contain the dimension being used as the filter
items.rationale: A metric can only be cut by a dimension its own definition includes, so a dashboard filter on anything else leaves it unchanged. Calculated fields that are part of the semantic model definition are applied to metrics, and metrics do respond to a mark selection, so neither of those explains a tile that stays still.
items.evidence_quote: If a metric's definition doesn't contain the additional dimension that you're using as a filter, then the metric doesn't update.

items.stem: Tableau Next offers data palettes that suit different kinds of data. Pair each palette with what it is for.

pairs.right: Distinguishing between distinct groups
Showing increasing or decreasing values across a low-to-high range
Contrasting values around a meaningful midpoint such as zero or an average
Using widely understood colour meanings, such as red for negative and green for positive

answer: Sequential::Showing increasing or decreasing values across a low-to-high range
Diverging::Contrasting values around a meaningful midpoint such as zero or an average
Semantic::Using widely understood colour meanings, such as red for negative and green for positive
items.rationale: The pair people confuse is sequential and diverging. Sequential runs low to high, diverging is anchored on a midpoint that means something, so using sequential for profit and loss hides the thing the reader is looking for.
items.evidence_quote: Data palettes provide context-aware options to match the type of data you're working with, such as: Categorical to distinguish between distinct groups Sequential to highlight increasing or decreasing values across a low-to-high range Diverging to contrast values around a meaningful midpoint, such as zero or an average Semantic to help users interpret data more quickly using colors with standard, widely understood meanings, such as red for negative values and green for positive.

items.stem: A forecast is being skewed by the current month, which is only part way through and so looks like a collapse. Name the Tableau Next forecasting setting that excludes the most recent periods from the data the forecast is built on.
items.rationale: Ignore Last drops a stated number of the most recent periods, counted in the chart's own time interval. It is the standard fix for a partial current period dragging a trend down.
items.evidence_quote: | Ignore Last | Specify the number of most recent periods to exclude from the data used in forecasting, based on the chart's time interval. |

rows: Set the forecast duration based on the chart’s time interval, such as days, weeks, or months.
Choose whether to fill missing data points with zeroes in the forecast.
Specify the number of most recent periods to exclude from the data used in forecasting, based on the chart’s time interval.

Set the percentage for the shaded area where the forecasted values are expected to fall. A higher percentage produces a wider shaded range that represents a higher likelihood that the actual values fall within that range. For example, if you select 95%, the model expects the actual values to fall within the shaded area with 95% likelihood.

items.stem: A measure has risen fairly steadily for three years with no seasonality. Which Tableau Next forecasting model suits it?
options: Ridge Regression
Holt-Winters
Exponential Smoothing
ARIMA
items.rationale: Ridge Regression is the one for a mostly linear trend, and its regularization keeps it from overfitting. Holt-Winters is the other model offered and is for data whose trend changes over time. The remaining two are real forecasting techniques but not options in Tableau Next.
items.evidence_quote: The Ridge Regression model forecasts data with a mostly linear trend and applies regularization to keep variable weights balanced and reduce overfitting.

items.stem: Raising the prediction interval on a Tableau Next forecast from 80% to 95% makes the shaded band around the forecast wider.
items.rationale: A higher percentage claims more confidence that the real value lands inside the band, and the only way to buy that confidence is a wider band. Readers often assume the opposite, taking a narrow band as the more confident forecast.
items.evidence_quote: A higher percentage produces a wider shaded range that represents a higher likelihood that the actual values fall within that range.

items.stem: An analyst picks the Sankey chart type in the Show Me pane. What is the minimum a Sankey needs before it can draw?
options: Two dimensions on Levels and one measure on Links
One dimension on Levels and two measures on Links
Two measures on Levels and one dimension on Links
One dimension and one measure, both on Levels
answer: Two dimensions on Levels and one measure on Links
items.rationale: A flow needs at least two stages to move between, which is why two dimensions are required on Levels, and the measure on Links is the quantity doing the moving. Getting this backwards is the usual reason a Sankey refuses to render.
items.evidence_quote: the Show Me pane shows you the minimum required fields for the chart type: two dimensions on Levels and one measure on Links.

items.stem: Over what range of time intervals can a calculated insight's dynamic time-window metrics be defined?
options: From seconds up to years
From minutes up to a single year
From hours up to 90 days
From days up to years, but no shorter than a day
items.rationale: The range runs from seconds to years, which is what lets the same mechanism serve both a ten-minute recommendation window and a multi-year trend. The one-minute floor that people generalise from belongs to streaming insights, and assuming a floor of a day rules out the real-time personalisation cases these metrics exist for.
items.evidence_quote: You can define and calculate dynamic metrics over configurable time intervals, from seconds to years (365+ days).

items.stem: A Tableau Next workspace is about to be deleted. Pair each kind of asset with what happens to it.

pairs.left: An asset that exists only in this workspace
pairs.right: It is deleted

pairs.left: An asset from this workspace that is also used in another workspace
pairs.right: It is deleted from both workspaces

pairs.left: An asset this workspace reused from another workspace
pairs.right: The original is left untouched

answer: An asset that exists only in this workspace::It is deleted
An asset from this workspace that is also used in another workspace::It is deleted from both workspaces
An asset this workspace reused from another workspace::The original is left untouched
items.rationale: Direction is what decides it. An asset this workspace owns goes wherever it is used, taking it out of the other workspace too, while an asset borrowed from elsewhere survives because this workspace never owned it. Assuming deletion is contained within the workspace is how people lose an asset someone else was relying on.
items.evidence_quote: If you delete a workspace, the assets inside the workspace are also deleted. If a workspace asset is used in another workspace, the asset is deleted from both workspaces. If the workspace contains an asset that's reused from another workspace, the original asset is unaffected.

items.stem: Arrange what happens to a CSV file uploaded to a Tableau Next workspace, from first to last.
options: The data in the file is parsed
The data is verified
The data is added to a new data object
The data object is used in a semantic model, visualization, or dashboard
answer: The data in the file is parsed
The data is added to a new data object
The data object is used in a semantic model, visualization, or dashboard
items.rationale: An upload is parsed, then verified, then landed as a new data object; only after that does it become available to a semantic model, visualization or dashboard. The upload does not become an analysable asset before the data object exists.
items.evidence_quote: The data is parsed, verified, and added to a new data object. You can then use it in a semantic model, visualization, or dashboard.

items.stem: A dashboard mixes visualizations built on two unrelated semantic data models, and the client wants one click to filter both at once. Which dashboard capability is designed for that?
options: Multi-model filtering
The Summary widget
Initial values for the dashboard
The dashboard query cache
items.rationale: Multi-model filtering is what spans fields on separate objects and disparate semantic data models in a single interaction. The Summary widget merges metrics into a narrative, initial values preset filters at load time, and the query cache only affects load performance.
items.evidence_quote: Simplify Cross-Functional Analysis by Using Multi-Model Filtering Filter fields across separate objects and visualizations that have disparate semantic data models with a single dashboard interaction.

items.stem: Pair each Tableau Next radial chart type with the analysis it is intended for.

pairs.right: Compare how individual values contribute to a whole
Combine a part-to-whole view with a prominent total or KPI value
Review values across equal, cyclical time periods and highlight differences in magnitude
Track progress toward goals across multiple entities

answer: Pie chart::Compare how individual values contribute to a whole
Donut chart::Combine a part-to-whole view with a prominent total or KPI value
Nightingale rose chart::Review values across equal, cyclical time periods and highlight differences in magnitude
Radial bar chart::Track progress toward goals across multiple entities
items.rationale: Pie and donut both show part-to-whole, but the donut is the one that also carries a prominent total or KPI in the centre. The Nightingale rose compares magnitude across equal cyclical periods, while the radial bar is the goal-attainment chart across entities.
items.evidence_quote: | Pie chart | Compare how individual values contribute to a whole. | | Donut chart | Combine a part-to-whole view with a prominent total or KPI value. | | Nightingale rose chart | Review values across equal, cyclical time periods and highlight differences in magnitude. | | Radial bar chart | Track progress toward goals across multiple entities. |

items.stem: A team working in a Data Cloud One companion org wants to bring a spreadsheet of targets into Tableau Next by uploading it. What access do they have to Add New Data by file upload there?
options: No access at all in a companion org
Full access, the same as in the home org
Access only for users holding the Platform Analyst permission set
Access limited to files already staged in the home org
answer: No access at all in a companion org
items.rationale: File upload is one of the few Tableau Next features a companion org loses outright, while studio, workspaces, dashboards and visualizations all keep full access. A design that assumes analysts can top up their data with a spreadsheet has to put them in the home org.
items.evidence_quote: | Add New Data (File Upload) | Full Access | No Access |

rows: Data Analysis from Tableau Agent in Tableau Next
Tableau Next Apps for Salesforce (i.e. Revenue Insights, Service Insights)

items.stem: In a Data Cloud One companion org, a semantic model that synced down from the home org can be edited there like any model the companion org created itself.
items.rationale: A companion org can create, edit and delete its own semantic models over DMOs, but anything synced from the home org is read-only. The home org stays the place a shared model is changed, which is what keeps the two from diverging.
items.evidence_quote: Users can create, edit, and delete SMs using DMOs. SMs synced from the home org can't be edited or deleted.

items.stem: Metric insight summaries generated through Agentforce for Analytics with Concierge: Analytics Q&A can draw on flex credits.
items.rationale: The agent-generated route may consume flex credits, which matters when insight summaries are switched on across a large user base. The non-agent route summarises with a language model instead and is gated by an org preference and a user permission rather than by credits.
items.evidence_quote: Insight summaries might consume flex credits when generated using Agentforce for Analytics with Concierge: Analytics Q&A.

items.stem: An org wants metric insight summaries without turning on the analytics agent. Which two of these must an administrator enable?
options: The Metric Insight Summaries org preference
The TableauFollowMetrics user permission
The Einstein Trust Layer for the org
A Tableau Agent built from the Analytics and Visualization template
Flex Credits on the Data 360 consumption card
answer: The Metric Insight Summaries org preference
items.rationale: Two switches, both included in the Tableau Next platform licence. Creating an agent is exactly what this route avoids, and the Trust Layer underpins the summaries rather than being something an admin turns on for them.
items.evidence_quote: For metric insight summaries that don't use the analytics agent, administrators need to enable the Metric Insight Summaries org preference and the TableauFollowMetrics user permission, which are included in the Tableau Next platform license

items.stem: In Data 360, what prompts a real-time insight to update its metrics?
options: A data event being processed
The insight's refresh schedule falling due
An identity resolution ruleset run finishing
The nightly refresh of the real-time data graph
items.rationale: Real-time insights are event driven: processing a data event updates the metric. The value itself is worked out at graph query time, and a real-time graph client has to do that last step on its side to get the true metric, so nothing about this runs on a timetable.
items.evidence_quote: Real-time insights update metrics when a data event is processed.

items.stem: Where are the NOW, SECOND_ADD and SECOND_SUB functions available for building a relative time window?
options: In the transform node of Visual Insight Builder
In the filter node of Visual Insight Builder only
In segment filter criteria only
In the semantic model's calculated field editor
answer: In the transform node of Visual Insight Builder
items.rationale: The functions live in the transform node, while the filter node offers a Relative DateTime operator instead. They are two different ways at the same idea, and reaching for the functions in the filter node is the natural mistake.
items.evidence_quote: The `NOW`, `SECOND_ADD`, and `SECOND_SUB` functions are available in the transform node for Visual Insight Builder.

items.stem: When a dashboard is set to reuse cached query results, how many minutes pass before an automatic refresh is triggered?
items.rationale: The cache window explains the complaint that a dashboard is showing stale numbers, and it is the first thing to check before investigating the data pipeline.
items.evidence_quote: Once enabled, the dashboard utilizes cached query results for 30 minutes before triggering an automatic refresh.

items.stem: What is the maximum number of pages a Tableau Next dashboard can have?
items.rationale: A hard ceiling worth knowing before promising a client a single dashboard covering every report they currently have.
items.evidence_quote: Dashboards can have up to 50 pages.

items.stem: How many Salesforce flow actions can be added to a single dashboard widget?
options: One
Up to five
Up to ten
Unlimited, though only one can run at a time
items.rationale: A widget takes a single flow action, although it can carry several navigation actions. The five-per-field limit that people half-remember applies to Salesforce actions on a visualization field, not to flow actions on a widget.
items.evidence_quote: Only 1 Salesforce flow action can be added per widget, but a widget can have multiple navigation actions.

items.stem: True or false: once the time period behind a Tableau Next metric goal has passed, the goal and its thresholds roll forward automatically into the following period.
items.rationale: Goals and thresholds do not recur when their time period ends; someone has to set them again at the start of each period. A client expecting rolling quarterly targets needs that manual step designed into the process.
items.evidence_quote: When the goal’s time period has passed, the goal and thresholds don’t recur.

items.stem: Before an analyst can drive a dashboard widget with a parameter, which artefact must they be able to open and edit, because that is where a Tableau Next parameter lives?
options: The semantic model
The dashboard that consumes the parameter
The workspace, alongside its data connections
The visualization the parameter is applied to
items.rationale: Parameters are created and stored in the semantic model, so parameter work needs semantic model access rather than only dashboard editing rights. Storing them in the dashboard or visualization would prevent the reuse the feature is built for.
items.evidence_quote: Parameters are created and stored in the semantic model.

items.stem: How many Salesforce actions can be added to a single visualization field?
items.rationale: Five per field, which is a different ceiling from the one flow action allowed per dashboard widget.
items.evidence_quote: Select up to 5 actions to add to the field.

items.stem: You added three Salesforce actions to a Tableau Next visualization, but a user with the correct analyst permission set sees only one of them. What best explains the difference?
options: A user is shown only those actions that are also available on the source object's Salesforce page layout
Only the first action added to a visualization is shown, and the rest need their own visualization
Salesforce actions appear only when the visualization is embedded in a Lightning page
Salesforce actions stay hidden until the visualization's semantic model is enabled for Analytics Agent Readiness
answer: A user is shown only those actions that are also available on the source object's Salesforce page layout
items.rationale: The visible set is the intersection of the actions the author added and the actions on the source object's Salesforce page layout, so a page layout change can silently remove an action. Embedding affects which actions are available on a page but is not what filters this list, and agent readiness is unrelated.
items.evidence_quote: Users see only the Salesforce actions that you add to the visualization and that are available on the source object's Salesforce page layout.

items.stem: Match each Tableau Next asset access role to the capability that the documentation gives that role.
options: Viewer
Editor
Owner

pairs.right: Interact with the asset and see all the fields it uses
Modify the asset
Delete and share the asset

answer: Viewer::Interact with the asset and see all the fields it uses
items.rationale: The three access roles are cumulative: viewers interact and can see the fields in use, editors additionally modify, and only owners can delete and share. Consultants get this wrong by assuming an editor can re-share an asset.
items.evidence_quote: Viewers can interact with the asset, ask questions about the asset and get answers, and see all the fields that the asset uses. Editors can modify the asset. Owners can delete and share the asset.

items.stem: A prospect asks which prebuilt Tableau Next App for Salesforce covers key contact centre performance metrics for their support organisation. Which app do you name?
options: Service Insights
Field Service Intelligence
Sales Insights
Agent Analytics
items.rationale: Service Insights is the packaged Data 360 plus Tableau Next solution for contact centre KPIs. Field Service Intelligence covers field service operational performance, Sales Insights covers pipeline and forecasting, and Agent Analytics measures AI agent sessions rather than human contact centre performance.
items.evidence_quote: Service Insights is a data-driven solution that displays key contact center performance metrics.

items.stem: A client wants Tableau Next dashboards and metrics to appear inside their own customer-facing web application, not inside Salesforce. Which Tableau Next capability is built for that?
options: The Tableau Next Embedding SDK
The Tableau Next following component for Lightning pages
The AppFrameworkTemplateBundle app template package
A Slack canvas card that refreshes for each viewer
items.rationale: The Embedding SDK is the supported route for putting Tableau Next components into a third-party web app, and it supplies the authentication methods. The following component and the Lightning web components are for Lightning pages inside Salesforce, and an app template package is for distributing analytics content between orgs.
items.evidence_quote: Use the Tableau Next Embedding SDK to integrate Tableau Next insights into your own web apps.

items.stem: A user with consumer permissions opens the Tableau Next app in a browser. What is their home page experience?
options: The Following tab
The list of workspaces they can access
The semantic model catalog
The Data 360 Profile Explorer
items.rationale: Consumers land on Following, the page that lists the metrics they follow, while analysts reach Following from the left panel instead. Workspaces and semantic models are authoring surfaces, and Profile Explorer belongs to Data 360.
items.evidence_quote: While analysts can find Following in the left panel, users with consumer permissions see the Following tab as their home page web experience in the Tableau Next app.

items.stem: What does the share option on a Tableau Next asset let you add or remove?
options: Viewers or editors
Owners or viewers
Admins or editors
Followers or subscribers
items.rationale: Sharing grants view or edit. Ownership is not something sharing can hand over, and following is a separate consumer behaviour.
items.evidence_quote: Use the share option to add or remove viewers or editors for an asset.

items.stem: An author has just created a dashboard in Tableau Next and has not shared it or changed any access setting. Who can see the dashboard?
options: Only the user who created it
Every user in the org, with viewer access
Every user who holds a Tableau Next Platform Analyst permission set
Every member of the analytics groups the creator belongs to
answer: Only the user who created it
items.rationale: New workspaces, dashboards, visualizations and semantic models start private to their creator, so access has to be granted deliberately. Org-wide visibility only happens if someone sets general access for the asset; holding an analyst permission set is a licence to author, not access to somebody else's asset.
items.evidence_quote: Workspaces, dashboards, visualizations, and semantic models are, by default, private to the users who create them.

items.stem: Put the stages of a Data 360 clean room collaboration into the order they happen for the consumer who starts it.
options: You save the collaboration in your Enterprise Edition home org
The provider receives an invitation to the collaboration
The provider accepts the invitation in their Enterprise Edition home org
You run permitted queries on the combined dataset
The query results are stored in a DMO
answer: You save the collaboration in your Enterprise Edition home org
The provider receives an invitation to the collaboration
The provider accepts the invitation in their Enterprise Edition home org
You run permitted queries on the combined dataset
The query results are stored in a DMO
items.rationale: Saving the collaboration sends the invitation automatically; only after the provider accepts in their own Enterprise Edition home org can permitted queries run on the combined dataset, and the output lands in a DMO ready for downstream use. Queries cannot run before acceptance, and results are not returned as a file.
items.evidence_quote: When you save a collaboration, the provider automatically receives an invitation to the collaboration. After the provider accepts the invitation in their Enterprise Edition home org, you can run permitted queries on the combined dataset. The results of the queries are stored in a DMO.

items.stem: A Data Access and Export request in Data 360 exports everything held for the named Individual profiles as a CSV to your Amazon S3 bucket. Within how many days is that file published?
items.rationale: The published commitment is within 15 days of the request, which is what you quote when a client asks how quickly a subject access request can be answered. It is not a same-day or 30-day process, and requests are submitted through the Consent API rather than the UI.
items.evidence_quote: This export is published as a CSV file to your defined Amazon S3 bucket within 15 days.

items.stem: A viewer has been given access to a dashboard in Tableau Next but still cannot see the records behind it. Where is access to the underlying data model objects controlled?
options: In Data 360
In the workspace sharing dialog
On the dashboard's own share settings
In the semantic model's business preferences
items.rationale: Asset sharing and data access are two different controls. Sharing a dashboard never grants the underlying object access, which is administered in Data 360.
items.evidence_quote: Access to data model objects and data lake objects is controlled in Data 360.

items.stem: Alongside installing the Embedding SDK, one type of Salesforce app must be set up to authenticate users before Tableau Next component code will work in a custom web app. Name that type of app.
items.rationale: Embedding Tableau Next components in an external app requires an External Client App (ECA) for authentication as well as the Embedding SDK in the web app. A Connected App or a Lightning web component alone does not satisfy the requirement.
items.evidence_quote: To embed Tableau Next components, an External Client App (ECA) for authentication is required and the Tableau Next Embedding SDK must be installed in your web app.

items.stem: Which Tableau Next assets can be placed on Lightning pages and custom pages using Lightning web components?
options: Metrics
Dashboards
Visualizations
Followed metrics
Data streams
Semantic models
items.rationale: The four presentation assets can be embedded. A semantic model and a data stream are not surfaces a user views, so neither is embeddable.
items.evidence_quote: Extend Tableau Next everywhere throughout your org by integrating Tableau Next metrics, dashboards, visualizations, and followed metrics into Lightning pages and custom pages using Lightning web components.

items.stem: In Tableau Next you can grant a user access to one individual metric without granting access to the semantic model that the metric is part of. True or false?
items.rationale: Metric access rides on semantic model access: granting the model grants its metrics, and access cannot be managed for an individual metric. A design that needs different audiences per metric therefore needs different semantic models, not per-metric sharing.
items.evidence_quote: By granting users access to a semantic model, you grant those users access to the metrics that are part of that semantic model. You can't manage access for individual metrics.

items.stem: Any user with edit access to a Tableau Next workspace can share that workspace with additional users.
items.rationale: Only the workspace owner can share a workspace, so an editor cannot widen access on the owner's behalf.
items.evidence_quote: Share a workspace | Only workspace owners can share.

items.stem: You have shared a semantic model with a group of analysts who already hold Tableau Next analyst permission sets, and they still cannot open it. Which additional requirement is specific to semantic models?
options: Access to the data space that the model belongs to
Membership of an analytics group that owns the model
Editor access to every dashboard built on the model
The Data Cloud Activation Specialist permission set
answer: Access to the data space that the model belongs to
items.rationale: Semantic model access is gated by the Data 360 data space the model lives in, granted through a data space permission set, on top of the Tableau Next share. Analytics group membership and dashboard roles do not grant data space access, and the Activation Specialist set is for segment activation.
items.evidence_quote: To access a semantic model, users must also have access to the data space that the model belongs to.

items.stem: Which objects can be shared with other users or groups using the share option in Tableau Next?
options: Workspaces
Dashboards
Visualizations
Semantic models
Data model objects
Data lake objects
items.rationale: The Tableau Next share option covers workspaces, dashboards, visualizations and semantic models. Access to data model objects and data lake objects is not shared from Tableau Next at all; it is controlled by tags and policies in Data 360, which is why a user can hold a visualization URL and still see nothing.
items.evidence_quote: Manage access to workspaces, dashboards, visualizations, and semantic models in Tableau Next. Use the share option to add or remove viewers or editors for an asset. Access to data model objects and data lake objects is controlled in Data 360.

items.stem: A team wants a persistent Slack surface where a Tableau Next metric keeps showing current numbers for whoever opens it, rather than the value at the moment it was posted. Which placement meets that?
options: A card pasted into a Slack canvas
A preview included in a channel message
A preview included in a direct message
A downloaded .png snapshot uploaded to the channel
answer: A card pasted into a Slack canvas
items.rationale: Canvas cards regularly refresh data from each viewer's perspective and show when the data was last refreshed. Previews in channels and DMs are point-in-time snapshots of the sender's view, and a downloaded image is frozen entirely.
items.evidence_quote: Unlike sharing a Tableau Next link in a direct message or channel, previews in Slack canvases regularly refresh data from each viewer’s perspective.

items.stem: A security reviewer asks whose permissions decide what data appears when someone opens a live data preview of a Tableau Next object in Slack. What do you tell them?
options: Each viewer's own security and data permissions
The sender's permissions, captured when the message was composed
The permissions of the Slack workspace owner
The permissions of the admin who enabled the Slack integration
answer: Each viewer's own security and data permissions
items.rationale: Live previews always load from the viewer's perspective, so each viewer sees only what their own Tableau Next and Data 360 permissions allow, and a viewer without access sees a no-access message. The sender's permissions govern the static point-in-time snapshot preview, which is the near-miss answer.
items.evidence_quote: For all live data previews, Slack and Tableau always load the data from the viewer’s perspective, respecting each viewer’s own security and data permissions.

items.stem: In a custom clean room collaboration template, writing the query use case as "overlap" behaves the same as writing it as "Overlap". True or false?
items.rationale: Values for enum fields such as role, useCase and type are case-sensitive, so lowercasing an accepted value like Overlap, Custom, Provider or Consumer breaks the template. Only the accepted casing is valid, whatever the surrounding JSON looks like.
items.evidence_quote: Values for enum fields such as role, useCase, and type are case-sensitive.

items.stem: As of the Winter ’26 release, filters that were applied to a dashboard when you copied its Tableau Next embed code are applied automatically when that component renders in your own web app. True or false?
items.rationale: The filters appear in the generated snippet but are not supported there, so filtering in an embedded component has to be implemented programmatically in the web app code. Budget development effort for filtering rather than assuming the copied state carries over, and remember the placeholder values in the snippet also have to be replaced.
items.evidence_quote: In Winter ‘26, these filters aren’t supported. Adding and using filters must be done programmatically in your web app code.

items.stem: A consumer follows four metrics but no insights summary ever appears on their Following page. What is the most likely cause?
options: Tableau AI has not been turned on by a Tableau admin
Insight summaries need at least five followed metrics
The followed metrics come from more than one semantic model
The user is missing the Tableau Next Platform Analyst permission set
answer: Tableau AI has not been turned on by a Tableau admin
items.rationale: Insight summaries depend on Tableau AI being enabled by an admin, so the org-level switch is the first thing to check. Two or more followed metrics is enough when the analytics agent is off, metrics from several models are fine, and an analyst permission set is not needed to consume summaries.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau AI must be turned on by your Tableau admin for insight summaries to be available.

items.stem: Where are Tableau Next Lightning web components supported?
options: Only in Lightning App Builder
In any Visualforce page
In Experience Cloud sites only
In any external web application through the embedding API
items.rationale: Support is limited to Lightning App Builder. Embedding into an external application is a separate route with its own component code, not these Lightning web components.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Next Lightning web components are only supported for Lightning App Builder.

items.stem: A client wants a Tableau Next metric on a public Experience Cloud site page that their team maintains in Experience Builder. Which statement is correct?
options: Tableau Next Lightning web components can't be added to Site pages in Experience Builder
Tableau Next components work in Experience Builder once the Embedding SDK is installed for the site
Site pages support the metric component, but not the dashboard or visualization components
Site pages support Tableau Next components once the CRM Analytics for Slack app is enabled
answer: Tableau Next Lightning web components can't be added to Site pages in Experience Builder
items.rationale: The Tableau Next Lightning web components are supported only in Lightning App Builder, so an Experience Builder site page is out of scope and the work has to go through the Embedding SDK route in a custom app instead. The SDK does not unlock Experience Builder, and the Slack app is unrelated to embedding.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Next Lightning web components are only supported for Lightning App Builder. They aren't supported in the Experience Builder for addition to Site pages.

items.stem: Sharing a Tableau Next asset can be used to give another user the owner role on it.
items.rationale: Sharing grants view or edit only. Ownership cannot be granted by sharing, which matters when the original author leaves the project.
items.evidence_quote: By sharing, you grant other users permission to view or edit an asset. You can't grant users the owner role.

items.stem: Previews never render when users paste Tableau Next links into Slack, even though Collaborate with Slack and Tableau Next is switched on. Which pair of Session Settings must be left disabled?
options: Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated, and Enforce login IP ranges on every request
Force relogin after Login-As-User, and Require HttpOnly attribute
Lock sessions to the domain in which they were first used, and Enable clickjack protection for Setup pages
Enforce login IP ranges on every request, and Enable caching and autocomplete on the login page
answer: Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated, and Enforce login IP ranges on every request
items.rationale: IP-restricting session settings break the Slack to Salesforce integration, so both of those specific settings must be off before previews appear. The other settings are real session controls but have no bearing on the Slack integration, and only one half of the fourth option is relevant.
items.evidence_quote: To resolve this, Session Settings for **Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated** and **Enforce login IP ranges on every request** must not be enabled.

items.stem: In Tableau Next, what is an analytics group created for?
options: Managing which users can reach Tableau Next assets
Grouping related metrics under a single semantic model
Partitioning Data 360 data so brands stay separate
Bundling dashboards for publication to the Marketplace
answer: Managing which users can reach Tableau Next assets
items.rationale: An analytics group is a membership container used when granting access to assets, so sharing can be done once to a group rather than user by user. Partitioning data is what a data space does, and the Marketplace is the template catalogue.
items.evidence_quote: Analytics groups help manage your users’ access to assets in Tableau Next.

items.stem: A client asks what has to be in place in their Salesforce org before Tableau Next can be used at all. What does Tableau Next depend on?
options: Data 360 and the Data 360 semantic layer
Data 360 alone, with the semantic layer needed only for AI features
