Data 360 and a Tableau Cloud site to publish content to
CRM Analytics, which Tableau Next reads its datasets from
answer: Data 360 and the Data 360 semantic layer
items.rationale: Tableau Next is not a standalone platform: it requires Data 360 for ingestion and query, and the Data 360 semantic layer, which is why creating the semantic layer is one of the enablement tasks rather than an optional extra for AI. No Tableau Cloud site is involved, and Tableau Next does not read CRM Analytics datasets.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Next requires Data 360 and the Data 360 semantic layer.

items.stem: An admin opens Tableau Next Administration to onboard ten new starters who have no Salesforce user records yet. What has to happen before those people can be given Tableau Next permission sets?
options: Their user records must be created in Salesforce first
They must be added from the Add Users page in Tableau Next Administration
They must be created in Data 360 Setup and then provisioned into Tableau Next
They must be added to an analytics group, which creates their user records
answer: Their user records must be created in Salesforce first
items.rationale: Tableau Next provisions existing Salesforce users; it cannot create them, so user creation is a Salesforce Setup task that precedes any Tableau Next assignment. The Add Users flow in Administration only provisions users who already exist, and analytics groups grant asset access rather than creating users.
items.evidence_quote: Users must already be created in Salesforce. You can’t add users in the Tableau Next app.

items.stem: An admin turns on Tableau Next Auditing so that user interaction events are collected and can later be modelled in Data 360. Name the Salesforce object those interaction events are collected in.
items.rationale: Auditing writes interaction events to the AnalyticsUserActivityEvent object, which is then connected in Data 360 and mapped to a DLO and DMO before it can be reported on. It is not exposed as a ready-made audit report inside Tableau Next.
items.evidence_quote: Turn on Auditing to collect interaction events in the AnalyticsUserActivityEvent object.

items.stem: An org has been running Data 360 under a Customer Data Platform license and now adds a Data Cloud license. What happens to the permission sets its users already hold?
options: They stop granting access to Data 360, so sets from the new license must be assigned
They are automatically replaced by the equivalent Data Cloud license permission sets
They keep working, because the new license changes only how the org is billed
They keep working for existing users, while only new users need the new sets
answer: They stop granting access to Data 360, so sets from the new license must be assigned
items.rationale: Permission sets are tied to the license that granted them, so the moment the Data Cloud license is added the old Customer Data Platform sets stop granting Data 360 access and every user has to be reassigned. Nothing migrates on its own, which is why User Access Policies are suggested to do it in bulk.
items.evidence_quote: When you add a Data Cloud license to an org that was previously operating Data 360 under a Customer Data Platform license, the permission sets granted by the Customer Data Platform license no longer grants access to Data 360.

items.stem: A custom Data 360 permission set that was made by cloning a standard one still picks up new permissions automatically as Data 360 features gain them.
items.rationale: Cloning copies the permissions that exist on the day it is cloned and nothing after that, so a custom set drifts behind each release and users silently lose access to new functionality. Only the standard permission sets are updated automatically.
items.evidence_quote: Custom permission sets aren’t automatically updated when Data Cloud features get new permissions, even if they’re created by cloning a standard Data Cloud permission set.

items.stem: A Data 360 customer holds only the standard Data Cloud license and asks which data governance capabilities they already have. Pair each capability with how it is licensed.
options: Manual tagging of data for governance
AI-assisted tagging of sensitive fields
Row-level security for unstructured data

pairs.left: Manual tagging of data for governance
pairs.right: Included with the standard Data Cloud license
Only with the Data 360 Dynamic Data Masking add-on
Not available under either license

answer: Manual tagging of data for governance::Included with the standard Data Cloud license
AI-assisted tagging of sensitive fields::Only with the Data 360 Dynamic Data Masking add-on
Row-level security for unstructured data::Not available under either license
items.rationale: Manual tagging comes with the standard license, AI-assisted tagging is one of the Dynamic Data Masking add-on features, and row-level security for unstructured data is the row in the licensing table marked No in both columns, so it cannot be bought at all. Row-level security on structured data is included, which is what makes the unstructured case easy to promise by mistake.
items.evidence_quote: | Governance Capability | Included with Data CLOUD | Included in Dynamic Data Masking | | --- | --- | --- | | OLS / FLS / RLS (Structured) | Yes | No | | RLS with Joins (Structured) | Yes | No | | OLS / FLS (Unstructured) | Yes | No | | Manual Tagging | Yes | No | | AI-Assisted Tagging | No | Yes | | RLS for Unstructured Data | No | No |

items.stem: During guided Tableau Next setup an admin runs the Turn On AI Features step. Which things does that single step take care of?
options: Configuring Data 360 connections
Enabling Einstein and Agentforce
Creating a Tableau Agent
Activating semantic authoring and metric insight summaries
Importing records from standard objects into Data 360
Applying the default record-level access policies for standard objects
answer: Activating semantic authoring and metric insight summaries
items.rationale: The AI step does the whole Einstein and Agentforce chain in one go, including creating the agent and switching on semantic authoring and metric insight summaries. Loading records from standard objects and choosing record-level access policies are the two separate later steps of guided setup, Connect Standard Objects and Secure Your Data.
items.evidence_quote: AI setup configures Data 360 connections, enables Einstein and Agentforce, creates a Tableau Agent, assigns admins agent access permissions, and activates Tableau Next features including semantic authoring and metric insight summaries.

items.stem: An analyst needs to create and change content freely in their own dedicated environment, but must only be able to look at what is in the production environment. Which Tableau Next standard permission set matches that requirement?
options: Tableau Unmetered Self-Service Analyst
Tableau Unmetered Platform Analyst
Tableau Unmetered Self-Service Consumer
Tableau Unmetered Admin
items.rationale: The Self-Service Analyst set is the one that pairs edit rights in a personal org with view-only rights in production. Platform Analyst can edit in production, Admin can edit and configure everything, and Self-Service Consumer cannot author at all.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Unmetered Self-Service Analyst | Allows edit access to Tableau Next features in personal orgs and view-only access in production org.

items.stem: Turning on Tableau Next also assigns the person who enabled it which permission sets?
options: Data Cloud Architect
Tableau Unmetered Admin
Tableau Next Consumer
Data Cloud Marketing Manager
items.rationale: Enablement self-assigns these two, which is why the admin who switched it on can immediately configure both Data 360 and Tableau Next while colleagues still see nothing.
items.evidence_quote: This also assigns you a Data Cloud Architect and Tableau Unmetered Admin permission set.

items.stem: A security review insists that the Data 360 team must not be able to reach Salesforce Setup functionality, yet they still need full access to Data 360 features. What does Salesforce tell you to do about the Data Cloud Architect permission set?
options: Clone it and remove the Customize Application permission
Assign it alongside a permission set that denies Setup access
Swap it for the Data Cloud Activation Manager permission set
Remove its Manage All Data Space definition permission
answer: Clone it and remove the Customize Application permission
items.rationale: Data Cloud Architect carries Customize Application, which is what opens up Setup, so the documented route is to clone the set and strip that one permission. Permission sets are additive and cannot deny anything, and Activation Manager has no access to Data Cloud Setup, data spaces or the semantic layer, so it is not a substitute for an architect.
items.evidence_quote: Data Cloud Architect grants users the Customize Application permission. To restrict access to Setup functionality, clone this permisison set and remove this permission.

items.stem: An org has bought 250 Tableau Next Creator licenses and wants a Personal Org for every one of those users. At most how many Personal Orgs can that org have?
items.rationale: The org-wide ceiling is the lower of 100 or the number of Creator licenses, so 250 licenses still stop at 100 Personal Orgs. The per-user rule of one Personal Org each does not raise that org-level cap.
items.evidence_quote: The total number of Personal Orgs allowed in an organization is limited to the lower of: 100 or the total number of Creator licenses in the organization.

items.stem: In a Data 360 org that uses policy-based governance, an admin clones a permission set so a group of CRM users can see a related list enrichment. What does that clone need that the standard permission set did not?
options: Manual enrollment in the data governance policy through Data Space Management
A record-level permit policy authored on each data model object it reads
The Customize Application permission, so that it can query DMOs
Registration as an additive permission set in Policy Builder
answer: Manual enrollment in the data governance policy through Data Space Management
items.rationale: In a policy-based governance org the governance policy knows about the standard permission sets, so anything cloned or custom has to be enrolled in the policy by hand in Data Space Management after it is created. Giving it the data space and the access level is not enough on its own, and no policy is authored per object to make a permission set work.
items.evidence_quote: In policy-based governance orgs, any cloned or custom permission set must be manually enrolled in the data governance policy via Data Cloud Setup –> Data Space Management after creation.

items.stem: Data 360 data governance policies restrict access at three different levels. Pair each level with the restriction it expresses.
options: Object-Level Security (OLS)
Field-Level Security (FLS)
Record-Level Security (RLS)

pairs.right: Make the Customer_Orders object available only to the Sales department
Hide the Credit Card Number field from users outside the finance team
Show a user only the customer records from their region or the ones they own

answer: Object-Level Security (OLS)::Make the Customer_Orders object available only to the Sales department
Field-Level Security (FLS)::Hide the Credit Card Number field from users outside the finance team
Record-Level Security (RLS)::Show a user only the customer records from their region or the ones they own
items.rationale: OLS decides whether the whole object is reachable, FLS hides individual columns, and RLS filters which rows a user sees by comparing the object with attributes of the logged-in user.
items.evidence_quote: **Object-Level Security (OLS):** The Customer_Orders object is accessible to users in the Sales department who are assigned to the appropriate data space. **Field-Level Security (FLS):** Hide the Credit Card Number field for users outside the finance team. **Record-Level Security (RLS):** Show customer records from a specific region to a user, or display only the records they own by comparing data from the protected object with attributes of the logged-in user.

items.stem: Which interface must be used to submit a Data Deletion (right to be forgotten) request for an individual data profile in Data 360?
items.rationale: Data Deletion requests for individual profiles are only accepted through the Consent API, so a client expecting a button in Data Explorer or a Policy Builder rule has to be redirected to an API integration.
items.evidence_quote: You can submit Data Deletion requests of individual data profiles in Data 360. All requests must be submitted using the Consent API.

items.stem: In Data 360, what determines which data spaces a given user can view and work in?
options: The permission sets assigned to the user
Sharing rules defined on each data lake object
The user's position in the Salesforce role hierarchy
The data space prefix carried in the object's API name
answer: The permission sets assigned to the user
items.rationale: Data space access is granted by associating permission sets with data spaces. The data space prefix only distinguishes object API names across spaces, and role hierarchy is used by record-level policies, not by data space assignment.
items.evidence_quote: Control access to data spaces with permission sets.

items.stem: A client with three consumer brands asks what a data space in Data 360 actually is. Which description is correct?
options: A logical partition that organizes data within a single Data 360 instance
A separate Data 360 instance provisioned per brand, region or department
A permission set that grants object-level access to Data 360 features
A container in Tableau Next that groups analytics assets for one team
answer: A logical partition that organizes data within a single Data 360 instance
items.rationale: A data space partitions data, metadata and processes inside one Data 360 instance; it is not a second instance, and it is not the permission set that later grants access to it, nor a Tableau Next workspace.
items.evidence_quote: A data space is a logical partition to organize your data for profile unification, insights, and marketing in Data 360.

items.stem: An author builds data assets in a Tableau Next workspace and never touches any data space setting. Which data space do those assets end up in?
options: The Default data space
A new data space named after the workspace
The data space associated with the author's permission set
No data space, until an administrator assigns one
items.rationale: Tableau Next places assets in the Default data space and only moves them if you deliberately add them to another data space that exists in Data 360; permission sets control access to spaces, they do not decide where a new asset lands.
items.evidence_quote: The app places your assets in the Default data space.

items.stem: Which Data 360 objects are data space aware, so that access to them can be scoped per data space?
options: Data lake objects (DLOs)
Data model objects (DMOs)
Calculated insight objects (CIOs)
Data graphs
Data streams
Data kits
items.rationale: The data space aware object list is DLOs, DMOs, CIOs and data graphs. Data streams and data kits are not on that list, so their visibility is governed through the objects they produce rather than by data space scope.
items.evidence_quote: These objects are data space aware. Data lake objects (DLOs) Data model objects (DMOs) Calculated insight objects (CIOs) Data graphs

items.stem: The standard Data Cloud and Customer Data Platform licenses include only a single data space, so an add-on license must be purchased before a second data space can be created.
items.rationale: Data space segregation is licensed: the standard licenses are limited to one space and additional spaces need the Data Spaces add-on, which is a commercial dependency to raise in scoping.
items.evidence_quote: The standard Data Cloud and Customer Data Platform licenses are limited to just one data space. To create additional data spaces, you must purchase an add-on license.

items.stem: When Data 360 is enabled, the default data space is automatically associated with the standard Data Cloud permission sets, with one exception. Which permission set is left out of that automatic association?
options: Data Cloud Architect
Data Cloud Activation Manager
Data Cloud Activation Specialist
Data Cloud User
items.rationale: The Architect permission set is the documented exception, so an architect who needs to work in the default space must be associated with it manually. The other standard permission sets - Activation Manager, Activation Specialist and Data Cloud User - are associated out of the box.
items.evidence_quote: When Data Cloud is enabled, the default data space is associated with standard Data Cloud permission sets, except the Data Cloud Architect.

items.stem: Inside one permission set, an admin clears the View setting for Segmentation in the feature permissions of a single data space. Where does that restriction take effect?
options: Only within that data space
In every data space associated with the permission set
In every permission set that carries the same object permissions
Across the whole org, overriding object permissions everywhere
items.rationale: Feature permissions are set per data space inside a permission set and act only there, whereas object permissions on the permission set apply to all of its associated data spaces by default.
items.evidence_quote: Feature permissions act only within the data space they’re set for.

items.stem: A record-level security policy authored on a DMO governs that object in only one data space. What makes the policy's reach that narrow?
options: The object's API name carries the data space prefix the policy is authored against
Feature permissions in a permission set act inside a single data space only
The policy is packaged inside that data space's local data kit
Policy Builder is opened from within one data space's setup pages
answer: The object's API name carries the data space prefix the policy is authored against
items.rationale: Policies are written against the API name, and a data space prefix is baked into that name, so the same DMO in another space is a different API name and is not covered. Feature permissions and data kits are separate mechanisms.
items.evidence_quote: When you create an record-level security policy (RLS) on a DMO or calculated insight object, the policy applies only to the data space where the object is available. This is because the API name includes the data space prefix, and policies are authored based on this API name.

items.stem: Record-level security policies filter the rows visible to a user while that user is creating a segment or a calculated insight in Data 360.
items.rationale: Segment and calculated insight creation runs in system context, so RLS is not enforced there; restriction has to be reasoned about at query and consumption time instead of assuming a segment inherits the author's row filter.
items.evidence_quote: RLS policies aren’t enforced when creating segments and calculated insights because these operations run in system context.

items.stem: A record-level security policy in Data 360 filters rows by comparing a field on the protected object with an attribute of the logged-in user. Which user attributes are supported for that comparison?
options: User ID
Role ID
Org ID
Profile ID
Permission Set ID
Queue ID
items.rationale: The supported attributes are the user's ID, role ID and org ID, all held as 18-character Salesforce IDs. Profile, permission set and queue IDs are not offered, so a design that needs profile-based filtering has to model that data as a joinable lookup instead.
items.evidence_quote: All supported attributes are Salesforce IDs stored in 18-character format: User ID – Unique ID of the logged-in user Role ID – User’s Salesforce role Org ID – User’s Salesforce organization

items.stem: A data space prefix in Data 360 must start with a letter and becomes part of the API name of every object in that space. At most how many alphanumeric characters can the prefix contain?
items.rationale: The prefix is capped at three alphanumeric characters and cannot be changed after saving, so the naming convention has to be agreed before any data space is created.
items.evidence_quote: Enter a unique data space prefix, starting with a letter and including up to three alphanumeric characters.

items.stem: A customer wants control of the key material behind Data 360 encryption but refuses to operate an AWS KMS account, preferring to supply the material through the Salesforce UI. Which key management option fits?
options: Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)
External Key Management (EKM)
Customer Managed Keys (CMK)
Cache-Only Key Service
items.rationale: BYOK takes customer-supplied key material directly in the Salesforce UI with no AWS KMS account. EKM is the option that requires an external AWS KMS account, and CMK has Salesforce generate and manage the tenant-specific keys.
items.evidence_quote: | Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) | Customers can bring their own key material directly into the Salesforce UI without needing an AWS KMS account.

rows: Salesforce generates and manages tenant-specific keys in the Salesforce UI.

Customers can bring their own key material directly into the Salesforce UI without needing an AWS KMS account. This option benefits customers who prefer not to access AWS KMS or use other key storage providers such as Azure or on-premise vaults.

items.stem: In Data 360 Policy Builder, at most how many conditions can a single record-level security policy contain?
items.rationale: A record-level security policy accepts up to five conditions, grouped and combined with AND/OR, so a rule needing more tests has to be split or pushed into a join against a lookup table.
items.evidence_quote: You can add up to five conditions to a record-level security (RLS) policy.

items.stem: A user already holds View All Records and Modify All Records on a data-space-aware object. What else is required before that user can use features and resources that are scoped to a particular data space?
options: They must be explicitly assigned to the space through Data Cloud Data Space Management
They must also be granted a record-level permit policy on that object
The data space must first be shared with a connected companion org
They must be assigned the Data Spaces add-on license on their user record
answer: They must be explicitly assigned to the space through Data Cloud Data Space Management
items.rationale: System-level permissions such as VAR and MAR do not associate a user with a data space; they may still allow querying data-space-aware objects, but data space assignment continues to gate data-space-scoped features and admin operations.
items.evidence_quote: To access Data Space-scoped features and resources, users must be explicitly assigned through Data Cloud Data Space Management.

items.stem: Name the Data 360 capability that lets you add a foundation model that is hosted on an external platform and connect it with AI Models, so the model can be used to create a model configuration that powers generative AI. Give the capability's name or its acronym.
answer: Bring Your Own Large Language Model
items.rationale: Bring Your Own Large Language Model (BYOLLM) is the capability for registering an externally hosted foundation model against AI Models. It is distinct from Bring Your Own Model (BYOM), which connects external predictive ML models such as SageMaker or Vertex AI models.
items.evidence_quote: The Bring Your Own Large Language Model (BYOLLM) capability enables you to add a foundation model hosted on an external platform and connect it with AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio).

items.stem: Conversational analytics in Tableau Agent is delivered by the Data Analysis subagent. On which surfaces can business users reach it?
options: Tableau Next
Salesforce
Slack
Tableau Cloud
Tableau Server
items.rationale: The Data Analysis subagent is described as meeting business users across Tableau Next, Salesforce and Slack, and the supported-surfaces page breaks those three down into Lightning and dashboard pages, Salesforce home, record and mobile, and Slack cards, channels and threads. Tableau Cloud and Tableau Server are the classic Tableau platforms and neither hosts the Data Analysis subagent.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Agent with the Data Analysis subagent is a deeply integrated, intelligent layer for conversational analytics, built to meet business users where they work, across Tableau Next, Salesforce, and Slack.

items.stem: Users query a product knowledge base both with loosely worded questions and with exact model codes such as LaserPrinter TX 440. Which Data 360 search index type is designed to serve both kinds of query?
options: Hybrid search
Vector search
Enriched indexing
An ensemble retriever
items.rationale: Hybrid search combines semantically aware vector search with the precision and speed of keyword search, which is what exact model codes need. Vector search alone handles meaning but matches numbers and domain terms poorly; enriched indexing adds generated metadata to chunks and an ensemble retriever combines retrievers rather than index types.
items.evidence_quote: In Data 360, hybrid search combines the strengths of semantically aware vector search with the precision and speed of keyword search.

items.stem: A client's team works in external AI assistants such as ChatGPT or Claude and wants those tools to answer from the company's governed Tableau Next semantic models without exporting the data. Which capability is built for that?
options: Tableau Next Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
Semantic Model AI Optimization
A Data 360 ensemble retriever
Tableau Agent in Slack
answer: Tableau Next Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
items.rationale: The MCP Server connects governed analytics, metadata and semantic models to external MCP-compliant AI agents without moving data. Semantic Model AI Optimization only assesses a model, an ensemble retriever searches Data 360 indexes, and Tableau Agent in Slack is still a Salesforce-hosted surface rather than an external AI client.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Next Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects your Tableau Next governed analytics, metadata, and semantic models to external MCP-compliant AI agents such as ChatGPT or Claude.

items.stem: What does Semantic Model AI Optimization produce when it runs against a semantic model?
options: An overall model health rating of Low, Moderate, or High, with the issues and suggested resolutions behind it
A test run of sample questions with a pass or fail verdict for each question asked
A generated set of field descriptions written directly into the model without review
A lineage diagram showing which data lake objects feed each semantic object
answer: An overall model health rating of Low, Moderate, or High, with the issues and suggested resolutions behind it
items.rationale: The feature runs automated checks and calculates an overall model health categorised as Low, Moderate or High, presented with rules, issues and suggested resolutions. Question-by-question testing is what semantic model testing does, and AI-generated descriptions are a separate capability.
items.evidence_quote: Semantic Model AI Optimization runs a series of automated checks against your semantic model and calculates an overall model health, which is categorized as Low, Moderate, or High.

items.stem: A client asks what Tableau Agent for Tableau Next actually is. Which answer describes it correctly?
options: A collection of pre-built agentic capabilities for conversational analytics, proactive insights, and automated data prep and semantic modeling
A workspace in Data 360 for building, training, and activating predictive machine learning models
An open standard that lets external AI clients query governed analytics assets and metadata
A generative AI notebook for uploading content, researching sources, and generating reports
answer: A collection of pre-built agentic capabilities for conversational analytics, proactive insights, and automated data prep and semantic modeling
items.rationale: Tableau Agent is a bundle of pre-built agentic capabilities spanning conversational analytics, proactive insights and automated data prep or semantic modeling. AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio) is the predictive modeling home, the Model Context Protocol is the open standard for external clients, and Notebook AI is the research notebook.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Agent for Tableau Next (formerly known as Agentforce for Analytics) is a collection of pre-built agentic capabilities that enable conversational analytics, deliver proactive insights, and automate data prep and semantic modeling.

items.stem: A prompt needs the most relevant content pulled from several searches across different data sources at once, not from a single one. Which kind of retriever fits?
options: An ensemble retriever
An individual retriever
A dynamic retriever
A default retriever
items.rationale: An ensemble retriever is a collection of individual retrievers, run together so results from multiple searches or data sources are combined and reranked. An individual retriever retrieves from a single search index; a dynamic retriever is only a placeholder for a value supplied by the prompt template at run time; a default retriever is a non-customisable retriever that Data 360 no longer creates for new search indexes.
items.evidence_quote: Use ensemble retrievers to get the most relevant information from multiple searches or data sources.

items.stem: You are building a custom individual retriever in AI Models so that a prompt gets more relevant content back. Which Data 360 object do you have to choose for the retriever, alongside setting its filters and its returned fields?
options: A search index
A data stream
A calculated insight
A prompt template
items.rationale: A custom individual retriever is configured on top of a search index, plus filters and the fields it returns. A prompt template consumes the retriever rather than being an input to it, and data streams and calculated insights are ingestion and modelling objects, not retriever inputs.
items.evidence_quote: To customize the retriever, select its search index, define filters, and specify what information it returns.

items.stem: Salesforce gives alternative names for predictors in its predictive AI documentation. Which names does it say mean the same thing?
options: Predictor variables
Independent variables
Dependent variables
Response variables
Target variables
items.rationale: Predictors are the inputs, so the synonyms are the input-side names. Dependent, response and target all describe the thing being predicted, which is the opposite side of the equation.
items.evidence_quote: Predictors are also known as predictor variables or independent variables.

items.stem: A search index over unstructured data creates citations for the content chunks it indexes. What are those citations for?
options: Checking that an AI answer grounded in that content is accurate
Recording which users have read each document
Tracking how often each chunk is retrieved, for tuning
Attributing the content to its copyright holder
answer: Checking that an AI answer grounded in that content is accurate
items.rationale: Citations exist so a reader can follow a generated answer back to the page or timestamp it came from and see for themselves. That is a verification mechanism, not usage tracking or rights management.
items.evidence_quote: Verify the accuracy of AI responses grounded in your unstructured data with inline citations for content chunks.

items.stem: A regulated client asks what Data 360 gives them for auditing an AI model. What does model lineage provide?
options: A traceable history of the model's lifecycle, from training data through to live use
A record of every prediction the model has returned, with the inputs behind it
A comparison of the model's accuracy against the version it replaced
A log of which users have run the model, and when each run happened
answer: A traceable history of the model's lifecycle, from training data through to live use
items.rationale: Lineage traces the model rather than its outputs, which is what makes work reproducible and auditable. A per-prediction log is a different thing and is not what lineage offers.
items.evidence_quote: Model lineage provides a traceable history of an AI model's lifecycle, from training data, versioning, deployment, and its use with live data.

items.stem: Model Builder raises quality alerts against a model. What does it detect them from?
options: The model's training data
The model's quality metrics
Cross-validation
The model's live prediction volume
Feedback submitted by users on predictions
items.rationale: All three sources are available before the model is in use, which is the point: quality alerts are meant to be addressed while a model is being built rather than after it has been making decisions.
items.evidence_quote: Model Builder displays quality alerts when it detects issues in your model's training data, quality metrics, or during cross-validation.

items.stem: A data science team has trained and deployed a churn model on Amazon SageMaker. The business wants Data 360 to consume its predictions without duplicating Salesforce data into the machine learning platform. Which Data 360 capability is built for that?
options: Bring Your Own Model (BYOM)
Query federation
Intelligent Context
A streaming insight paired with a data action
items.rationale: BYOM connects a model already built and deployed on an external platform to Data 360 using a zero-copy approach, so the platform reads Salesforce data in place and the predictions come back for use in profiles and segments. Query federation leaves external data in place but has nothing to do with models, Intelligent Context builds search index configurations, and a streaming insight computes its own aggregates rather than calling out to a trained model.
items.evidence_quote: Bring Your Own Model (BYOM) lets you connect models built in external platforms with Data 360. BYOM provides direct access to Salesforce data in external ML platforms and uses a zero-copy approach, which eliminates the need to duplicate data.

items.stem: Put the stages of a Data 360 hybrid search into the sequence in which they happen when a query is run.
options: Retrieve results from the keyword index and from the vector index
Merge the two sets of results into one
Rerank the merged results with the ranking model
answer: Retrieve results from the keyword index and from the vector index
Merge the two sets of results into one
Rerank the merged results with the ranking model
items.rationale: Hybrid search first retrieves from both the keyword and the vector index on similarity to the query, then fuses those results, and only then does the ranking model rerank the merged list. Reranking is not applied to each index separately before merging.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 Hybrid search retrieves results from two indexes—keyword and vector— based on the similarity with the query and then merges (fuses) the results. The ranking model then reranks the merged results.

items.stem: An externally hosted foundation model has been connected to AI Models and given a model configuration. What is Model Playground used for at that point?
options: Trying prompts against the configuration and judging the responses it generates before production
Establishing the endpoint connection between the external model provider and Salesforce
Training a predictive model on Data 360 data without writing any code
Building the vector search index that grounds prompts in unstructured data
answer: Trying prompts against the configuration and judging the responses it generates before production
items.rationale: Model Playground is where you test prompts and hyperparameter settings and evaluate the generated responses before the model goes into production. Making the endpoint connection is the separate act of adding the foundation model, and model training and search indexing are different features entirely.
items.evidence_quote: Before you put a model into production, test it using prompts in Model Playground to evaluate the generated responses based on your model’s hyperparameter settings.

items.stem: Salesforce has renamed several Tableau Next AI features. Match each earlier name to the name now used for it.
options: Agentforce for Analytics
Concierge: Analytics Q&A
Data Pro

pairs.right: Tableau Agent
The conversational analytics capability in Tableau Agent
Semantic Modeling

answer: Concierge: Analytics Q&A::The conversational analytics capability in Tableau Agent
items.rationale: Agentforce for Analytics became Tableau Agent, Concierge: Analytics Q&A became the conversational analytics capability inside it, and Data Pro terms are being renamed to Semantic Modeling. Mixing these up leads consultants to describe conversational analytics as a separate product rather than a capability of Tableau Agent.
items.evidence_quote: Starting in July '26, Agentforce for Analytics in Tableau Next is now called Tableau Agent. Concierge: Analytics Q&A is now referred to as the conversational analytics capability in Tableau Agent. We're also gradually renaming select Data Pro terms to Semantic Modeling.

items.stem: Which qualities does an AI-ready semantic model have, so that agents can reliably interpret business context from it?
options: Clear labels
Complete descriptions
Low ambiguity
Consistent metadata
Row-level security predicates on every object
A published dashboard for every metric
Materialized aggregates for each measure
items.rationale: AI readiness is defined as clear labels, complete descriptions, low ambiguity and consistent metadata. Row-level security, published dashboards and materialized aggregates are real platform concerns but none of them is part of the AI-readiness definition.
items.evidence_quote: An AI-ready model has clear labels, complete descriptions, low ambiguity, and consistent metadata.

items.stem: Tableau Agent bundles several capabilities. Which description matches its conversational analytics capability rather than one of the others?
options: Business users ask freeform questions about metrics and dashboards built on a semantic model and get answers in text and charts
Analytics and data stewards conversationally curate and create semantic objects while authoring a semantic model
Business users conversationally set up alerts that trigger on conditions they choose for metrics they care about
Admins conversationally scope which semantic models and assets an agent may use when it answers
answer: Business users ask freeform questions about metrics and dashboards built on a semantic model and get answers in text and charts
items.rationale: Conversational analytics is question-and-answer over analytics assets that sit on a semantic model, returned as rich text and visualizations. Curating semantic objects belongs to the data preparation and semantic modeling capability, and condition-based notifications belong to proactive insights and alerts.
items.evidence_quote: Business users can ask freeform questions about analytics assets (such as metrics and dashboards) based on a semantic model to get trusted answers from their data in rich text and visualizations.

items.stem: Put the stages of preparing content for retrieval from a Data 360 search index into the order in which they happen.
options: Loading the content
Chunking the content
Vectorizing the chunks
Storing the content in a search-optimized way
answer: Storing the content in a search-optimized way
items.rationale: Data preparation for retrieval runs loading, then chunking, then vectorizing, then storing in a search-optimized way. Vectorizing before chunking is the common misconception, but embeddings are generated from the chunks.
items.evidence_quote: Data preparation for retrieval from a search index involves loading, chunking, vectorizing, and storing content in a search-optimized way.

items.stem: A semantic model has several fields whose labels and descriptions overlap, and the agent returns inconsistent answers as a result. Which Semantic Model AI Optimization check surfaces that problem?
options: Similar Meanings (Beta)
Missing Description
Missing Relationships
Model Health
items.rationale: Similar Meanings uses AI to detect synonyms, acronyms and semantic overlaps that create ambiguity. Missing Description looks for absent descriptions rather than duplicated ones, Missing Relationships flags disconnected objects, and Model Health is the overall rating the checks roll up into, not a check itself.
items.evidence_quote: The Similar Meanings (Beta) feature uses AI to detect synonyms, acronyms, and semantic overlaps to prevent ambiguity.

items.stem: A custom retriever in Data 360 can keep several of its versions active at the same time, so different prompt templates can each be pointed at a different version.
items.rationale: Editing and saving a custom retriever creates a new version, and although many versions can exist, only one of them is active at any moment, so prompt templates all resolve to the same active version.
items.evidence_quote: You can create multiple versions, but you can have only one version active at a time.

items.stem: A retriever runs on behalf of a user who has no access to one of the source records behind the indexed content. What happens to that record?
options: It is left out of what the retriever returns
It is returned to the prompt with its field values masked
It is returned, and the check is applied when the LLM answers
The retriever stops and returns a permission error to the caller
answer: It is left out of what the retriever returns
items.rationale: Retrievers apply the data governance policies and run access checks on the results, so an inaccessible source record simply does not appear in the results. It is not masked, not deferred to the LLM step, and it does not fail the whole retriever call.
items.evidence_quote: If the AI agent or user calling the retriever doesn’t have access to the source record, it doesn’t appear in the retriever results.

items.stem: How does Data 360 build the chunks for a search index?
options: It splits the content into sentences, then merges them into chunks up to the max token limit
It cuts the content at the max token limit wherever that falls
It splits on paragraph breaks and discards paragraphs over the limit
It sends the whole document to the embedding model, which decides the boundaries
answer: It splits the content into sentences, then merges them into chunks up to the max token limit
items.rationale: Sentences are the unit, so a chunk boundary never lands mid-sentence. That is why raising the max token limit produces fewer, larger chunks rather than differently cut ones.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 separates sentences in your content and then merges the sentences into chunks based on your specified max token setting.

items.stem: A search index configuration is created in Data 360 and the chunking strategy is left alone. What is the default max token limit for a chunk?
items.rationale: 512 by default. The limit controls how much text lands in a chunk, and Salesforce advises a lower setting for non-Latin-based content, so the default is a starting point rather than a ceiling that suits every corpus.
items.evidence_quote: In Data 360, the max token limit is set to 512 by default.

items.stem: Predictive AI in Data 360 uses four terms that are easy to blur together. Pair each with its meaning.

pairs.right: A custom statistical tool built from past results with known outcomes
A derived value representing a possible future business outcome
The conditions that most strongly drive that outcome
A suggested action a user can take to improve that outcome

answer: Predictive model::A custom statistical tool built from past results with known outcomes
Prediction::A derived value representing a possible future business outcome
Top predictors::The conditions that most strongly drive that outcome
Prescription::A suggested action a user can take to improve that outcome
items.rationale: The model produces the prediction, the top predictors explain it, and the prescription is the only one of the four that asks a person to do something. Prescriptions attach to variables a user can actually influence, such as shipping method, which is what separates them from predictors in general.
items.evidence_quote: A predictive model is a custom statistical tool that predicts future business outcomes based on trends and patterns in past results, plus current business data. A prediction is a derived value, produced by a predictive model, that represents a possible future business outcome. Top predictors are the conditions that most significantly drive the predicted outcome. A prescription is a suggested action that a user can take to improve the predicted outcome.

items.stem: A prediction request asks for top predictors to be returned alongside the prediction. In what order do they come back?
options: Decreasing order of magnitude
The order the variables appear in the data model object
Alphabetically by variable name
Increasing order of magnitude, so the strongest is last
items.rationale: Strongest first, which means an interface can take the first two or three and show them without sorting anything. Top predictors are also optional: they are returned only if the request asks for them.
items.evidence_quote: If requested, top predictors are returned from a predictive model in decreasing order of magnitude.

items.stem: A team is about to ingest unstructured data and build search indexes over it. Which permission set does Salesforce name for that work?
options: Data Cloud Architect
Data Cloud Activation Specialist
Data Cloud Activation Manager
Data Cloud User
items.rationale: Architect, the same set required to set Data 360 up in the first place. The activation-facing permission sets govern segments and activations and do not extend to ingesting unstructured data or indexing it.
items.evidence_quote:
| To ingest unstructured data and create search indexes | 
One of these permission sets:

-   Data Cloud Architect

rows: To ingest unstructured data and create search indexes

items.stem: Model Builder reports an area under the curve figure for a model. What does that figure measure?
options: How well the model separates two classes, such as yes and no
How much of the variation in the outcome the model explains
How far the model's predictions sit from the actual values on average
How evenly the training data was split between classes
answer: How well the model separates two classes, such as yes and no
items.rationale: AUC belongs to binary classification and measures discrimination between a positive and a negative class. The other options describe R squared, error measures and class balance, all real ideas that AUC is not.
items.evidence_quote: Area under the curve (AUC) is a performance metric for binary classification. It measures the ability of a model to distinguish between two classes: positive and negative (true and false, yes and no, and so on).

items.stem: What a citation carries depends on the kind of file the chunk came from. Pair each file type with what its citation includes.

pairs.right: Page number and file type
Page number, page name and file type
Start and end time stamps, and file type
File type only

answer: Excel::Page number, page name and file type
Audio and video files::Start and end time stamps, and file type
items.rationale: Excel is the one that carries a name as well as a number, because a sheet has both. Anything outside the named formats gets the file type alone, so a citation cannot point a reader to a location inside it.
items.evidence_quote: | PDF | Page number, file type | | Excel | Page number, page name, and file type | | PowerPoint | Page number, file type | | Audio and video files | Start and end time stamps, file type | | Other file formats | File type |

rows: Page number, page name, and file type
Start and end time stamps, file type

items.stem: The Integrations tab of an AI model lists the channels through which it is used for inference. Which channels appear there?
options: Batch data transforms that use the AI node
Flows that reference the model through Data 360 actions
Predict jobs, whether streaming or batch
Personalization Maps using predictions in targeting rules
Segments that filter on the model's output
Dashboards that display the model's predictions
answer: Batch data transforms that use the AI node
Flows that reference the model through Data 360 actions
Predict jobs, whether streaming or batch
Personalization Maps using predictions in targeting rules
items.rationale: Four channels, all of them places where inference actually happens. A segment or a dashboard reads values the model already produced, so neither is an inference channel and neither appears in the tab.
items.evidence_quote: You can view these inference channels in the Integrations tab. Batch Data Transforms: Data transforms that use the AI node for inferences. Flows: Flows that reference the model by using Data 360 actions. Predict jobs: Streaming or batch jobs used for inferences. Personalization Maps: Predictions from models used in Salesforce Personalization targeting rules to refine personalization decisions.

items.stem: With data masking enabled in the Model Playground prompt settings, data is kept inside the Einstein Trust Layer rather than reaching third-party large language models during testing.
items.rationale: The Playground setting does two things: it stops data leaving the Trust Layer for a third-party model while testing, and it masks sensitive data in the response. Turning it off is what lets that data travel.
items.evidence_quote: When enabled, data masking prevents data from leaving the Einstein Trust Layer to third-party large language models during testing and masks all sensitive data in a prompt response.

items.stem: A user holds the Data Cloud User permission set and needs to work with models in AI Models. What can they do?
options: Use a model, including getting predictions and improvements from it
Create and update models, but not delete or activate them
Activate an existing model, but not create one
View model metadata only, with no ability to get predictions
answer: Use a model, including getting predictions and improvements from it
items.rationale: Data Cloud User is the consumption-side grant: run the model and read what it returns. Creating, updating, deleting and activating all sit with Data Cloud Architect, so a project that expects analysts to build models has the wrong permission set.
items.evidence_quote: | Data Cloud User | Restricted access to use a model, including getting predictions and improvements derived from a model. |

items.stem: A search index configuration is already in place and the team wants to change it. What can be changed on an existing configuration?
options: Fields and file extensions for chunking can be added; other settings are read-only
Any setting can be changed, and the index rebuilds automatically
Only the max token limit can be changed
Nothing; a new configuration has to be created and the old one deleted
answer: Fields and file extensions for chunking can be added; other settings are read-only
items.rationale: Editing is additive only. Everything else can be viewed but not modified, so a decision like the chunking strategy is effectively made once and has to be got right before the index is built.
items.evidence_quote: If needed, you can edit Data 360 search index configurations to add fields or file extensions for chunking. You can view but not modify other existing settings.

items.stem: A semantic model powers working dashboards, but Tableau Agent will not answer questions grounded in it. Which prerequisite is most likely missing?
options: A user with Semantic Model editing permission has not turned the model on in the Analytics Agent Readiness dialog box
The model has not been listed as a template in the Tableau Next Marketplace
The model's data connection has not had acceleration turned on with Full Refresh
The model's metrics have not been given a sentiment and an aggregation
answer: A user with Semantic Model editing permission has not turned the model on in the Analytics Agent Readiness dialog box
items.rationale: Any semantic model the agent queries must first be enabled for use in Tableau Next, and only a user with Semantic Model editing permission can do that. Marketplace listing, acceleration and metric sentiment all affect other things and none of them gates agent access.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Agent requires that any semantic model it queries is enabled for use in Tableau Next. A Tableau Next user who has Semantic Model editing permission must enable the semantic model in the Analytics Agent Readiness dialog box.

items.stem: A business user asks Tableau Agent with the Data Analysis subagent a question about a metric. What does the agent generate and run in order to answer?
options: A semantic query against the underlying semantic model of the metric or dashboard
A SOQL query against the Salesforce object that the metric was built from
A SQL query issued directly against the data lake objects in Data 360
A refresh of the calculated insight that supplies the metric's values
answer: A semantic query against the underlying semantic model of the metric or dashboard
items.rationale: Tableau Agent uses one query path: it generates a semantic query against the semantic model behind the associated metric or dashboard, then narrates and visualizes the output. It does not bypass the semantic layer with SOQL or raw SQL, and it does not re-run calculated insights.
items.evidence_quote: Tableau Agent generates and runs a semantic query against the underlying semantic model of an associated metric or dashboard.

items.stem: A client wants Inspector proactive data alerts to tell them within minutes of a Tableau Next metric breaching a condition. What should you tell them about how often those conditions are evaluated?
options: The conditions are checked up to once per day
The conditions are checked up to once per hour
The conditions are checked every time the metric's data refreshes
The conditions are evaluated continuously as data streams into Data 360
answer: The conditions are checked up to once per day
items.rationale: Inspector evaluates alert conditions at most daily, so it cannot support minute-level or refresh-driven notification. Promising near-real-time alerting on this feature would mis-scope the work.
items.evidence_quote: Inspector checks the conditions up to once per day, and if the conditions are met, a notification is sent to channels chosen by your admin.

items.stem: Using the Data Connection and Analytics Creation template, Tableau Agent discovers data and generates visualizations from natural language questions. Which visualizations can it currently produce?
options: Bar charts and line charts only
Bar, line, and pie charts only
Any chart type that Visualization Builder offers
Only the chart type already defined on the semantic model's metrics
answer: Bar charts and line charts only
items.rationale: The template's stated limitation is that only bar and line charts are supported, so anything else has to be built by hand afterwards in Visualization Builder. The agent can create the underlying assets, including semantic models, but that does not widen the chart types it generates.
items.evidence_quote: Review these limitations before using the Data Connection and Analytics Creation template in Tableau Agent: Duplicate tables or missing join key relationships can affect the generated assets and the agent's analysis. Only bar charts and line charts are currently supported.

items.stem: Agent Scoping gives a Tableau Agent a fallback list of semantic models to search. How many models or fewer does Salesforce recommend selecting, to improve the agent's accuracy?
items.rationale: The page sets no hard cap on the fallback list - it says any number can be added - but names 10 or fewer as the guidance for accuracy, and the model picker itself allows up to 10 at a time.
items.evidence_quote: You can add any number of semantic models to the fallback list, however selecting 10 or fewer models improves agent accuracy.

items.stem: You configure a Title field to be prepended to the chunks generated from a Knowledge article DMO so the prompt gets more context. Data 360 abandons the prepending when the prepended field content is longer than a certain number of tokens. What is that limit?
items.rationale: Data 360 skips prepending fields when the prepended values run longer than 512 tokens, which is also the default max token limit for a chunk, so prepended metadata has to be kept short or it is silently dropped.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 skips prepending fields if the length of the prepended fields is greater than 512 tokens.

items.stem: Two chunks come back from a hybrid search with hybrid scores of 0.9 and 0.6. What are those score values legitimately good for?
options: Comparing how results rank against each other for that one query
Setting a single relevance cut-off that holds good across all queries
Comparing the relevance of results coming from two different search indexes
Judging in absolute terms how good a chunk is as grounding for a prompt
answer: Comparing how results rank against each other for that one query
items.rationale: Hybrid scores are not absolute values, so they only support comparing the ranking of results within the same query. Using them as a fixed global threshold, or comparing them across queries or indexes, reads meaning into a number that does not carry it.
items.evidence_quote: The score values aren’t absolute and realistically must be used only to compare ranking results for the same query.

items.stem: In a Data 360 search index configuration, the LLM-based parsing and LLM-based visual data preprocessing options can be applied to which file types held in unstructured data model objects? Select all that apply.
options: PDF
HTML
DOCX
PPTX
XLSX
CSV
TXT
MP4
items.rationale: The LLM-based parsing and visual data preprocessing options are offered only for PDF, HTML, DOCX and PPTX files from unstructured data model objects. XLSX, CSV, TXT and MP4 are all supported unstructured formats that Data 360 will index and chunk, but they cannot use these LLM-based options.
items.evidence_quote: Note Parsing and preprocessing options are available only for PDF, HTML, DOCX, and PPTX file types from UDMOs, not for data model objects (DMOs), including those that have a file attachment UDMO.

items.stem: In an enriched Data 360 search index, the generated Summary metadata aims for a word count within a stated range. What is the maximum number of words it aims for?
items.rationale: The Summary metadata aims for a minimum of 100 and a maximum of 250 words. 100 is the lower bound of the same range, and 512 is the default chunking max token limit, which is a different setting entirely.
items.evidence_quote: Provides a summary of the content, highlighting key topics and entities. If possible, aim to encompass a minimum of 100 words and a maximum of 250 words.

items.stem: A stakeholder wants a predictive model in Data 360 to explain the combined effect of two variables together, such as region and month. Which algorithm can produce that kind of explanation?
options: Generalized Linear Model (GLM)
XGBoost
Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM)
K-means
items.rationale: Only GLM can produce explanations based on the interaction between variables. XGBoost and GBM are the other two algorithms offered in the Select Algorithm step but neither gives interaction-based explanations, and K-means is a Data 360 clustering algorithm rather than a choice for a predictive model.
items.evidence_quote: Only GLM can produce explanations based on the interaction between variables, such as the combined impact of region and month together.

items.stem: The generally available Tableau Next MCP Server is the component that supplies tools for creating, updating, and deleting dashboards, semantic models, visualizations, and alerts.
items.rationale: Those create, update and delete tools are early access in the separate Tableau Next MCP Beta Server, which is a companion to the generally available server and sits ahead of general availability. Promising write-back through the GA server would over-scope a delivery.
items.evidence_quote: The Tableau Next Model Context Protocol (MCP) Beta Server is a companion to the generally available Tableau Next MCP Server. It gives you early access to tools that create, update, and delete dashboards, semantic models, visualizations, and alerts before they reach general availability.

items.stem: A chunk is longer than the embedding model's own maximum token limit. What happens to the text past that limit?
options: The model ignores it when generating the embedding
The chunk is rejected and logged as an error
The chunk is split again into two embeddings
The text is summarised down to fit the limit
answer: The model ignores it when generating the embedding
items.rationale: The overflow is dropped silently, so an oversized chunk produces an embedding built from only its opening. Nothing fails, which is what makes this worth knowing: the symptom is poor retrieval rather than an error.
items.evidence_quote: Embedding models create tokens from text and they ignore any text beyond their max token limit.

items.stem: Acting on a prescription from a predictive model changes the predicted outcome, but is not guaranteed to change the actual one.
items.rationale: The distinction matters when a business is judging whether the model worked. A prescription moves the model's estimate, and reality may or may not follow, so measuring prescriptions by whether the prediction improved proves nothing on its own.
items.evidence_quote: The prescription affects the predicted outcome, not necessarily the actual one.

items.stem: While building a search index, Data 360 has to estimate the token count of the text going into a chunk. How does it approximate that count?
options: By counting words in Latin-based languages and punctuation marks in non-Latin-based ones
By counting characters and dividing by four, whatever the language
By asking the embedding model to count the tokens before chunking
By counting words in every language, adjusted by a fixed language factor
answer: By counting words in Latin-based languages and punctuation marks in non-Latin-based ones
items.rationale: The approximation changes with the script, because a word is roughly one token in Latin-based languages and that relationship breaks down in languages like Japanese. It explains why the same max token setting yields very differently sized chunks across a multilingual corpus.
items.evidence_quote: To approximate the token count when merging sentences into chunks, Data 360 uses the number of words for Latin-based languages and the number of punctuation marks for non-Latin-based languages (such as Japanese).

items.stem: Model Builder raises a low area under the curve alert once the figure falls below a stated value. What is that value?
items.rationale: Below 0.6 the model is judged to be performing poorly and worth improving before activation. There is a high alert as well, which catches the opposite problem.
items.evidence_quote: Model Builder displays an alert when it detects a high or low AUC based on these values. Below 0.6 (low) Above 0.95 (high)

items.stem: A model comes back with an unusually high area under the curve and Model Builder raises an alert about it. What does Salesforce say that suggests?
options: Data leakage, which should be investigated and the offending variables removed
That the model is ready to activate with no further work
That the training data was too small for the result to be trusted
That the two classes are too evenly balanced
answer: Data leakage, which should be investigated and the offending variables removed
items.rationale: A model that performs suspiciously well is usually seeing something it would not have at prediction time. Treating a high AUC as good news is the instinct this alert exists to interrupt.
items.evidence_quote: A high AUC indicates that the model performs so well that data leakage can be a factor. Investigate and remove any variables from your model that can cause data leakage.

items.stem: Each integration listed against an AI model carries metadata about that integration. Which details are shown?
options: Model status, active or inactive
Integration type
Last run date
Run status
The data model objects involved
The number of predictions returned
The user who created the integration
items.rationale: Five details, and volume is not among them: the list tells you what runs, against which objects, and whether the last run worked, which is what shortens an investigation. Counting predictions is a billing question answered elsewhere.
items.evidence_quote: Each integration shows the model status (active or inactive), type, last run date, run status, and data model objects (DMOs)

items.stem: An unstructured data lake object is being removed, and the unstructured data model object mapped to it carries a search index configuration. What does Data 360 require in this case?
options: The search index has to be deleted before the UDMO and its mappings can be
The mappings have to be removed before the search index can be deleted
The UDMO has to be deleted before the search index can be
Nothing; deleting the UDLO removes the index and mappings with it
answer: The search index has to be deleted before the UDMO and its mappings can be
items.rationale: Removal runs from the outside in: the page's procedure deletes the retrievers, then the search index, then the data model object, and only then the UDLO. Nothing cascades from the UDLO downwards, so the index has to go before the UDMO and its mappings can.
items.evidence_quote: If a UDMO mapped to the UDLO has a search index configuration, you must first delete the search index before you can delete the UDMO and any mappings to it.

items.stem: What does identity resolution in Data 360 produce?
options: Unified profiles built from source profile data
Segments ready for activation
Calculated insights over profile data
A data graph for real-time retrieval
answer: Unified profiles built from source profile data
items.rationale: Identity resolution is the engine that generates unified profiles. Segments, calculated insights and data graphs are separate capabilities that consume the result.
items.evidence_quote: Identity resolution is the processing engine that generates unified profiles from source profile data stored in Data 360.

items.stem: What does an identity resolution ruleset contain?
options: Match rules and reconciliation rules
Match rules and the mapping from data lake objects to data model objects
Reconciliation rules and the publish schedule for unified profiles
Match rules and the segment filters that consume the unified profiles
items.rationale: The two halves do different jobs: match rules decide which records are the same person, reconciliation rules decide which value wins where the matched records disagree. Mapping and segmentation sit outside the ruleset.
items.evidence_quote: Identity resolution rulesets contain match and reconciliation rules that specify how to link multiple sources of data into a unified profile.

items.stem: Identity resolution creates a kind of object that bridges the source records and the unified profile, letting you see which sources fed a given profile. It is also required before calculated insights can be built on unified profiles. What is that kind of object called?
items.rationale: Unified link objects are the audit trail of unification. Without them you can see the unified profile but not which source records produced it, and calculated insights over unified profiles cannot be built at all.
items.evidence_quote: Unified link objects serve as the link between the source data and unified objects. Unified link objects allow you to view source data of each unified profile and are required for creating calculated insights for unified profiles.

items.stem: A client expects unification to choose the best value for each field and overwrite the rest. What actually happens to the source values?
options: Nothing: no winning values are picked and no existing data is overridden
The most recently updated source value wins and replaces the others
Values are merged into a golden record and the source records are archived
A reconciliation rule deletes the losing source records
answer: Nothing: no winning values are picked and no existing data is overridden
items.rationale: A unified profile is a system of reference, not a golden record. It gives you keys to every source record rather than a single best version, which is the expectation to reset early in a project.
items.evidence_quote: Identity resolution doesn’t pick winning values or override any existing data while unifying profiles.

items.stem: An identity resolution ruleset is configured for a real-time use case and runs for the first time. Which kind of matching does that first run use?
options: Scheduled matching, which is always used for the first run
Real-time matching, since that is how the ruleset is configured
Neither, because the first run only validates the configuration
Both, running in parallel so the results can be compared
answer: Scheduled matching, which is always used for the first run
items.rationale: The first pass over the data is always scheduled, and only afterwards is the ruleset updated incrementally. That matters for go-live planning: a real-time design still waits on a full scheduled run before it can answer anything.
items.evidence_quote: Scheduled matching is used the first time your identity resolution ruleset runs. After the first successful run, your identity resolution ruleset is updated incrementally using scheduled matching when data in the primary data model object changes.

items.stem: A field uses the Last Updated reconciliation rule, and two matched records carry exactly the same last updated date and time. How is the winning value chosen?
options: Alphabetically
By source priority order
By whichever value occurs most often
At random, so the result can differ between runs
items.rationale: An alphabetical tie-break is deterministic, which is the point: the same inputs give the same unified profile on every run. Expecting a random or source-ordered outcome is the usual guess.
items.evidence_quote: If matching records have the same last updated date and time, a value is selected alphabetically.

items.stem: A ruleset is running under real-time matching. Which match methods are available to it?
options: Exact
Exact Normalized
Fuzzy - High Precision
Fuzzy - Medium Precision
Fuzzy - Low Precision
items.rationale: Real-time matching drops to the two precise methods whatever the match rule asks for, so a rule tuned with fuzzy matching behaves differently in real time than it did on a scheduled run. That is the source of a lot of surprise about real-time consolidation rates.
items.evidence_quote: In real-time matching, match methods are restricted to Exact or Exact Normalized matching only, regardless of the scheduled match selected for a given match rule.

items.stem: Reconciliation rules pick a single winning email address and phone number for a unified profile, in the same way they pick a single first name.
items.rationale: Contact points are the deliberate exception. Every contact point from every source stays on the unified profile, because an activation may need to reach a person on any of them. Priority between contact points is decided in the activation, not by reconciliation.
items.evidence_quote: Reconciliation rules don't apply to contact points such as email or phone number. All contact points remain part of a unified profile, so all contact points are available when creating activations for segments on unified profile.

items.stem: A client trusts their billing system over their web forms and wants that preference to decide which value reaches the unified profile. Which reconciliation rule expresses that?
options: Source Priority
Last Updated
Most Frequent
Ignore Empty Values
items.rationale: Source Priority is the only rule that ranks the sources themselves. Last Updated and Most Frequent both ignore where a value came from, and Ignore Empty Values is a setting applied alongside a rule rather than a rule of its own.
items.evidence_quote:
| Source Priority | 
This rule sorts your data lake objects in order of most to least preferred for inclusion in the unified profile.

items.stem: To compare a strict match rule against a looser one, a team builds a second ruleset on the same entity and leaves both running. What is the cost of leaving the second one in place?
options: Unified profiles from every ruleset count toward the entitlement limit
Only the ruleset marked as default counts toward the entitlement limit
The second ruleset is free while it stays unpublished to segments
Nothing, because the two rulesets share one set of unified profiles
answer: Unified profiles from every ruleset count toward the entitlement limit
items.rationale: Each ruleset produces its own unified profiles and all of them are counted, so a comparison left running quietly doubles the number consumed. Salesforce's own advice is to treat the second ruleset as temporary and delete it once the better rules are chosen.
items.evidence_quote: Use the second ruleset as a temporary way to create the best ruleset for your data, and then delete the second ruleset. Unified profiles from all rulesets count toward your entitlement limit.

items.stem: Filters on a ruleset's primary data model object decide which source records enter identity resolution at all. At most how many filter groups does one ruleset support?
items.rationale: Three groups, each holding at most three field conditions, so nine conditions is the ceiling. That is deliberately coarse: filters are meant for partition-level separation such as splitting B2B from B2C accounts, not for picking out individual records.
items.evidence_quote: Each ruleset supports up to 3 filter groups with up to 3 field conditions per group.

items.stem: How often does identity resolution process rulesets?
options: Every 60 minutes to 24 hours, depending on the data source
Continuously, as each individual source record is changed
Once every 24 hours, on the same schedule for every source
Only when someone runs the ruleset manually from setup
answer: Every 60 minutes to 24 hours, depending on the data source
items.rationale: Each source is on its own timeline within that window, so unified profiles are not immediately consistent with the sources. Real-time identity resolution is a separate capability.
items.evidence_quote: Identity resolution processes rulesets as frequently as every 60 minutes to 24 hours, depending on the data source.

items.stem: A real-time data graph is kept current with the unified profiles that scheduled ruleset runs produce. How many times a day does that update happen?
items.rationale: Once. Real-time matching answers in milliseconds against the graph, but the profiles behind it are refreshed from the scheduled run only daily, so a profile built overnight is not visible to real-time matching until that refresh.
items.evidence_quote: Once per day, the real-time data graph is updated with unified profiles generated by a scheduled ruleset run.

items.stem: Real-time matching applies a different set of reconciliation rules from scheduled matching, so a field can reconcile one way in real time and another way on the nightly run.
items.rationale: Reconciliation is identical across modes. It is the match methods that change in real time, narrowing to Exact and Exact Normalized, so the difference between modes is which records are judged to be the same person, not which value wins afterwards.
items.evidence_quote: Identity resolution uses the same reconciliation rules in all modes, regardless of whether match rules are scheduled or real-time.

items.stem: Unified profile ID values keep changing between ruleset runs, which is breaking downstream joins. Which reconciliation rule does Salesforce recommend on ID fields to settle them?
options: Source Priority
Last Updated
Most Frequent
Whichever rule the object's default already uses
items.rationale: A fixed ranking of sources gives a fixed answer, so the same source wins every run and the ID stops moving. Last Updated and Most Frequent both let the winner change as data arrives, which is exactly the instability being complained about.
items.evidence_quote: To stabilize ID values, use the Source Priority reconciliation rule on ID fields.

items.stem: Changing a filter condition on an active identity resolution ruleset causes the whole ruleset to be reprocessed rather than updated incrementally.
items.rationale: A filter changes which records were ever eligible, so nothing short of a full rerun can be correct. The practical consequence is to pause the schedule, make every configuration change at once, and resume, rather than tuning filters one at a time on a live ruleset.
items.evidence_quote: Adding or changing a filter condition on an active ruleset triggers a full reprocessing of the ruleset.

items.stem: A ruleset's rules need reworking, but downstream objects reference it by name and id and those references must survive. What does Salesforce tell you to do?
options: Update the existing ruleset rather than deleting and recreating it
Delete it and recreate it with the same name, which restores the id
Clone it, switch the downstream references, then delete the original
Deactivate it, recreate it alongside, and merge the unified profiles
answer: Update the existing ruleset rather than deleting and recreating it
items.rationale: Deleting is irreversible and takes the unification history with it, and a recreated ruleset does not get the old id back. Updating keeps the name and id while overriding the existing data, which is the only route that leaves downstream references intact.
items.evidence_quote: To keep the same ruleset name and ruleset ID and override existing data, update the ruleset instead of deleting it.

items.stem: Which destinations can segmented Data 360 data be sent to by creating an activation target?
options: External file storage
An external activation platform
Another data model object (DMO) inside Data 360
An inbound data stream
A calculated insight object (CIO)
A Tableau Next workspace
answer: Another data model object (DMO) inside Data 360
items.rationale: Activation targets cover three families of destination: file storage such as Amazon S3 or SFTP, external activation platforms, and other DMOs within Data 360 itself. Data streams bring data in rather than take it out, a calculated insight is an input to a segment, and a Tableau Next workspace holds analytics assets rather than receiving an activation.
items.evidence_quote: Depending on your use case, data can be activated to various targets, from file storage, external activation, or to other data model objects (DMOs) in Data 360.

items.stem: A client asks what an activation target in Data 360 actually holds. Which description is correct?
options: The authentication and authorization information for one activation platform
The contact points and attributes chosen for one segment's publish
