The profiles most recently published to a marketing platform
The filter criteria that narrow a segment before it publishes
answer: The authentication and authorization information for one activation platform
items.rationale: An activation target is the stored connection to a platform such as Marketing Cloud Engagement or Meta, which is why one target can be reused by many segments. The contact points and attributes belong to the activation, the published records land in the Audience DMO, and the filters belong to the segment.
items.evidence_quote: An activation target is used to store authentication and authorization information for a given activation platform, like Marketing Cloud Engagement or Meta.

items.stem: Each time a Data 360 segment publishes, one object is created or updated to record which profiles qualified. What is that object called?
items.rationale: Publishing a segment writes the qualifying profile IDs to the Segment Membership DMO, which is what a consultant queries in Data Explorer or Tableau to prove who is in a segment. The Audience DMO records what was sent to an activation target, which is a different question.
items.evidence_quote: Each time you publish a segment, a data model object (DMO) is created or updated to store segment membership information. To identify who's included in a segment, use the Segment Membership DMO (type Segment_Membership).

items.stem: A client already using Data 360 wants to push audience segments to Google and Meta so they can target their first-party data in campaigns. Which add-on license does that require?
options: Ad Audiences
Data 360 Profiles
Data Cloud One
Marketing Cloud Engagement
items.rationale: Advertising to platforms such as Google and Meta needs the Ad Audiences add-on license, which also brings back insights from those activations. Activating to AppExchange advertising partners is the case that needs only the base Data Cloud license, and the other options are a license and products that do not unlock advertising platforms.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 supports integrations with advertising platforms such as Google and Meta. Advertising on these platforms requires the Ad Audiences license.

items.stem: While building a segment in Data 360, an analyst uses the Approximate Segment Population field. What does that field report?
options: An estimated population, given as a range of possible values at 95% confidence
An exact count of the population, recalculated each time a rule is changed
The number of profiles sent to the activation target on the last publish
A projection of the population at the end of the segment's lookback window
answer: An estimated population, given as a range of possible values at 95% confidence
items.rationale: The approximate count is computed from a sample of the profile data and normalised back up, so it returns a confidence range rather than a figure to quote to a client. The exact population only arrives when the segment is saved, and the count of profiles actually delivered belongs to activation history.
items.evidence_quote: The approximate count provides an estimated segment population, represented as a range of possible values with 95% confidence.

items.stem: An ISV activation platform needs to resolve digital identifiers such as UID2 and RampID across media platforms. Which standard data model object should that identifier data be ingested and modelled into?
items.rationale: Digital identifier data belongs in the standard ContactPointDigitalId DMO, which activation toolkit platforms query to resolve digital identities. Pushing the identifiers into custom fields on the Individual DMO instead is explicitly discouraged and leaves anonymous identifiers unusable by those activations.
items.evidence_quote: Ingest and model your digital identifier data by using the standard `ContactPointDigitalId` data model object (DMO). Independent Software Vendors (ISV) use the activation toolkit to build activations that query this DMO to resolve digital identities across digital media platforms.

items.stem: A client asks why Data 360 has filters in both segmentation and activation when one set would seem to do. What is the difference in purpose?
options: Segment filters narrow who is in the audience; activation filters narrow which values personalize the message
Segment filters run at publish time; activation filters run when the segment is built
Segment filters apply to profile data; activation filters apply to engagement data
Segment filters are evaluated in Data 360; activation filters are evaluated by the target platform
answer: Segment filters narrow who is in the audience; activation filters narrow which values personalize the message
items.rationale: The two answer different questions: who to send to, and what to say to them. A customer who bought several products in the window is in the segment once, but the activation filter decides which product name reaches the message.
items.evidence_quote: Apply filters to a segment to narrow your audience. Use activation filters to narrow down relevant values with related attributes that personalize messages.

items.stem: A retailer has run a second identity resolution ruleset that groups its people by last name and address, and now wants segment criteria evaluated for each group as a whole rather than for each person in it. Name the object to set as the segment target.
items.rationale: Households are built by consolidating unified individuals, and segmenting on Unified Household is what applies the criteria at household level rather than to each person in it.
items.evidence_quote: You can consolidate Unified Individuals into groups of individuals called households. Segment on Unified Household to identify households with specific criteria.

items.stem: A client wants to build segments over free-text data without maintaining lists of exact keywords to match on. Which Data 360 segmentation feature addresses that?
options: Vector filters, which use NLP to sort through unstructured data
Value suggestions, which offer the values already ingested for an attribute
Campaign engagement filters, which match on engagement counts
Einstein segments, which build a segment from a written prompt
answer: Vector filters, which use NLP to sort through unstructured data
items.rationale: Vector filters are the feature aimed squarely at unstructured data, and they can filter structured and unstructured data in one segment. Einstein segments also involve natural language but the language is the user's prompt, not the data being filtered.
items.evidence_quote: Vector filters reduce reliance on exact keyword matches and manual data organization, allowing you to create accurate segments efficiently. This feature uses NLP algorithms to sort through unstructured data in segment creation.

items.stem: A campaign carries four offers and a customer could qualify for three of them, but should receive only the best one. Which Data 360 segment type is built for that?
options: A waterfall segment
A real-time segment
A dynamic segment
A standard segment with exclusion criteria
items.rationale: A waterfall segment walks existing segments in priority order and places each person only in the highest-priority one they match, producing mutually exclusive audiences. Exclusion criteria on a standard segment can carve out one audience but does not rank a whole list for you.
items.evidence_quote: If you’re running a campaign with multiple offers, use a waterfall segment to process a list of existing segments in a priority order. The primary goal is to ensure that an individual who qualifies for more than one segment is placed only into the highest-priority segment they match.

items.stem: A standard segment is created in Data 360 and the Lookback Window is left at its default. How many days of data does that default window cover?
items.rationale: The Lookback Window defaults to 90 days and can be extended up to 2 years, so a segment that is expected to look back further has to have the window widened deliberately at creation.
items.evidence_quote: Set the Lookback Window for your segment. The default is 90 days. You can set it up to 2 years.

items.stem: A client needs segment membership pushed to their Marketing Cloud Engagement target several times a day instead of on the standard 12- or 24-hour schedule. Which publish choice meets that, and on what interval?
options: Rapid Publish, on a daily schedule at a 1-hour or 4-hour interval
Publish Now, triggered hourly by a scheduled Salesforce flow
A dynamic segment, which takes parameter values at execution time
A real-time segment, which completes on demand in milliseconds
answer: Rapid Publish, on a daily schedule at a 1-hour or 4-hour interval
items.rationale: Rapid Publish is the documented way to increase segment refresh frequency to the activation targets, and it runs daily at either a 1-hour or a 4-hour interval. Publish Now is a manual one-off, and real-time and dynamic segments solve on-demand evaluation rather than a faster recurring publish to a target.
items.evidence_quote: When you create a segment, choose Rapid Publish to run on a daily schedule at a 1-hour or 4-hour interval.

items.stem: The Segment On setting names the object a standard Data 360 segment is built on. Which objects can be selected there?
options: An object marked as Profile or Engagement type during ingestion
Any object in the data model, including audience and segment membership objects
Only the Unified Individual object produced by identity resolution
Any data lake object that a data stream has landed in Data 360
answer: An object marked as Profile or Engagement type during ingestion
items.rationale: Segment On is limited to DMOs whose category was set to Profile or Engagement when the data was ingested, which is why a client who wants to segment on a reference table has to model it as one of those types first. Unified Individual is a common choice but not the only one, and a DLO cannot be segmented on until it is mapped to a DMO.
items.evidence_quote: Segment On defines the target object used to build your segment. You can choose an object marked as Profile or Engagement type during ingestion.

items.stem: A client unifies their customer data with an identity resolution ruleset and now wants to activate a segment. Which object must they use as the activation membership?
options: The Unified Individual DMO
The Individual DMO from the source that owns the contact point
The segment membership DMO for the Segment On object
The Audience DMO created for the activation target
items.rationale: Activation membership is the grouping of fields sent in an activation, and once identity resolution is in use it must be taken from the Unified Individual DMO so the activation resolves to unified profiles. A source Individual DMO would activate unmerged records, and the segment membership and Audience DMOs are outputs of publishing rather than the membership you select.
items.evidence_quote: If you are using identity resolution ruleset to unify your data, you must use the Unified Individual data model object (DMO) as the activation membership.

items.stem: A client wants to filter a segment on a metric from a calculated insight. What does that impose on the object chosen in Segment On?
options: It has to be a Profile type object
It has to be an Engagement type object
It has to be the Unified Individual object
It has to be the object the insight's SQL aggregates over
answer: It has to be a Profile type object
items.rationale: Segmenting on an Engagement type object is allowed in general, but as soon as a calculated insight is used in the segment the Segment On object must be a Profile type. The insight still has to join to the segmented table and carry its primary key as a dimension, but that is a requirement on the insight rather than on the object type.
items.evidence_quote: When using a calculated insight in a segment, the Segment On data model object (DMO) that you choose must be a Profile type.

items.stem: A client activates a segment to Google and expects an audience insights report back. The activated segment population has to be larger than a stated figure before any report is produced. What is that figure?
items.rationale: A Google audience report is only produced when the activated population exceeds 1,000 users, so a narrow test segment will activate successfully and still return no insights. Google also adds randomised noise and redacts small high-indexing categories, so the scores that do come back are approximations.
items.evidence_quote: To qualify for audience insights reporting, the activated segment population must be more than 1,000 users.

items.stem: A client has built a real-time segment in Data 360 and asks where it can be published. What is a real-time segment supported against?
options: A real-time data graph only
Marketing Cloud Engagement only
Any target that accepts a 1-hour publish schedule
External activation platforms such as Google Ads and Meta
items.rationale: A real-time segment responds in milliseconds and is supported only against a real-time data graph, so it cannot be pointed at an activation target at all. Marketing Cloud Engagement and file storage are the targets that accept the 1-hour and 4-hour rapid publish schedules on a standard segment.
items.evidence_quote: Real-Time Segment | Not applicable (millisecond response) | Real-time data graph only

rows: None - Can't publish to activation targets

items.stem: Data 360 shows a Segment Status against every segment. Pair each status value with what it tells you about that segment.
options: Active
Processing
Error
Inactive

pairs.right: The segment is created and all segment functionality is available
A publish of the segment is in progress
The segment is still active but cannot be published manually
The segment can only be deleted

answer: Active::The segment is created and all segment functionality is available
Processing::A publish of the segment is in progress
Error::The segment is still active but cannot be published manually
Inactive::The segment can only be deleted
items.rationale: Error does not mean the segment is broken or gone - it stays active and keeps its scheduled behaviour, but a manual publish is refused, which is why a client seeing Error is in a different position from one seeing Inactive, where deletion is the only action left.
items.evidence_quote: Active | Segment created and all segment functionality available | Processing | Publishing segment in progress | Recounting | Recounting the segment population in progress | Error | Segment is active but can't be manually published | Inactive | Segment can only be deleted

rows: Segment created and all segment functionality available
Recounting the segment population in progress
Segment is active but can’t be manually published

items.stem: Consent preferences used as segment filter criteria must be mapped to objects from the Privacy Data Model; custom objects are not supported for this.
items.rationale: The Privacy Data Model is a recommendation rather than a requirement, and consent preferences held on custom DMOs or attributes can be used as filter criteria too. Reading the recommendation as a rule leads teams to remodel data that would have worked as it stood.
items.evidence_quote: We recommend that consent preferences be mapped to objects from the Privacy Data Model but they can be mapped to custom objects as well.

items.stem: An org runs identity resolution but a segment is built on the Individual object rather than the Unified Individual. What does Salesforce warn can happen to the population?
options: It can contain duplicate or skipped entities
It is capped at the number of unified profiles in the org
It excludes anyone whose records came from more than one source
It is recalculated only when the ruleset next runs
answer: It can contain duplicate or skipped entities
items.rationale: Segmenting below the unified layer counts source records rather than people, so one customer known to three systems can appear three times, and the deduplication that identity resolution exists to provide is bypassed. The count is wrong in both directions, which is why the page names skipped as well as duplicate entities.
items.evidence_quote: Segmenting on the Individual instead of the Unified Individual can result in duplicate or skipped entities in your count.

items.stem: A calculated insight metric is dragged onto an activation and turns out to be non-aggregatable. What does that require?
options: At least one dimension filter on the metric
An aggregation to be chosen, such as Sum or Max
The metric to be republished before it can be used
The activation target to support related attributes
answer: At least one dimension filter on the metric
items.rationale: A non-aggregatable metric has no way to collapse many values into one, so a dimension filter has to do it instead. For aggregatable metrics the filter is optional, because an aggregation like Sum or Min already resolves the value.
items.evidence_quote: At least one dimension filter is required for non-aggregatable metrics in order to narrow down the attribute to one specific value.

items.stem: Attribute output names are being customised on an activation so the file matches what the target platform expects. Two of the attributes come from different data model objects and would naturally carry the same name. What does Data 360 require?
options: Output names must be unique across the whole activation, whichever object they come from
Output names must be unique only within each data model object
Duplicate output names are allowed and are suffixed automatically
Duplicate output names are allowed as long as the attributes have different data types
answer: Output names must be unique across the whole activation, whichever object they come from
items.rationale: Uniqueness is enforced across the activation as a whole, so an attribute called Name on two different DMOs forces at least one of them to be renamed. Nothing is suffixed for you.
items.evidence_quote: The output names must be unique across all attributes in the activation, including attributes from different data model objects (DMOs).

items.stem: An analyst expects to pick an activation template while creating an activation, but none is offered. What has to be true before one appears?
options: A template must already exist that matches both the target platform and the DMO
A template must already exist for the target platform, whichever DMO is used
The segment must have published at least once so the template can be inferred
The activation target must be enabled for templates in its settings
answer: A template must already exist that matches both the target platform and the DMO
items.rationale: Both halves have to match, which is why a template built for one DMO does not appear for an activation on another even when the target platform is identical. Nothing is generated from a previous publish.
items.evidence_quote: Before you use a template during activation creation, at least one activation template must exist that matches the target platform and DMO for your activation.

items.stem: An activation template fills in settings automatically when an activation is created. Which settings does it populate?
options: Contact points
Source priority
Filters
Enrichment data
The publish schedule of the segment
The activation target's authentication details
items.rationale: A template covers the four settings that get rebuilt by hand on every similar activation. It does not touch the segment's publish schedule, and authentication belongs to the activation target rather than to the activation.
items.evidence_quote: The template prefills the activation's configuration with the stored contact point selection, source priority, filters, and enrichment settings.

items.stem: Value suggestions offer the values already present in the data when an analyst types into a segment filter. For which data model object fields can they be switched on?
options: Fields whose data type is Text
Fields whose data type is Text or Number
Any field on a DMO marked as Profile type
Any field that has fewer than 1,000 distinct values
answer: Fields whose data type is Text
items.rationale: Text fields only, and the switch lives on the DMO record home rather than in the segment. The thousand-value figure is real but it caps how many suggestions are shown, not which fields qualify.
items.evidence_quote: You can enable value suggestions for data model object (DMO) fields if the data type is Text.

items.stem: A segment built on the account object is being activated to an AppExchange partner target. The Unified Individual DMO can be selected as the activation membership for that activation.
items.rationale: For AppExchange partner targets, Unified Individual is not offered as the activation membership when the segment is built on account or unified account objects, so a B2B audience for a partner target has to be designed around a different membership object.
items.evidence_quote: Unified Individual DMO isn't available for segments built on account or unified account objects for AppExchange partner targets.

items.stem: A client wants to publish a Data 360 segment to an AppExchange partner advertising platform for the first time. Put the setup tasks into the order they have to be completed.
options: Install the managed package required for using external activation platforms
Configure the platform parameters, authentication details and required mappings
Define the activation target, its destination system, data mapping and scheduling
Create the activation that publishes the segment
answer: Install the managed package required for using external activation platforms
Configure the platform parameters, authentication details and required mappings
Define the activation target, its destination system, data mapping and scheduling
Create the activation that publishes the segment
items.rationale: The chain is package, then platform, then target, then activation: the external activation platform is configured after the managed package is installed, the activation target is defined against that platform, and all three are prerequisites of creating the activation itself.
items.evidence_quote: Make sure that you've completed these tasks before creating an activation: Install a Managed Package - Install the managed package required for using external activation platforms. Set Up an External Activation Platform - Configure an external activation platform after installation. Set up platform parameters, authentication details, and required mappings. Create an External Activation Target in Data 360 - Define an activation target by specifying the destination system, data mapping, and scheduling details.

items.stem: An activation sends related attributes taken from engagement data, and the segment behind it is set to rapid publish. How many days of engagement data does that activation consider when it picks its output values?
items.rationale: Activation normally considers a 90-day lookback for engagement data, but selecting related attributes on an activation whose segment uses rapid publish shortens that window to seven days, so older engagement records are silently ignored in the output.
items.evidence_quote: If related attributes are selected for an activation with a rapid segment publish, the lookback window is seven days.

items.stem: An activation is configured for incremental refresh so that only changed records go to the target. In which circumstances is the whole activation transferred to the target anyway?
options: The activation's very first publish to that target
A publish that follows a change to the activation
The first publish after a refresh has failed
Any publish more than 12 hours after the previous one
A publish in which every record in the segment has changed
answer: The activation's very first publish to that target
A publish that follows a change to the activation
items.rationale: The first publish for every activation target is a full refresh whatever refresh type is chosen, and editing the activation forces another full refresh, so a client should expect two full volumes of data before incremental behaviour settles in. After a failure the next refresh is incremental from the last successful publish, and neither elapsed time nor the proportion of changed records promotes a run to a full refresh.
items.evidence_quote: The first publish for all activation targets is always a full refresh, regardless of the refresh type you choose. A full refresh is also triggered whenever you make changes to the activation. In both cases, the entire activation is transferred to the target.

items.stem: An activation set to incremental refresh sits behind a segment that publishes hourly. Changes to records that are already in the audience are not picked up on every run: they are processed no more often than one fixed interval. How long is that interval?
items.rationale: Modifications to existing records are processed at most once every 12 hours, and the extra runs inside that window carry only newly added or removed records. A client on a 1-hour publish schedule therefore sees additions and deletions quickly but updated attribute values at most twice a day.
items.evidence_quote: Modifications to existing records are processed no more than once every 12 hours. Any additional runs within that 12-hour window include only records that are newly added or removed.

items.stem: A segment uses an Is Not Equal To filter on a text attribute. The client points out that customers who have no value at all for that attribute are missing from the population. What explains this, and what brings them back?
options: The operator drops records whose field is null; add a Has No Value filter alongside it in an Or block
The operator is case-sensitive on blank strings; replace it with Does Not Contain on the same attribute
The lookback window excluded those records; widen the window and republish the segment
Null is treated as an empty string and matched the filter; merge the containers with a nested operator
answer: The operator drops records whose field is null; add a Has No Value filter alongside it in an Or block
items.rationale: A record whose field is null is not included by an Is Not Equal To filter, so the null population has to be added back deliberately with a Has No Value filter combined in an Or block. Case sensitivity is not the issue - text operators are case-insensitive - and the lookback window filters on engagement dates rather than on null attribute values.
items.evidence_quote: If a record containing a field with a `Null` value is referenced in an Is Not Equal To segment filter, the record isn't included in the segment population. To include the record, configure a filter in the segment to check if the field Has No Value. Then add the Has No Value and Is Not Equal To filters within an Or block.

items.stem: Match Count, the approximate number of audience members matched on an advertising partner platform, is reported for Conversion API (CAPI) activation targets.
items.rationale: CAPI targets are the documented exception: match count appears on the Insights tab for the ordinary advertising targets such as Meta, Google Ads and LinkedIn, but not for CAPI. Expecting a match rate back from a CAPI activation leads to a support case rather than a number.
items.evidence_quote: Match count values for Conversion API (CAPI) targets are not shown.

items.stem: An org changes its Salesforce time zone. Segments created afterwards behave as expected, but the ones created before it carry on publishing on the old clock. How is that fixed?
options: Resave each existing segment
Republish each existing segment
Deactivate and reactivate each existing segment
Nothing can be done; existing segments keep their original time zone permanently
items.rationale: A time zone change does not reach back into existing segments, and only a save applies the new one. Republishing runs the segment without touching its configuration, so it changes nothing here.
items.evidence_quote: Newly created segments follow the updated time zone. To update the time zone of an existing segment, resave the segment.

items.stem: When the clocks change for daylight saving, a segment on a 24-hour publish schedule shifts with them so that it keeps publishing at the same local time.
items.rationale: Publishing is scheduled as an interval, not as a wall-clock time, so nothing exists for daylight saving to adjust. The publish keeps its spacing and drifts an hour against local time, which is worth flagging to anyone timing a campaign around it.
items.evidence_quote: Segment publish is scheduled based on a time interval (for example, 12 or 24 hours) rather than a specific date and time. Therefore, a segment publish time doesn't adjust for DST.

items.stem: A real-time segment has been created and now has to be usable from the real-time data graph. Which fields from the segment membership DMO have to be added to that graph?
options: Segment ID
Timestamp
Unified Individual ID
Publish Status
Activation Target ID
items.rationale: Two fields, and without them the segment exists but the graph cannot answer with it. Worth pairing with the segment's other constraints: a real-time segment cannot use exclusion criteria or nested batch segments.
items.evidence_quote: To make the segment available in your real-time data graph, add the Segment ID and Timestamp fields from the segment membership DMO object to the real-time data graph.

items.stem: Salesforce lists any one of Data Cloud Architect, Data Cloud Activation Manager or Data Cloud Activation Specialist as enough to create a waterfall segment. Which permission sets does it list for creating a real-time segment?
options: Data Cloud Architect only
The same three permission sets
Data Cloud Architect or Data Cloud Activation Manager
Data Cloud Activation Specialist only
items.rationale: Real-time segments are the narrower grant: Architect alone, where most segmentation tasks accept any of the three. An activation specialist who can build waterfall segments all day will find this one refused, which is easy to mistake for a bug.
items.evidence_quote:
| To create a real-time segment | 
Permission set:

-   Data Cloud Architect

items.stem: Suggested values for segment filters are held in a dataset of their own. For how many days are they retained?
items.rationale: Thirty days, which is why a value ingested long ago and never used since can stop appearing as a suggestion. On attributes with more than a thousand values only the thousand most frequent are offered, so a rare value may never appear at all and has to be typed exactly.
items.evidence_quote: Suggested values are retained for 30 days in the suggested values dataset.

items.stem: A client asks what a data kit is for in Data 360. Which description is right?
options: It wraps the packageable Data 360 metadata so a complete solution can be created and deployed
It exports the records held in a set of data lake objects so they can be loaded into another org
It snapshots a data space so the org can be rolled back to an earlier configuration
It bundles permission sets and users so access can be recreated in a target org
answer: It wraps the packageable Data 360 metadata so a complete solution can be created and deployed
items.rationale: A data kit carries metadata and process definitions, not data and not users. Expecting records to travel with it is the commonest misconception, and it is why a deployment can look complete while the target org holds nothing.
items.evidence_quote: A data kit wraps around all the packageable Data 360 metadata so that you can create and deploy complete solutions on Data 360.

items.stem: What does Salesforce give as reasons to use a sandbox with Tableau Next?
options: Provide a training environment
Test AppExchange packages or integrations
Isolate customization and development work from production until you are ready to deploy
Run production reporting while the production org is upgraded
Hold an archive of assets that have been deleted from production
answer: Isolate customization and development work from production until you are ready to deploy
items.rationale: Every documented reason is about doing work safely before it reaches production. A sandbox is neither a standby production environment nor an archive, and treating it as either is how orgs end up depending on one.
items.evidence_quote: Use a sandbox to: Test changes against copies of your production data and users. Provide a training environment. Test AppExchange packages or integrations. Isolate customization and development work from your production environment until you're ready to deploy changes.

items.stem: Data 360 offers two kinds of data kit. Name the one used to move metadata from a sandbox org into a production org, which cannot be used for packaging.
items.rationale: The DevOps data kit is the migration tool and the standard data kit is the distribution tool. Reaching for the standard kit to promote a sandbox build is the usual mistake, and it also changes which data space the work can land in.
items.evidence_quote: DevOps Data Kit: Use a DevOps data kit to migrate Data 360 metadata from a sandbox org to a production org, but not to package Data 360 metadata.

items.stem: A batch data transform deployed in a data kit arrives in the destination org carrying its schedule, and that schedule is running once the kit is installed.
items.rationale: The schedule deploys with the transform and is live immediately, so a kit installed into production starts doing work without anyone pressing anything. Worth checking before installing a kit built against a sandbox cadence.
items.evidence_quote: When you deploy a batch data transform in a data kit, the transform's schedule is included in the deployment. The schedule is active in the destination org after installation.

items.stem: A team builds a solution in a non-default data space and needs it deployed into a differently named data space in the target org. Which statement about data kits and data spaces applies?
options: A DevOps data kit deploys to the same data space it was created from, so the target space has to match
A DevOps data kit deploys to any data space chosen at install time
A standard data kit must be created from, and deployed to, the default data space
Neither kit type carries the data space, which is always chosen during deployment
answer: A DevOps data kit deploys to the same data space it was created from, so the target space has to match
items.rationale: The two kit types differ in exactly this. A DevOps kit can be built from any data space but lands in the same one, which constrains how orgs name their spaces. A standard kit is the flexible one: built from the default space and deployable to any space in the target org.
items.evidence_quote: You can create the DevOps data kit from any data space, but you deploy it to the same data space in the target org.

items.stem: A dashboard and the semantic model it reads are both ready to promote out of a sandbox, and the team plans to move them with change sets. What does Tableau Next require?
options: The semantic model can't travel in a change list with the dashboard, so it has to be deployed in a data kit
Both can go in one change list, as long as the semantic model is listed ahead of the dashboard
Both can go in one change list, as long as the target org already has a matching data space
The semantic model has to be rebuilt by hand in the target org, because it can't be deployed from a sandbox
answer: The semantic model can't travel in a change list with the dashboard, so it has to be deployed in a data kit
items.rationale: The restriction is on the change list. A semantic model cannot ride along with the assets and has to go in a data kit, so a promotion that looks like one release is two operations - the thing to plan for rather than discover.
items.evidence_quote: Semantic models and Tableau Next assets can't be deployed in a single change list. You must deploy semantic models using data kits.

items.stem: A standard data kit can be created from whichever org the solution was built in, including a sandbox or a full production org.
items.rationale: Standard data kits come from Developer Edition orgs only, which shapes how an ISV or partner has to organise their build. A sandbox is not a route to one.
items.evidence_quote: Create your standard data kit from Developer Edition orgs only.

items.stem: Tableau Next assets and the semantic models behind them have to reach a Data 360 companion org. What route does Salesforce give?
options: Deploy the semantic models to the home org, confirm they have synced to the companion, then send the assets by change set
Deploy a data kit containing both the semantic models and the assets straight to the companion org
Deploy the semantic models by change set to the companion org, then the assets by data kit
Rebuild the semantic models in the companion org, then send the assets by change set
answer: Deploy the semantic models to the home org, confirm they have synced to the companion, then send the assets by change set
items.rationale: Companion orgs do not support data kits at all, and semantic models can only be deployed by data kit, so models can never be deployed to a companion directly. They arrive by syncing from the home org, and only the Tableau Next assets travel by change set.
items.evidence_quote: Data 360 companion orgs don't support data kits, meaning semantic models and other Data 360 assets can only be deployed to home orgs. To deploy Tableau Next assets in a companion org, you must first deploy your semantic models to your home org. Next, validate that the semantic models are synced to the companion orgs. Then, you can deploy your Tableau Next assets to the companion orgs using a change set.

items.stem: A partner is packaging a data stream into a managed package with a data kit. Put these tasks into the order the workflow requires.
options: Create a data kit from Data 360
Select and add the data streams and data stream definitions in the data kit package
Define the deployment sequence for data kit components
Create a package in Package Manager with the data kit
Install the created package in a Salesforce org
answer: Create a data kit from Data 360
Select and add the data streams and data stream definitions in the data kit package
Define the deployment sequence for data kit components
Create a package in Package Manager with the data kit
Install the created package in a Salesforce org
items.rationale: The kit is created, filled and sequenced inside Data 360, and only then does Package Manager come into it. The step people forget is defining the deployment sequence, which is what makes components install in a workable order in the target org.
items.evidence_quote: Create a data kit from Data 360. Select and add the data streams and data stream definitions in the data kit package. Define the deployment sequence for data kit components. Upload the data kit package in Data 360. Publish the data kit in Package Manager. Create a package in Package Manager with the data kit. Install the created package in a Salesforce org.

items.stem: A batch data transform is deployed in a data kit and arrives in the target org with its output DLO-to-DMO mappings missing. What was left out of the kit?
options: The output DLOs themselves, which have to be added to the kit explicitly
The target DMOs, which have to be added before the transform
The data space definition the mappings belong to
The deployment sequence, without which mappings are applied in the wrong order
answer: The output DLOs themselves, which have to be added to the kit explicitly
items.rationale: A mapping travels with the object it belongs to, so adding the transform alone leaves its output mappings behind. The same pattern catches people with calculated insights, whose dependencies also have to be added by hand or the deployment fails.
items.evidence_quote: To ensure the Output DLO-to-DMO mappings are carried over during deployment, the Output DLOs themselves must be explicitly added to the Data Kit configuration.

items.stem: In the Tableau Next Metadata API, how many instances of a single entity type can one deploy request include at most?

items.evidence_quote: A data share target sets up connectivity with an external system.

items.stem: A client asks what happens to their data when Data 360 objects are made available to an external analytics platform through a data share. Which statement describes the arrangement?
options: The external platform can use the Data 360 objects without the data being loaded into it, with near real-time access
The objects are exported to the external platform on a nightly batch schedule and refreshed in full each night
The objects are copied into the external platform once, then kept current afterwards by change data capture events
The external platform's tables are copied into Data 360 first, and the objects are then queried from there
answer: The external platform can use the Data 360 objects without the data being loaded into it, with near real-time access
items.rationale: Zero copy data sharing exposes Data 360 objects to the external system without loading the data there, and gives near real-time access. The batch-export and change-data-capture options describe copy-based integration, which is exactly what a data share avoids.
items.evidence_quote: Zero copy data sharing with data shares lets you share Data 360 objects without loading the data into an external system and gives you near real-time access to data.

items.stem: Data 360 objects have been made available to a Snowflake account through a data share. In what form does a Snowflake user find them?
options: As views in the Snowflake account
As datasets in the Snowflake account
As data catalog views registered in AWS Lake Formation
As tables registered in Unity Catalog
answer: As views in the Snowflake account
items.rationale: Snowflake surfaces shared Data 360 objects as views, which can then be joined to Snowflake tables. Datasets is the form used in Google BigQuery, data catalog views belong to the AWS Lake Formation route, and Unity Catalog is the Databricks path.
items.evidence_quote: You can access Data 360 objects as views in a Snowflake account.

items.stem: A client's analysts want to point Tableau Desktop straight at their Data 360 data. Which connector should they build on?

Customer Data Platform connector

items.evidence_quote: You can connect to these Tableau products from Data 360 using the Salesforce Data Cloud connector. Using the Salesforce Data Cloud connector requires Tableau Desktop version 2023.2 or later.

items.stem: A data share target is no longer wanted and the Delete option refuses to remove it. What has to be true before a data share target can be deleted?
options: It must not be linked to a data share
It must have no successful share in the last 30 days
Its objects must first be removed from the data share
It must be disabled before it can be deleted
answer: It must not be linked to a data share
items.rationale: Only unlinked targets can be deleted, so the order of work is to unpick the data share first and remove the target afterwards. Emptying the share of objects is not the same as unlinking the target from it.
items.evidence_quote: Before you delete the target, make sure that it’s not linked to a data share. You can’t delete a linked target.

items.stem: An analyst creates a Query Editor workspace and picks a data space, then cannot find an object they know exists in Data 360. What is happening?
options: Query Editor shows only the objects available in the selected data space
Query Editor shows only objects the analyst personally owns
The workspace has to be saved before objects are listed
Objects appear only once a query has referenced them at least once
answer: Query Editor shows only the objects available in the selected data space
items.rationale: The data space chosen when the workspace is created scopes everything the workspace can see, so an object in a different space is simply absent rather than hidden by permissions. The fix is another workspace in the right space.
items.evidence_quote: Query Editor displays only the objects available in the selected data space.

items.stem: The data governance policies enforced inside Data 360 keep applying automatically to objects that an external system reads through a data share.
items.rationale: Data shares do not honor Data 360 governance policies, so equivalent controls have to be applied at the data share target. Otherwise privileged users in the receiving organization can view and query all records of the shared objects.
items.evidence_quote: Data shares don't honor the data governance policies enforced by Data 360.

items.stem: Which Data 360 object types can be put into a data share so that an external system can read and query them?
options: Data lake objects (DLOs)
Data model objects (DMOs)
Calculated insight objects (CIOs)
Data streams
Segments
Activation targets
items.rationale: A data share carries DLOs, DMOs and CIOs, which is what lets the receiving system build analytics and machine learning on harmonized data. Data streams, segments and activation targets are ingestion and audience constructs, not shareable objects.
items.evidence_quote: Data Shares provide easy access for external systems to use data in Data 360. With access to data lake objects (DLOs), data model objects (DMOs), and calculated insight objects (CIOs), you can build powerful analytical insights and machine learning models.

Salesforce Edge Network

items.evidence_quote: Query workspaces aren't synchronized with companion organizations. Create query workspaces specific to the org you use.

items.stem: In the receiving AWS account, four tasks are carried out on the Lake Formation console so that a Data 360 data share can be queried from Amazon Redshift. Put them in the required sequence.
options: Accept the data share
Create the resource link to the target region
Mount the Salesforce Data 360 objects as data catalog views
Grant permissions to query the live and unified data
answer: Create the resource link to the target region
Mount the Salesforce Data 360 objects as data catalog views
Grant permissions to query the live and unified data
items.rationale: The receiving account accepts the share, links the resource into the target region, mounts the Data 360 objects as data catalog views, and only then grants query permissions. Granting before mounting leaves nothing for the permissions to apply to.
items.evidence_quote: In the customer AWS account, on the Lake Formation console, accept the data share, create the resource link to the target region, mount Salesforce Data 360 objects as data catalog views, and grant permissions to query the live and unified data in Amazon Redshift.

items.stem: One Data 360 org accepts a data share request from another Data 360 org. Where do the shared objects sit in the receiving org immediately afterwards?
options: In the default data space, from where they can be moved afterwards
In a new data space created automatically for the source org
In a data space matching the name they occupied in the source org
Outside any data space until an admin assigns one to them
answer: In the default data space, from where they can be moved afterwards
items.rationale: The target org stores an accepted data share in the default data space; relocating the objects is a separate exercise using Add Data to a Data Space. Nothing mirrors the source org's data space or creates one on acceptance.
items.evidence_quote: By default, the target org stores the data share in the default data space. To move the objects in the data share to your desired data space, see Add Data to a Data Space Using Data Lake Objects.

items.stem: A Snowflake data share target has been created and the OAuth sign-in completed. What becomes of the security integration object that was created in Snowflake for it?

It must stay in place, because it is reused on every data refresh
It must be recreated each time another data share is linked to the target
It must be replaced by a private network route before data can flow
answer: It is no longer needed, because the authentication runs only once
